Riparian soils are often spatially heterogeneous and poorly mapped due to their mosaic structure. In this study they were systematically described to capture variability in hydromorphic and biogeochemical properties across landscape positions. The dataset enables cross-climate comparison of riparian function and sensitivity to environmental change, providing a valuable foundation for modelling nutrient retention, release, and transformations at the land-water interface. The data are openly available via the Environmental Information Data Centre.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: China’s Roads Network and Material Stocks Database in 2021 (CRANMS)
abstract: China’s rapid urbanization has led to a substantial increase in material stocks, particularly in road construction with cement being a major component. Accurate knowledge of road material stocks and their distribution are essential for constructing material stocks and flows accounts, and promoting sustainable resource management. However, existing estimates mainly focus on the use of multiple materials in particular case study areas or the use of a limited number of materials in certain road types, failing to form a comprehensive understanding of different road construction materials across China. This study presents China’s Roads Network and Material Stocks Database (CRANMS), a high-precision road network database integrating road structure and material stocks data. With the help of multiple data sources and GIS techniques, CRANMS provides detailed spatial data on China's road network, including material use, length, and administrative classification, and location. The dataset was validated through comparisons with national statistical data and existing literature. The database covers approximately 97% of China’s total road length relative to official statistical records and provides road-segment-level estimates of construction input material quantities, enabling users to aggregate material stocks by road class, province, or material category. The dataset is intended for use in material stocks accounting, infrastructure-related material flow analysis, and spatial comparison of road material stocks.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A metadata-managed FAIR end-to-end workflow for microbial community omics data analysis
abstract: High-throughput omics technologies enable detailed molecular profiling of complex microbial communities, yet FAIRification of the resulting datasets is commonly treated as a secondary step performed after data analysis. This approach overlooks the practical benefits of integrating standardized metadata early in the research process: experimental conditions directly determine how raw data should be processed, so capturing interoperable metadata at the outset creates a machine-actionable basis for driving and documenting the entire analytical workflow. Here, we describe a modular, containerized workflow implemented in Common Workflow Language that follows the single-containment principle and records software provenance, tool versions, and parameter settings at each processing step. Using defined mock metagenomic community datasets as controlled benchmarks, we demonstrate how machine-readable experimental metadata can initiate and parameterize multi-step analyses covering read quality control, assembly, binning, quality assessment, and functional annotation. The resulting provenance chains link experimental context, workflow definitions, and derived data products to support traceability and downstream reuse.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Microscopy Image Dataset of pulmonary vessels for Quantitative assessment of fibrosis
abstract: Structural remodeling of the vascular wall is a universal response to chronic damage, pressure overload or flow overload. Therefore, this process occurs in a wide range of diseases affecting both the systemic and pulmonary circulations. Vascular wall fibrosis is one of the most important factors in the pathogenesis of various types of pulmonary hypertension. In this regard quantitative assessment of collagen deposition in the vascular wall is crucial for both preclinical studies and directly affects the life prognosis for patients with pulmonary hypertension. Also, histological analysis is the gold standard for assessing vascular structural remodeling. This dataset includes 705 micrographs of vascular wall region with varying degrees of vascular wall fibrosis that developed in various types of pulmonary hypertension. All included studies were devoted to the investigation of pulmonary arterial hypertension and chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension in male Wistar rats. Lung sections were stained with Picro-Mallory and digitized using a whole slide scanner. Pulmonary artery branches were subdivided into vessel segments, and exported as fixed-size micrographs. For each micrograph, the dataset provides a region-of-interest mask and two independent expert annotations, including binary masks of the vascular wall and intramural fibrosis zones. The presented database will be useful for the development of new software solutions for the analysis of histological micrographs.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Proteomic profiling of cortex and spinal cord in Tau-P301L transgenic cynomolgus macaques
abstract: Tau pathology is a defining feature of several neurodegenerative disorders, but reusable proteomic resources from non-human primate tauopathy models remain limited. Here we describe a four-dimensional label-free quantitative proteomic dataset from cortex and spinal cord tissues of wild-type and Tau-P301L transgenic cynomolgus macaques. The dataset comprises 16 neural tissue samples from four wild-type and four Tau-P301L animals, with paired cortical and spinal cord specimens collected from each monkey. Samples were analysed by LC-MS/MS on a Bruker timsTOF Pro platform, and label-free quantification was performed with MaxQuant against a Macaca fascicularis UniProt protein database. In total, 6,632 protein-group entries were identified, of which 6,520 protein groups were retained in the analysis-ready matrix for quality control and reuse. The accompanying records include raw mass spectrometry files, processed expression matrices, sample metadata and analysis scripts. This Data Descriptor provides a reusable non-human primate proteomic resource for tissue-resolved analysis and comparison of tau-associated molecular features.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A comprehensive six-year (2015–2020) dataset of six daily ground-level air pollutant concentrations across China
abstract: Air pollution poses significant risks to public health and the environment, highlighting the need for long-term, spatially comprehensive air quality datasets. Here, we present a large-scale ground-based air pollutant dataset comprising 4,453,372 daily records from 2,040 monitoring stations across mainland China during 2015-2020. The dataset includes concentrations of six major air pollutants: ozone (O 3 ), carbon monoxide (CO), nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ), sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ), and particulate matter (PM 2.5 and PM 10 ). To address missing observations in long-term monitoring records, we applied a LightGBM-based imputation framework that integrates model selection, feature enrichment, and iterative imputation to leverage spatiotemporal dependencies and inter-pollutant relationships. Each record is enriched with 128 features, including meteorological variables, remote sensing products, geographic attributes, anthropogenic indicators, and temporal descriptors.Comprehensive technical validation demonstrates that the reconstructed dataset preserves realistic temporal dynamics, spatial patterns, statistical distributions, and inter-pollutant correlation structures without introducing systematic biases. Benchmark experiments further illustrate the dataset’s usability for air pollution prediction tasks. This dataset is designed with machine-learning readiness, providing a comprehensive, high-quality, and standardized resource with spatiotemporally explicit data to advance air quality research, develop and benchmark machine learning models, conduct exposure assessment, and enable data-driven environmental management across China.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: COVID Data for Shared Learning (CDSL): a multimodal publicly accessible dataset of electronic health records and chest imaging from hospitalized COVID-19 patients
authors: Miguel Ángel Armengol de la Hoz
abstract: Comprehensive, high-resolution, and accurate datasets are critical for advancing COVID-19 research. However, most early pandemic datasets were limited to demographic data and sparse clinical information, often lacking diagnostic imaging tests. We present COVID Data for Shared Learning (CDSL), a multimodal publicly accessible database of patients hospitalized with COVID-19 in Spain. This dataset includes de-identified medical data from 4,479 hospitalization episodes, represented by distinct patient_id values, covering electronic health records with demographics, admissions, diagnoses, clinical and treatment information, and radiological images, specifically 4,608 X-ray images from 1,616 episodes and 1,440,156 computed tomography slices from 784 episodes. Comprehensive anonymization techniques were implemented by removing protected health information to ensure patient privacy, and extensive technical validation was conducted to confirm data completeness, internal consistency, and image conversion quality. Open-source code for data preprocessing, metadata extraction, and database deployment is publicly available to support reproducibility and community-driven improvement. Early in the pandemic, CDSL was shared to support timely COVID-19 research and became one of the earliest publicly accessible multimodal COVID-19 datasets available to the international research community. CDSL aims to promote global collaboration by sharing clinical data to advance healthcare research and drive innovation in personalized medicine and public health.

title: WISO-SAT: A global database of stable hydrogen isotopes in water vapor from eight satellite missions
abstract: Stable isotopes of hydrogen, including deuterium ( δ D), provide a critical tracer for understanding Earth’s hydrological cycle and climate dynamics. Recognizing this, the last two decades have seen a number of remote sensing missions geared towards measuring the ratio of HDO/H2O in water vapor. At present, however, observational gaps persist in remote regions and across satellite platforms. Furthermore, these data span different time periods, altitudes, and are inconsistently formatted, complicating intercomparison. To address this, we describe WISO-SAT, a harmonized multi-instrument database of monthly δ D and moisture concentration retrievals from eight satellite missions (SCIAMACHY, GOSAT, GOSAT-2, TROPOMI, TES, AIRS, CrIS, IASI) distributed as instrument-specific gridded NetCDF products at 1° × 1° and 5° × 5° horizontal resolutions. Key innovations and standardization of these 8 data products are made through bias correction across platforms and by providing uncertainty quantification. The dataset spans 2002–2024, enabling studies of decadal climate variability and changes in the seasonal cycle. These standardized and publicly available water vapor isotope products address a critical gap in isotopic observations from satellites across different timelines, supports climate model evaluation and development (e.g., isotope-enabled GCMs), and process-level studies of atmospheric phenomena such as moisture transport, rain formation and evaporation, and atmospheric rivers. An open-access repository includes NetCDF files and preprocessing codes used to format each dataset. We also provide example notebooks and scripts demonstrating model-satellite averaging kernel application and regression-based bias correction for surface δ D comparison. WISO-SAT enables novel applications in atmospheric science and hydrology, and provides an open data product that can be used to validate the simulation of Earth’s water cycle in GCMs.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: An improved chromosome-scale genome assembly of whiteleg shrimp, Litopenaeus vannamei
abstract: The whiteleg shrimp ( Litopenaeus vannamei ) is one of the most economically significant species in global aquaculture. We present a high-quality, chromosome-level genome assembly for L. vannamei , generated by integrating PacBio HiFi, Nanopore ultra-long, and Hi-C sequencing data. The final assembly spans 1.95 Gb (contig N50: 1.97 Mb), with approximately 97.25% of sequences anchored to 44 pseudochromosomes. Repetitive sequences constitute approximately 1.195 Gb, representing 71.95% of the genome. We annotated a total of 26,830 protein-coding genes, 23,952 of which were functionally characterized. The assembly exhibits exceptional completeness, achieving BUSCO scores of 70.98% (genome mode) and 69.80% (protein mode). This reference genome will serve as a fundamental resource for future genetic research on key economic traits and molecular breeding applications in L. vannamei .
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: AI-Refined Ensemble Precipitation and Temperature Projections for Regional Impact Assessment over the Conterminous United States
abstract: Access to high-resolution long-term earth system projections is essential for advancing research in hydrology, agriculture, disaster management, and adaptation planning. This Data Descriptor presents an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-refined ensemble of Earth system model (ESM) projections for the conterminous United States at 1/24° (~4 km) spatial resolution. The dataset was generated by downscaling ten Coupled Models Intercomparison Project phase 6 (CMIP6) Earth system models (ESMs) under two emissions scenarios (SSP245 and SSP585) for an 80-year period (1980–2059). Two AI-driven methods, Super-Resolution Convolutional Neural Networks (SRCNN) and Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Networks (SRGAN), were applied to produce high-resolution daily precipitation and minimum/maximum temperature. This descriptor documents the input datasets, processing workflow, bias-correction steps, file structure, variables, spatial and temporal coverage, and technical validation of the released data. Validation analyses compare the generated products with Daymet observations and existing downscaled datasets to characterize spatial patterns, biases, temporal consistency, and differences among products. The dataset provides daily high-resolution historical and future earth system projections that can support regional, impact assessment, and related applications, and details the AI downscaling framework, training protocols, and evaluation strategies to ensure reproducibility and usability.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: 3′ mRNA-seq dataset of human chondrocytes treated with caspase-1 and -8 inhibitors under osteoarthritis-like conditions
abstract: About 655 million persons worldwide are affected by osteoarthritis (OA), associated with excruciating chronic pain and disability in the elderly. Inflammation and cell death are two key events in OA and also key canonical functions of caspases. Since caspases play an important role in modulating inflammation, pharmacological caspase inhibitors have been widely utilized to study diseases involving inflammation in animal models and clinical trials. Among these, key caspases, which are responsible for activation of the corresponding pathways, include caspase-8 for the receptor mediated apoptotic pathway and caspase-1 as the key inflammatory caspase being involved in OA pathogenesis. OA- and non-OA chondrocytes were treated with caspase-1 and -8 inhibitors and TNF-α. RNA was isolated after 3 days from three biological replicates (n = 3) of each group and processed for single-end RNA sequencing (1 × 114 bp). Data were pre-processed and analyzed with R programming language v4.2.2. Downstream analysis included identification of differentially expressed genes providing a comprehensive overview of unique and shared transcriptional changes in both OA and non-OA cohorts.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Applications of broadband echosounders in fisheries and plankton acoustics - a compilation of test datasets
abstract: Broadband echosounders are used by the plankton and fisheries acoustics community to assess distribution, abundance and behaviour of fish and larger zooplankton. Multiple calibrated echosounders can be combined to measure acoustic backscatter across a wide frequency range. This publication presents several example datasets that showcase the diverse applications of broadband echosounders from different platforms like ships, net-pens and towed bodies. These datasets include acoustic targets such as fish, both with and without swim bladders, larger zooplankton, and calibration spheres. Each dataset consists of files from the Kongsberg Discovery EK80 system and includes associated metadata and calibration information. The datasets offer details regarding the objectives of the experiments, provide ground truth information when available, and outline the platform and configuration of data collection and transducers. This collection serves as a resource for testing, developing, and demonstrating data processing methods for broadband acoustic data.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Unveiling hidden seismicity: An AI-derived catalog of 380k earthquakes for Sichuan Province, China
abstract: Long-term, high-resolution seismic monitoring is a prerequisite for characterizing seismic structures, delineating fault geometry, and mitigating earthquake risks. Located on the eastern margin of the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau, Sichuan Province is among the most seismically active regions in China, with particularly intense activity concentrated in the shale gas extraction zones of the southern Sichuan Basin. However, conventional manual earthquake catalogs are often incomplete with respect to microseismic events, limiting detailed seismological research. In this study, we constructed and released a high-resolution earthquake catalog for the Sichuan Province ranging from January 2019 to December 2020. Using continuous waveform data from 261 seismic stations, we adopted a deep learning-based workflow that involved phase picking, followed by event association and absolute location constrained by a high-resolution regional 3-D velocity model. The resulting catalog comprises 380,886 seismic events, approximately 5 times the number reported in the standard manual catalog for the same period. Completeness magnitude improved substantially, decreasing from M L 1.0 in the manual catalog to M L 0.1 in our catalog. This dataset provides a high-quality basis for subsequent studies in seismic activity analysis, seismic tomography, and hazard assessment.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Gap-free telomere-to-telomere genome assembly of greater amberjack (Seriola dumerili)
abstract: Greater amberjack ( Seriola dumerili ) is an important commercial fish species in both capture fisheries and aquaculture around the world. However, no high-quality telomere-to-telomere (T2T) reference genome was reported to date, which greatly limits the studies of evolutionary and functional genomics in greater amberjack. In this study, we reported the first gap-free T2T genome of greater amberjack combing DNBSEQ short reads, PacBio HiFi long reads, Hi-C, and ONT ultra-long reads data. The genome spans 693.45 Mb with contig N50 of 29.32 Mb. 98.62% of genome sequences were anchored on 24 chromosomes without gaps. 48 telomeres were identified on both ends of all chromosomes. BUSCO assessment, average reads mapping ratio, and quality value (QV) evaluation jointly indicate the high quality and completeness of the genome assembly. 25,371 protein-coding genes and 183.86 Mb repeating elements were identified. These results provide valuable resources for the evolutionary genomics research, genetics, and molecular genetic breeding in greater amberjack.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: An integrated dataset of clinopyroxene-melt and amphibole-melt cation partitioning in hydrous alkaline primitive to intermediate magmas
abstract: Trace element partitioning in clinopyroxene and amphibole governs the geochemical evolution of alkaline magmas, directly impacting liquid lines of descent reconstruction, volcanic hazard assessment and magmatic ore exploration in these volcanic settings. However, predictive models for these complex mineral phases remain limited by a lack of experimental data constraining the effects of intensive and extensive thermodynamic properties on cation substitutions in coexisting amphibole-clinopyroxene crystals. To expand this knowledge base, we present a dataset of clinopyroxene-melt and amphibole-melt partition coefficients. Piston cylinder experiments utilized natural alkali basalt and mugearite starting compositions, with starting H 2 O contents ranging between 3.7 and 7 wt.%, and T comprised between 1100 °C and 975 °C. The coexistence of both mineral phases in all the experiments allowed us to derive a set of clinopyroxene-melt and amphibole-melt partition coefficients especially important when interpreting amphibole-clinopyroxene parageneses in alkaline magmas. Furthermore, by employing the lattice strain formalism and an iterative numerical approach, it was possible to provide additional constraints to partitioning results, further validating the dataset. This validated dataset provides the empirical foundation for predictive partitioning models, necessary for modeling magma differentiation and dynamics in both active and quiescent alkaline plumbing systems.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Mount Etna Absolute Gravimetry Dataset: 19 Years of Measurements (2007–2025)
abstract: This Data Descriptor presents a curated dataset of absolute gravity measurements collected at Mount Etna between 2007 and 2025, providing a 19-year record of gravity changes across one of the most active volcanic systems worldwide. The dataset comprises repeated observations at 13 benchmarks spanning summit, upper flank, and peripheral sectors, enabling the investigation of gravity changes over multiple spatial and temporal scales. Combined with complementary relative gravity observations, the dataset provides a high-quality reference for volcano monitoring, time-series analyses, geophysical model calibration, inversion studies, and integration with deformation, seismic, and geochemical observations. This openly available dataset represents one of the longest continuous absolute gravity records acquired at an active volcano and provides a valuable resource for investigating subsurface mass redistribution associated with volcanic activity.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: SPEC-2B Dataset: a Visible-Near Infrared (VIS-NIR) Reflectance Spectra of Blueberry Fruits Across Cultivars and Maturity Stages
abstract: Reliable assessment of blueberry fruit maturity using optical proximal sensing requires standardized and well-documented spectral datasets covering multiple cultivars and ripening stages. To this end, we present the SPEC-2B Dataset, a curated collection of visible-near infrared (VIS-NIR) reflectance spectra acquired from blueberry (Vaccinium corymbosum L.) fruits representing three commercial cultivars (Duke, Legacy, and Blue Ribbon) and three visually assessed maturity categories. The dataset comprises 9588 reflectance spectra acquired using a compact spectrometer under consistent illumination geometry and acquisition protocols. Following preprocessing and quality control, a working spectral range from approximately 500 to 1000 nm was retained for analysis. All spectra were processed using a documented preprocessing workflow that includes dark signal correction, white reference normalization, integration-time normalization, wavelength trimming, and quality control procedures, including an empirical O2-A band index and an optional filtered subset to reduce localized spectral perturbations around 760 nm. Technical validation was conducted using descriptive statistics, empirical signal-to-noise ratio characterization, and principal component analysis (PCA) to examine internal consistency, spectral stability, and variance structure across cultivars and maturity categories. The dataset, associated metadata, raw spectral measurements, quality-control files, and visualization scripts are made publicly available to support reproducible research in agricultural spectroscopy, proximal sensing, and fruit quality assessment.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Multi-area single-cell calcium imaging dataset of the mouse cortex across wakefulness, sleep, and anesthesia
abstract: We present a reusable dataset of neuronal population activity from multiple cortical areas, recorded from layers 2/3 of the mouse cortex at single-cell resolution during wakefulness, natural sleep (including NREM and REM sleep), and isoflurane anesthesia. Using wide-field two-photon microscopy, we recorded approximately 4,000 to 10,000 neurons per session at 7.65 Hz and provided the spatial coordinates of individual neurons. The repository provides both processed datasets and the corresponding raw imaging movies (TIFF) and electrophysiological recordings (MATLAB format). Processed data are distributed in MATLAB format and include ΔF/F fluorescence signals, deconvolved spike estimates, Gaussian-smoothed spike estimates, behavioral state annotations, and metadata. This dataset supports reuse in studies of cortical population dynamics, brain-state-dependent activity, and spatially distributed neuronal organization. It should also be useful for method development, benchmarking, and comparative analyses of large-scale neuronal activity across physiological and pharmacological brain states.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Coarse grained molecular dynamics dataset of cyclic peptide interactions with lipid membranes
abstract: A large, standardized dataset of coarse grained molecular dynamics simulations is presented to characterize the interaction of cyclic peptides with an anionic lipid membrane under controlled conditions. The dataset comprises more than 10,000 trajectories generated using a chirality aware force field designed for cyclic peptide nanotubes and includes 3,855 peptide sequences simulated with identical protocols. Over 1,000 structural and energetic descriptors were extracted from each trajectory, quantifying peptide membrane contacts, interaction energies, and conformational variability. These descriptors provide mechanistically interpretable features that extend beyond sequence information and enable systematic comparison of membrane interaction behaviors across a chemically diverse peptide space. Example analyses demonstrate how the dataset supports unsupervised characterization of interaction profiles and the development of machine learning models that predict membrane behavior from coarse grained structure, illustrating its reuse potential for computational design and mechanistic studies of membrane active cyclic peptides.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Cesarean Scar Defect Segmentation in Transvaginal Ultrasound Images: a Dataset and Benchmark
abstract: Cesarean Scar Defect (CSD) is one of the most prevalent complications following cesarean delivery. Transvaginal ultrasonography is widely used for primary CSD screening. Accurate determination of CSD outline and dimensions is crucial for treatment. However, CSDs are frequently overlooked by sonographers due to small size and irregular morphology, suboptimal image quality, and limited clinical awareness in resource-constrained settings. Despite artificial intelligence advances in medical imaging, no public dataset exists for transvaginal ultrasound CSD segmentation. To address this gap, we present a comprehensive CSD dataset derived from 186 diagnosed patients, comprising 1,111 images and 16 videos, ultimately yielding 501 positive samples of confirmed CSD with precise pixel-level manual annotations. Annotations are performed following standardized clinical guidelines through collaboration between experienced sonographers and trained PhD students. This work provides high-quality benchmark resources for advancing medical image segmentation algorithms and promoting clinical innovation. Ultimately, improved CSD diagnosis and subsequent treatment strategies can enhance the quality of life in women of reproductive age, representing significant value for both medical research and clinical practice.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: ToxiFruit: A Multi-class Image Dataset for Formalin Adulteration Detection in Fruits
abstract: The unauthorized use of formalin preservatives to delay ripening and extend shelf life of fruits remains a critical food safety concern, particularly in regions with limited routine monitoring. To support computer vision and machine learning research on adulteration detection, we present ToxiFruit , a curated multi-class image dataset focused on formaldehyde adulteration in fruits. The dataset contains 7,200 original images evenly distributed across eight classes, covering four commonly consumed fruits in Bangladesh (apple, malta, mango, and banana) captured in two conditions: fresh and formalin-treated. Images were collected under natural lighting across four geographically distinct locations in Bangladesh, introducing real-world variation in illumination, background, and fruit appearance. To support model development and benchmarking, four augmented derivatives were generated from each original image, producing 28,800 augmented images and 36,000 image files when combined with the 7,200 original images. All images were standardized to 224 × 224 pixels. HCHO-related sensor responses were measured for both fresh-control and formalin-treated samples using the same sensor module, while label consistency was further assessed through independent expert inspection. ToxiFruit provides a practical benchmark resource for developing, evaluating, and deploying automated fruit adulteration detection and food safety monitoring systems.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Global dataset of heat wave types based on multi-level atmospheric temperature anomalies
abstract: Heat waves’ processes in the tropospheric column and their vertical structure have attracted growing attention recently, but data-demanding continental or global analyses remain rare. Here we present HW3D, a global dataset designed to classify heat waves according to their vertical temperature structure. HW3D encompasses heat wave types based on temperature anomalies at 13 tropospheric levels from the ERA5 reanalysis in 1979–2024 over both land and marine environments in the 5° × 5° grid. Heat waves are classified into near-surface, lower-tropospheric, higher-tropospheric, and omnipresent types. Their characteristics such as start date, length, and extremity are presented, along with temperature anomalies at individual levels for studying vertical cross-sections. While the share of the four individual heat-wave types is relatively balanced over mid-latitudes, near-surface heat waves clearly predominate in the tropics. We also illustrate possibilities of the dataset on record-breaking heat waves in each subdomain, which were most frequent in the recent 2015–2024 decade for all four heat wave types and over both land and marine regions.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Technologically-useful Heuslers from a Genetic Algorithm Search
abstract: A genetic algorithm based global crystal structure optimisation was performed using the MatterSim-v1.0.0-5M machine-learned potential to find minimum enthalpy structures for technologically useful systems obeying the Heusler stoichiometry, X 2 YZ. We define technologically useful as not contain toxic, radioactive, or highly expensive elements. The presented dataset contains the results of this search for optimal structures for 9614 stoichiometric combinations.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A telomere-to-telomere chromosome-scale genome assembly of longfin batfish (Platax teira)
abstract: Longfin batfish ( Platax teira ) is a tropical marine fish species belonging to the family Ephippidae in the order Perciformes and suborder Percoidei. It is widely distributed in the Indo-Pacific region, including the South Sea and around Taiwan in China. The longfin batfish has a distinctive black-and-white coloration with a unique ornamental value. It also features fast growth and tender, delicious flesh. In this study, we successfully constructed the first telomere-to-telomere (T2T) chromosome-scale genome for the longfin batfish by integrating PacBio HiFi, Nanopore ONT ultra-long reads, and Hi-C sequencing technologies. The final assembled genome size was 694.3 Mb, with a scaffold N50 of 30.0 Mb. It was anchored onto 24 chromosomes, presenting a complete set of 48 telomeres. We predicted 192.0 Mb of repetitive sequences and annotated 25,662 protein-coding genes. The genome and protein BUSCO scores reached 98.8% and 98.4%, respectively, indicating high genome completeness. This high-quality T2T genome data provides an essential foundation for further research on the functional genomics, genetic diversity, and selective breeding of the longfin batfish.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Multimodal RGB-D Dataset of Visuo-Gestural Facial Expressions in Peruvian Sign Language
abstract: Peruvian Sign Language (LSP) is used by approximately 8,790 deaf individuals in Peru, yet computational resources for automatic sign language recognition remain critically limited. Visuo-Gestural Facial Expressions (VGFEs) convey essential grammatical and semantic information in sign languages, but existing datasets focus predominantly on manual gestures, neglecting these non-manual components that are fundamental for linguistic interpretation. We present SIGNO-PERU-FER, a multimodal dataset of dynamic VGFEs in Peruvian Sign Language. The dataset comprises 1256 synchronized RGB-D video sequences from 16 native LSP signers performing 14 Visuo-Gestural Facial Expressions categories selected for their visual similarity and classification challenges. Each sequence includes RGB video (1920 × 1080, 30 fps), depth maps (512 × 512), and 468 3D facial landmark points. Each recorded sequence was captured using an Azure Kinect DK device in controlled laboratory conditions with uniform lighting. Baseline recognition benchmarks are provided to support reuse and to characterize the technical difficulty of minimal pairs of VGFEs in LSP. The dataset supports research on sign language technologies, multimodal facial behavior modeling, and inclusive AI systems.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A multi-project, multi-domain, and feature-engineered Itemlet dataset for empirical software engineering
abstract: The ability to benchmark new approaches and replicate already published research in empirical software engineering has suffered from limited advancement over time because there was no large-scale, multi-domain dataset containing both raw workflow data and derived features in one place. To address this, we created the Itemlet dataset, which is compliant with agile-based software engineering tasks. It is comprised of 727,282 data points from 204 projects with publicly accessible Jira issue trackers across 19 different domains. There are 108 features per sample, which consist of 60 raw structural fields retrieved from the JIRA REST API and 48 derived features. The raw structural fields and the derived features were designed to support three types of research tasks: (1) sprint planning and effort proxy analysis; (2) requirements prioritization; and (3) complexity classification. The effort-related fields are proxies reflecting how agile teams record effort; the dataset does not contain independently validated deliverable size measures (such as function points) required for formal effort estimation in the classical sense. We also demonstrated that the dataset complies with FAIR principles on fifteen criteria; except for one, all criteria are completely satisfied. The dataset can be accessed under CC-BY 4.0 license terms and has been archived at Zenodo with a DOI number: https://zenodo.org/records/19411554 .
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Neuromorphic Vision-Based Dataset for Soil Characterization and Slip Estimation in Space Rover Applications
abstract: Reliable rover mobility on planetary surfaces remains challenging due to complex wheel–soil interactions that can lead to excessive slip, sinkage, loss of traction, and ultimately rover immobilization. Existing approaches for soil characterization and slip estimation rely on a variety of sensing modalities, yet publicly available datasets combining neuromorphic vision with synchronized rover mobility measurements and ground-truth slip information remain limited. In this article, we present a neuromorphic vision-based dataset which offers microsecond latency, high temporal resolution, and low power consumption for soil characterization and slip estimation in planetary rover applications. The 48 GB dataset comprises 270 experiments collected across three terrain classes, five velocity settings, two illumination conditions, and multiple controlled slip scenarios. Each experiment contains synchronized event streams acquired from a neuromorphic camera together with wheel encoder measurements, rover pose estimates obtained from a motion-capture system, terrain labels, and slip measurements. The dataset is a resource for developing neuromorphic vision-based rover perception algorithms for soil characterization, slip estimation, and enhanced rover mobility.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A multi-omics dataset of the developing zebrafish intestine: longitudinal transcriptomic and microbiome profiles in wild-type and IgZ knockout models
abstract: The gut microbiota and host immune system engage in corresponding interactions that are essential for mucosal immune homeostasis. In mammals, immunoglobulin A (IgA) is a key regulator of intestinal immunity and microbial composition. Although teleost fish have IgZ (IgT), a functional equivalent of IgA, its developmental function in regulating gut immunity and microbiota homeostasis is still unknown. To investigate these, we generated a zebrafish IgZ knockout ( igz −/− ) model to study the long-term effects of IgZ deficiency on intestinal immune regulation during development. We integrated intestinal microbiome and transcriptome analyses of wild-type and igz −/− zebrafish at 1, 2, and 3 months of age, together with assessments of IgZ secretion, intestinal pathology, and inflammatory responses. Gut microbial communities were profiled by 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and intestinal transcriptomes were analyzed by high-throughput RNA sequencing. Overall, our dataset provides better insights into the interplay between gut immunity and microbiota in zebrafish following IgZ deficiency across different developmental stages.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: An Annotated Aerial Dataset for Training and Benchmarking Computer Vision Models in Turkey Behavior Analysis
abstract: We present a dataset of annotated aerial images of turkey behaviors acquired using an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) in an experimental poultry facility. Video recordings were collected from 160 Nicholas Select turkey toms between 5 and 32 days of age and converted into image frames. The dataset comprises 2, 388 images with bounding box annotations for eight behavioral categories: feeding , drinking , sitting , standing , perching , huddling , wing flapping , and dead . Each image contains multiple individuals captured from an oblique aerial perspective, reflecting realistic flock conditions. The images are provided with object detection annotations encoded in YOLO format for each behavioral category. This dataset supports the development, training, and benchmarking of computer vision models for automated poultry behavior analysis. It provides a resource for research in Precision Livestock Farming (PLF), particularly for non-invasive monitoring of animal behavior using aerial imagery.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Sixteen isotropic 3D fluorescence live-imaging datasets of gastrulation in the red flour beetle Tribolium castaneum (Coleoptera: Tenebrionidae)
abstract: Gastrulation is a pivotal phase of early embryogenesis during which initially uniform cells undergo coordinated movements and fate specification to establish the basic body plan. Although previous studies have advanced our understanding of gastrulation in the red flour beetle Tribolium castaneum , quantitative morphogenetic data remain limited. Here, we present the second Systematic Live Imaging Collection of Embryogenesis (SLICE-2), consisting of sixteen isotropic 3D fluorescence live imaging datasets that document gastrulation and early germband elongation in Tribolium . Imaging was performed using light sheet fluorescence microscopy in conjunction with a homozygous transgenic line that expresses mEmerald-labeled nanobodies against histone H2A/H2B. Embryos were recorded along four directions, and the resulting axial image stacks were subjected to multiview fusion to obtain isotropic 3D images of entire embryos with reduced shadowing artifacts. The collection includes weighted-average fusion and fusion-deconvolution derivatives, and nuclei segmentation data are available for selected developmental stages. SLICE-2 expands the microscopy data resources for Tribolium , enabling comprehensive analyses of gastrulation dynamics while also providing benchmark data for image processing, segmentation, and modeling approaches.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Large-scale, Stratified, Fully Annotated Acoustic Forest Soundscape Dataset of Avian Vocalizations from Eastern North America
abstract: Global environmental change is altering biodiversity through shifts in phenology, population dynamics, and animal behavior, creating a need for rapid, scalable approaches to monitoring biological communities. Passive Acoustic Monitoring (PAM) offers a powerful and scalable approach for assessing biodiversity and detecting changes in animal communities. Recent advances in deep learning methods have accelerated automated analysis of PAM data, yet progress is constrained by the limited availability of large, high-quality, strongly annotated datasets for training and evaluation. Here, we present a curated collection of three large-scale, multi-species datasets of avian vocalizations recorded using PAM across four forested landscapes in the northeastern United States. The collection comprises 217 hours of audio with expert-generated labelled annotations for ~183,000 vocalizations across 88 bird species. We provide open access to raw audio recordings, annotation files, and detailed metadata describing recording locations and sampling context. These datasets are designed to support the development, benchmarking, and validation of automated species detection and classification algorithms, while also enabling ecological analyses of species occurrence, activity patterns, and acoustic behavior. This strongly labelled acoustic data is intended to facilitate reproducible, cross-disciplinary research at the intersection of bioacoustics, ecology, and deep learning.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: The Vienna 4G/5G Drive-Test Dataset
abstract: Machine learning for mobile network analysis, planning, and optimization is often limited by the lack of large, comprehensive real-world datasets. This paper introduces the Vienna 4G/5G Drive-Test Dataset, a city-scale open dataset of georeferenced Long Term Evolution (LTE) and 5G New Radio (NR) measurements collected across Vienna, Austria. The dataset combines passive wideband scanner observations with active handset logs, providing complementary network-side and user-side views of deployed radio access networks. The measurements cover diverse urban and suburban settings and are aligned with time and location information to support consistent evaluation. For a representative subset of base stations (BSs), we provide inferred deployment descriptors, including estimated BS locations, sector azimuths, and antenna heights. The release further includes high-resolution building and terrain models, enabling geometry-conditioned learning and calibration of deterministic approaches such as ray tracing. To facilitate practical reuse, the data are organized into scanner, handset, estimated cell information, and city-model components, and the accompanying documentation describes the available fields and intended joins between them. The dataset enables reproducible benchmarking across environment-aware learning, propagation modeling, coverage analysis, and ray-tracing calibration workflows.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of Helichrysum odoratissimum, a medicinal plant from Southern Africa
abstract: Helichrysum odoratissimum , a plant species native to Southern Africa, holds deep cultural significance and is widely used in traditional medicine. It is valued for its antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties and is cultivated and traded in South Africa due to its growing commercial relevance to the pharmaceutical and cosmetic industries. Despite its ecological and economic importance, genomic resources for this species remain limited. Here, we report a high-quality chromosome-level genome assembly for H. odoratissimum to facilitate investigations into its genetic basis of bioactivity, environmental adaptation, and taxonomic relationships. High-molecular-weight DNA extracted from leaf tissue was sequenced using Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) long-read sequencing, and Hi-C proximity ligation data were generated to enable chromosome-scale scaffolding. The final assembly spans 2.45 Gb, with a scaffold N50 of 354 Mb, and was anchored and oriented into seven chromosome-scale pseudomolecules, with 2,760 smaller scaffolds remaining unplaced. Assembly quality and completeness were evaluated using QUAST, BUSCO and Merqury, and chromosomal structure was validated using Hi-C contact maps. Genome annotation identified 67,980 genes, including 52,270 protein-coding genes, with functional assignments generated using eggNOG-mapper. This genome provides a foundational resource for functional genomics, conservation planning, molecular breeding, and the discovery of bioactive compounds underpinning the medicinal and commercial value of H. odoratissimum .
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A preprocessed multimodal neuroimaging dataset from Quebec Parkinson Network for biomarker discovery
abstract: Open, multimodal, neuroimaging datasets are a key resource for the development of biomarkers and statistical models that can support disease monitoring and treatment planning in Parkinson’s disease (PD). Here we present the first release of Quebec Parkinson Network Neuroimaging Cohort (QPN-NC), a cross-sectional cohort of 202 individuals with PD and 69 older adults with multimodal MRI and extensive clinical and neuropsychological evaluations. The main objective of this data collection is to investigate neural correlates of motor and non-motor symptoms and facilitate comparisons with other PD studies. This QPN-NC release comprises well-characterized clinical assessments and curated imaging data processed through five neuroimaging pipelines. Additionally, we provide harmonized data annotations to facilitate search and cohort matching across other PD datasets. We share the tools and software used in this data release to enable data discovery, reproduce image processing, and help other studies to adopt best practices and community standards. Together with other datasets, QPN-NC will improve our understanding of PD and aid the translation of neuroimaging biomarkers into the clinic.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A continental-scale dataset of ground beetles with high-resolution images and validated morphological trait measurements
abstract: Despite the ecological significance of invertebrates, global trait databases remain heavily biased toward vertebrates and plants, limiting comprehensive ecological analyses of high-diversity groups like ground beetles. Ground beetles ( Coleoptera: Carabidae ) serve as critical bioindicators of ecosystem health, providing valuable insights into biodiversity shifts driven by environmental changes. While the National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON) maintains an extensive collection of carabid specimens from across the United States, these primarily exist as physical collections, restricting widespread research access and large-scale analysis. To address these gaps, we present a multimodal dataset digitizing over 13,200 NEON carabids from 30 sites spanning the continental US and Hawaii through high-resolution imaging, enabling broader access and computational analysis. The dataset includes human-made measurements of elytra length and width of each specimen image, establishing a foundation for automated trait extraction using AI. High correlations between measurements made by humans from images to those taken by humans on physical specimens ensure reliability for ecological and computational studies. By addressing invertebrate under-representation in trait databases, this work supports AI-driven tools for trait-based research, fostering advancements in biodiversity monitoring and conservation.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Multimodal Dataset of Student Oral Presentations with Sensors and Evaluation Data
abstract: Oral presentation skills are a critical component of higher education, yet comprehensive datasets capturing real-world student performance across multiple modalities remain scarce. To address this gap, we present SOPHIAS ( S tudent O ral P resentation monitoring for H olistic I nsights & A nalytics using S ensors), a 12-hour multimodal dataset containing recordings of 50 oral presentations delivered by 65 undergraduate and master's students at the Universidad Autónoma de Madrid, comprising 46 individual presentations with a mean presentation duration of 9 min 48 s ( SD = 33 s) followed by a mean Q&A duration of 6 min 28 s ( SD = 3 min 02 s), and 4 group presentations with a mean presentation duration of 14 min 11 s ( SD = 1 min 40 s) followed by a mean Q&A duration of 8 min 22 s ( SD = 1 min 21 s). SOPHIAS integrates eight timestamped sensor streams from high-definition webcams, ambient and webcam audio, eye-tracking glasses, smartwatch physiological sensors, and clicker, keyboard and mouse interactions. In addition, the dataset includes slides and rubric-based evaluations from teachers, peers, and self-assessments, along with timestamped contextual annotations. The dataset captures presentations conducted in real classroom settings, preserving authentic student behaviors, interactions, and physiological responses. SOPHIAS enables the exploration of relationships between multimodal behavioral and physiological signals and presentation performance, supports the study of peer-assessment and provides a benchmark for developing automated feedback and Multimodal Learning Analytics tools. The dataset is available for research, including both academic and legitimate commercial research and development, under controlled access through Science Data Bank, subject to approval of a Data Usage Agreement (DUA), with code provided through GitHub.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A High-Resolution, Spatially Consistent Multi-Source Fusion Dataset for Photovoltaic Infrastructure in China
abstract: The global energy transition has driven a rapid expansion of clean energy infrastructure, with photovoltaic (PV) systems playing a central role. As the world’s largest producer and installer of PV systems, China has witnessed sustained growth in installed capacity over recent years. Reliable, high-resolution spatial data on PV infrastructure are essential for informing energy policy, optimizing grid integration, assessing land use conflicts, and evaluating ecological impacts. While several publicly available PV datasets for China exist, they vary substantially in time periods, data sources, identification methodologies, and data precision, creating challenges for users who require consistent, high-quality inputs for their analyses. To systematically evaluate and integrate these heterogeneous datasets, this study develops a validation framework incorporating data fusion, DeepLab V3+ validation, and manual annotation. Applying this framework and based on accessible PV datasets, we construct China’s High-Resolution Photovoltaic Comparison and Fusion (PVCF) dataset, a high-resolution PV vector dataset for China updated to December 2025. The results reveal substantial inconsistencies among the nine source datasets, with low-agreement regions, defined as areas identified as PV by only a single dataset, constituting the largest proportion and covering a substantial area. Building upon 2,776.74 km 2 of high-agreement PV areas from the nine existing datasets, defined as regions identified by no less than five sources, the PVCF further incorporates 5,830.72 km 2 of manually annotated, refined, or newly identified PV patches, together with 1,682.69 km 2 of PV area validated using DeepLab V3+, yielding a total area of 10,290.15 km 2 . The northwestern provinces collectively account for 4,613.58 km 2 (44.83%) of the national total, predominantly in the form of large clustered utility-scale solar farms, while eastern China is dominated by fragmented and dispersed distributed and rooftop systems. As the most recent high-resolution PV vector dataset for China, PVCF provides a robust data foundation for applications in PV policy planning, biodiversity assessment, and ecological research.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Multi-tissue mRNA-seq, miRNA-seq and single-cell RNA-seq data from heat-stressed lactating Holstein cows
abstract: We present a multi-tissue, multi-omics transcriptome dataset from lactating Holstein cows under heat stress (HS) or pair-fed thermoneutral (PFTN) conditions. The dataset comprises: (i) bulk mRNA-seq from five tissues (rumen epithelium, liver, mammary gland, subcutaneous adipose tissue and skeletal muscle); (ii) small RNA-seq (miRNA-seq) from adipose tissue and skeletal muscle; and (iii) single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). Data were generated from three independent experiments using comparable controlled HS versus PFTN designs in environmentally controlled chambers; arteriovenous blood metabolite and hormone measurements are also provided. In total, the dataset includes bulk mRNA-seq from 37 tissue samples across five organs, miRNA-seq from 16 samples, scRNA-seq from six PBMC samples (82,013 cells), and blood biochemistry over a 14-day treatment period. Raw sequencing data and processed matrices newly generated in this study have been deposited in the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), while the previously published mammary gland and rumen epithelium data remain available under their original SRA accessions; arteriovenous blood biochemistry and additional phenotypic data are available from figshare. This resource enables investigation of tissue-specific and systemic molecular responses to heat stress in dairy cattle.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Making Mediterranean trophic interactions easier to study: the MAISHA dataset
abstract: Understanding trophic interactions is essential for ecology and for implementing and managing conservation policies. In the Mediterranean Sea, although dietary studies are increasing, marine trophic data remain fragmented. Here, we present the MAISHA (Mediterranean Archive of Integrated Stomach and feeding Habits Analyses) dataset, which results from a standardization process across 213 stomach content studies involving 287 species (248 of which are fish). Prey and predator data were standardized taxonomically using WoRMS, and diet contributions were normalized. Geographic and taxonomic biases are evident, with most studies concentrated in the Western Mediterranean Sea and a lack of data on bottom prey, such as invertebrates, and top predators (e.g., elasmobranchs). The collection revealed heterogeneity in reported diet measures and in prey taxonomic resolution. This study highlights critical gaps in marine trophic ecology and underscores the need for coordinated, standardized, and open data on trophic interactions in the Mediterranean Sea.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A dataset of drought-induced tree mortality in Canada’s boreal forests from 1970 to 2020
abstract: Drought can trigger widespread tree mortality events and is considered one of the most critical stressors affecting the health of forest ecosystems today. However, datasets documenting drought-induced tree mortality at broad spatial and long-term temporal scales remain scarce. Here, we present a long-term dataset of drought-induced tree mortality in Canada’s boreal forests. The dataset was generated using an ecological process-based model that incorporates the latest understanding of drought-induced mortality mechanisms, namely hydraulic failure and carbon starvation. This grid dataset has a spatial resolution of 5 km and spans the period from 1970 to 2020. The dataset has been independently validated, demonstrating the robustness of the estimated drought-induced tree mortality rates. A robust dataset on drought-induced tree mortality can not only support ecological researchers in understanding the impacts of drought on forest systems but also provide critical information for managing drought impacts across sectors and disciplines, thereby supporting the development of relevant policies and strategies. The dataset is freely accessible and available for download through an open online portal.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Synchronized Multimodal Characterization of Physiological, Environmental, and Behavioral Responses During Controlled Indoor Thermal Exposure
abstract: This Data Descriptor presents synchronized multimodal measurements for characterizing physiological, environmental, behavioral, and perceptual responses during controlled office thermal exposure. Data were collected from 26 participants across 50 experimental sessions conducted in a climate-controlled chamber under two stable thermal conditions, referred to as lower temperature (LT) and higher temperature (HT). Each session followed a standardized 15-phase office protocol comprising acclimation, resting baseline, cognitive tasks, motor transitions, structured discussion, and washout periods. The dataset integrates high-frequency peripheral physiology (electrodermal activity, photoplethysmography, inertial motion, and skin temperature), wearable electroencephalography (4 channels), centralized climate chamber monitoring, localized indoor air quality sensing, ultrasonic distance-based behavioral monitoring, and repeated phase-level subjective perception questionnaires. The released files preserve empirically observed sampling rates rather than imposing nominal device rates: median rates are 19.14 Hz for EDA, 29.29 Hz for PPG, 29.43 Hz for motion, 8.32 Hz for skin temperature, and a mean rate of 265.57 Hz for EEG. All modalities are temporally aligned using an authoritative session-level master timeline provided at session, phase, and minute resolution. The release includes minimally transformed session-aligned time-series exports, machine-readable quality-control artifacts, and comprehensive data dictionaries describing variable semantics, units, and preprocessing steps. The resource is designed to support reproducible multimodal synchronization research, signal-quality benchmarking, thermal comfort modeling, and cross-domain data fusion under controlled office thermal exposure conditions.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A multi-period dataset of retrogressive thaw slump susceptibility for Northern Hemisphere permafrost regions
abstract: Permafrost thaw accelerates the initiation and expansion of retrogressive thaw slumps (RTSs), with critical implications for the terrestrial carbon cycle and land-surface energy budgets. However, long-term datasets characterizing spatiotemporal variations in RTS susceptibility across Northern Hemisphere permafrost regions remain lacking. Here, we integrate 55,673 georeferenced RTS occurrence records with machine learning models to generate a 1-km spatiotemporal dataset of RTS susceptibility from 2000 to 2100 under multiple climate change scenarios. RTS susceptibility is defined as the relative occurrence probability of RTS under specified environmental conditions. We independently modelled RTS susceptibility for the Arctic and Tibetan Plateau and merged the individual outputs to construct a spatially harmonized dataset for the Northern Hemisphere. Model performance was evaluated using standard classification metrics, yielding mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.96 ± 0.005. The dataset includes georeferenced RTS inventories and gridded susceptibility maps for the entire Northern Hemisphere permafrost domain, covering the baseline period and diverse future climate scenarios. These products provide a foundational resource for quantifying permafrost hazard risks, infrastructure exposure, and carbon-climate feedbacks under climate warming.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Synchronized Vibration Data Collection for Fault Diagnosis of Induction Motors under Varying Rotating Speeds and Loading Conditions
abstract: This paper presents a vibration dataset for fault diagnosis of three-phase induction motors operating at variable speeds, controlled by a Siemens S7–1500 programmable logic controller (PLC) and an INVT GD20-1R5G-S2 variable-frequency drive (VFD). The dataset captures triaxial vibration signals from two ADXL355 accelerometers mounted at the bearing housing and motor frame, acquired at a sampling rate of 4 kHz using a Teensy 4.1 microcontroller. Data were collected across five operating speeds (varying from 10 to 50 Hz in steps of 10 Hz) and two mechanical load conditions (5 kg load and no-load), covering six fault scenarios: normal condition, mechanical looseness, horizontal shaft misalignment at 3 mm and 5 mm, and vertical shaft misalignment at 3 mm and 5 mm. The complete dataset comprises 60 CSV files totaling 1.72 GB, each containing six vibration channels and a numerical fault label. Technical validation was performed through time-domain and frequency-domain signal analysis, followed by machine learning classification using Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) classifiers, achieving accuracies of 99.79%, 96.73%, and 92.96%, respectively, across 12 fault classes. These results confirm the dataset’s suitability as a benchmark for rotating machinery fault diagnosis research, with potential applications in machine learning, deep learning, and cross-speed generalization fault detection methodologies.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Benchmark Dataset of Vibrational Signals for Artificial Intelligence Applications in Mechanical Systems
abstract: This study introduces a benchmark dataset of 7,000 vibration signals from a modular mechanical transmission system, simulating real-world setups with artificially induced faults in gears, V-belts, and roller chains. Data were collected under various configurations, capturing fault propagation across interconnected modules and including both healthy and faulty states. Time- and frequency-domain analyses reveal distinct vibrational patterns under fault conditions. To assess diagnostic complexity, classic unsupervised fault detection models, using statistical features and deep learning autoencoders, were applied. Low clustering accuracy and poor label alignment highlighted the difficulty of detecting subtle anomalies without supervision. The dataset’s variability and realism offer a robust resource for advancing signal processing using machine learning and deep learning in condition monitoring. This work provides a scalable, diverse, and diagnostically rich dataset, addressing gaps in existing resources that often focus on isolated components and lack fault diversity, and supports research in unsupervised learning, representation learning, and predictive maintenance within Industry 4.0.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A computer vision dataset for detecting roseau cane scale
abstract: Roseau cane scale ( Nipponaclerda biwakoensis ) is an invasive insect pest responsible for widespread die-offs of roseau cane ( Phragmites australis ) across coastal Louisiana and neighboring states. Monitoring scale densities currently depends on labor-intensive visual inspection, in which cane samples must be manually stripped and counted during each survey season. To support restoration and management efforts, we developed three curated and annotated image datasets of scale-infested roseau cane internodes — high resolution, downsampled, and tiled — to evaluate the performance of object detection models for automated scale detection. A total of 265 high-resolution RGB images were collected under controlled laboratory conditions and processed using a tiling pipeline that preserves small object detail, resulting in 1,346 labeled tiles. We validated the efficacy of these datasets in training scale detection models using a YOLOv8n model framework. The results of our validation show that tiling the larger images down to 512 × 512 pixels achieved the strongest performance, with 76.80% precision, 61.50% recall, 69.70% mAP50, and 40.50% mAP50–95, slightly outperforming the downsampled 2048 × 1536 pixel full-frame images. These results demonstrate that object detection models are feasible for the detection of roseau cane scale. Moreover, the datasets provide a foundation for scalable, automated monitoring of roseau cane scale populations and other related pests, supporting the future development of digital monitoring tools for ecological assessments and management efforts.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: LLM Board Game Tournaments: A Dataset of Moves, Validity, and Reasoning
abstract: We present A Dataset of LLM Strategic Play , comprising 9,572 tournament records from a controlled eight-round Swiss-system tournament involving 20 LLMs across four board games: Tic-Tac-Toe, Connect Four, and their goal-inverted variants, Suicide and Not Connect Four. Move records include the model identity, board state, legal moves, observed latency, and textual justification. Moves are validated with a GDL-based arbiter and a rectification protocol that allows up to 10 retries. Overall, 25.2% of LLM-generated moves are invalid, approximately 50% in Suicide; in total, 106 game sequences ended in automatic forfeit, represented by terminal records in the dataset. Even the best-performing model records an invalid-move rate of 10.7%, showing that rule-following errors remain present under these evaluation conditions. These observations illustrate the use of simple board games as controlled domains for evaluating LLM behavior, where strategic decision-making can be examined together with compliance with formal constraints. The proposed pipeline–GDL-based validation, Swiss tournament design, and rectification protocol–is domain-agnostic and can be extended to other GGP settings, supporting scalable evaluation of LLM decision-making under formal rules.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Aerodynamic Data for Validation: The CHN-T1 Large Aircraft Standard Model Dataset
abstract: With the increasing demand for high-fidelity aerodynamic validation benchmarks for advanced civil aircraft design, this paper presents an open-access, high-Reynolds-number transonic wind tunnel dataset for the CHN-T1 standard large aircraft model, generated from systematic tests conducted in the European Transonic Wind Tunnel (ETW). Tests were performed on the full CHN-T1 configuration with horizontal and vertical tailplanes, under two boundary layer transition settings: fixed artificial transition and free natural transition. The test envelope covers a Mach number range of 0.20–0.90, Reynolds numbers from 3.6 × 10 6 to 37.8 × 10 6 , achieved via pressurization combined with cryogenic cooling down to 115 K and ambient 300 K conditions, with a total of 33 valid aerodynamic polars acquired. The comprehensive dataset includes corrected aerodynamic coefficients, freestream flow conditions and model attitude data. It addresses the scarcity of high-Reynolds-number data and the common lack of lateral-directional and full-configuration measurements in existing public benchmarks. This dataset provides a reliable benchmark for CFD solver validation, wind tunnel flow quality assessment, and the development of data-driven aerodynamic model, supporting the advancement of modern civil aircraft design.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Steady-State Visual-Evoked EEG Dataset for Visual Function Assessment via Biomarker Extraction
abstract: Amblyopia and intermittent exotropia (IXT) are prevalent pediatric visual impairments characterized by deficits in cortical visual processing. Understanding the underlying neurophysiological mechanisms and tracking neural recovery requires high–quality, objective data, yet open–access EEG datasets specifically designed for these pediatric populations—particularly those with a longitudinal dimension—remain scarce. Here, we present the steady–state visual–evoked EEG (S2VEEG) dataset, a 64–channel electroencephalography (EEG) dataset collected from pediatric participants, including amblyopia, IXT, and healthy controls. The S2VEEG dataset uses a multimodal experimental paradigm comprising resting–state recordings, transient Visual Evoked Potentials (VEP), and Steady–State Visual Evoked Potentials (SSVEP). The dataset employs a longitudinal design, capturing neural activity both at baseline and following therapeutic interventions (perceptual learning for amblyopia and strabismus surgery for IXT). For technical validation, differential entropy (DE) and small–worldness properties are extracted as features and analyzed using Support Vector Machine (SVM), Residual Graph Convolutional Broad Network (RGCB), and Emotion Transformer (EmT) classifiers. The classification performance suggests that the recorded EEG signals contain discriminative electrophysiological information across visual function states, thereby supporting the usability of the S2VEEG dataset as candidate discriminative measures for methodological development and exploratory analyses. These results are intended as a technical validation of data quality and feature separability, while this resource provides a valuable platform for future studies investigating brain–eye interactions, treatment–induced neuroplasticity, and the development of objective biomarkers for monitoring visual function recovery.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Dataset for Glycemic Control Analysis in Type 1 Diabetes under Multiple Daily Injection Treatment in Free-living Conditions
abstract: Open-source datasets of glucose monitoring play a critical role in facilitating research in diabetes management and treatment, while allowing the development of Artificial Intelligence models for blood glucose forecasting. While many efforts are spent on patients with Type 1 Diabetes with Continuous Glucose Monitoring, many patients are still relying on Multiple Daily Injection treatment due to lower cost and easier accessibility. Due to individual differences in living styles and physiological responses to various insulin treatments, more structured datasets with detailed behavioral and physiological factors in real-life living conditions are expected. Contributing to the research on Type 1 Diabetes, this study introduces the OU-DATASET, a longitudinal, multimodal resource for analyzing glycemic control within multiple daily injection treatment. The dataset includes glucose level monitoring, insulin injection, activity tracker data (heart rate, steps) records, and self-reported lifestyle events (meals, exercise, stress) collected from 22 participants on multiple daily injection therapy over an 8-week period. This descriptor details the data collection protocol, data architecture, and accessibility of the dataset. The OU-DATASET supports further development of data-driven algorithms and models for the treatment management of Type 1 diabetes.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: GermND-3M: A multi-crop multi-variety multi-modal dataset for germplasm variety-quality-viability nondestructive detection
abstract: Rapidly nondestructive assessment of germplasm variety, quality, and viability (VQV) is required to ensure genetic integrity and support the secure conservation and utilization of crop germplasm. However, large-scale, standardized, and openly available scientific datasets encompassing multiple crops, varieties, and modalities are still lacking in the field of intelligent nondestructive VQV detection of germplasm resources. We constructed GermND-3M, a multi-crop, multi-variety, and multi-modal dataset for germplasm VQV nondestructive detection. The dataset comprises 3,214 varieties from four major crops, including 1,000 rice varieties, 595 wheat varieties, 1,000 maize varieties, and 619 soybean varieties. Each variety comprised 100 seeds. The dataset integrates hyperspectral imaging, volatile-gas sensing, and grain phenotypic imaging data from seeds, together with corresponding variety, quality, and viability labels. Standardized acquisition and processing protocols were applied to ensure data comparability. Dataset usability was evaluated using classical machine-learning and deep-learning models. GermND-3M provides a standardized resource for the development and benchmarking of nondestructive germplasm assessment methods and supports data-driven germplasm conservation and crop breeding.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Reporting and hosting a dataset of high-impedance faults in medium-voltage covered conductors
abstract: This work presents a multimodal dataset characterizing high-impedance faults (HIF) in medium-voltage covered conductors under controlled single-phase, phase-to-ground contact conditions. Insulation reduces wildfire risks but restricts fault currents below conventional detection thresholds. This restriction delays the onset of the fault signature. The dataset documents the temporal evolution of these events by integrating high-resolution electrical waveforms sampled at 20 kS/s with power-quality metrics from an IEC 61000-4-30 Class A analyzer. Complementary modalities include radiometric thermography and visual video with embedded audio for selected cases. The experimental design covers 22 groups and 142 segments, spanning conductor tip geometry, air gaps, surface materials, and moisture actions. Instrumentation uses independent acquisition platforms to minimize electromagnetic interference. Technical validation confirms a signal-to-noise ratio exceeding 5:1 at nominal voltage and metrological consistency between platforms. This repository provides a structured framework for validating physical models and developing detection algorithms addressing incipient dielectric failure in overhead distribution networks.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A global, historical, harmonized land-use dataset spanning 1900 to 2023 at 0.05° resolution reconstructed based on remote sensing and statistical data
abstract: Understanding long-term land-use and land-cover dynamics is fundamental for quantifying human impacts on Earth system and supporting global carbon-cycle and climate assessments. However, existing global land-use and land-cover datasets rarely reconcile high spatial resolution with long-term temporal coverage, limiting their applicability for century-scale Earth system analyses. To address this problem, we developed a top-down land-use reconstruction framework integrating fine-resolution remote-sensing land-cover information with Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) cropland and grazing-land statistics to produce a global, historical, harmonized land-use dataset for 0.05° resolution (approximately 5.6 km at the equator) (called HLUH-5km), a dataset providing spatially explicit fractions of six major land-use types for the period 1900–2023. HLUH-5km was assessed through a multi-level validation framework. It shows strong agreement with FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment (FRA) national forest area statistics, which were collected separately from the FAO Statistical Database (FAOSTAT) cropland and grazing-land data used as allocation inputs at the national level (slope = 1.01, R 2 = 0.96), indicating that the reconstructed forest trajectories are consistent with reported national forest inventories. The dataset also captures within-country spatial variability consistent with reported subnational land-use records across multiple regions. Grid-level comparison with satellite-derived land-cover products and regional historical reconstructions further demonstrate improved spatial consistency relative to existing global historical reconstructions. HLUH-5km provides a coherent basis for land-use analysis, terrestrial carbon accounting, and Earth system modeling.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Legacy Snow Load Dataset: Long-Term Measurements of Roof and Ground Snow Loads in Norway
abstract: Long-term empirical datasets are fundamental to the development, calibration, and verification of structural design models, yet the sustained efforts required to establish such datasets are often under-recognised.
