This Data Descriptor presents a curated and digitised dataset of roof and ground snow-load measurements collected by Professor Halvor Høibø (1924–2013) in Norway between 1966 and 1986. The dataset comprises full-scale measurements on agricultural buildings with gable roofs, including windward and leeward roof snow loads, ground snow loads, snow densities, roof geometry, exposure descriptors, and temporal information. These measurements have played a central role in the development of structural snow-load models and have informed international design standards, including ISO 4355 and EN 1991-1-3, as well as related North American standardisation work. The dataset has now been standardised, quality-controlled, and extended with geolocation and harmonised metadata, enabling integration with modern climate reanalysis products and facilitating climate-sensitive snow-load research. The dataset is provided in an open, reusable format to support reproducibility, comparative studies, and future assessments of non-stationarity in snow loads under a changing climate.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Global Dataset of Surface NO2 Estimation Based on Machine Learning Using Process-based Information
abstract: Nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) is a key air pollutant associated with numerous adverse human and environmental health outcomes, yet globally consistent, fine-resolution long-term surface NO 2 datasets remain scarce due to the shortcomings of available data sources and the complex relationships between emissions and surface NO 2 concentrations. Here, we improve estimates of global monthly surface NO 2 concentrations at fine spatial resolution (0.01° × 0.01°) over 2005–2023 by developing, optimizing, and applying a highly efficient gradient boosting decision tree (LightGBM) framework underpinned with multi-source datasets, including geophysical process-based a priori information that leverages simulations with the GEOS-Chem chemical transport model, road‐network metrics, land‐cover features, and other relevant environmental predictors over 2005–2023. Evaluated against 9,913 ground monitors across 66 countries, the machine learning model achieves significant agreement for the benchmark year 2023 with 10-fold spatial cross-validation for monthly surface NO 2 estimates ( \({R}^{2}\) = 0.82, RMSE = 2.34 ppb, slope = 0.97), and similar long-term performance over 2005–2023 ( \({R}^{2}\) = 0.76, RMSE = 3.42 ppb, slope = 0.97). We apply Buffered Leave Isolated Sites and Clusters Out (BLISCO) spatial cross-validation to rigorously account for spatial autocorrelation, finding that traditional spatial cross-validation overestimates performance over unmonitored areas and that process-based physical and chemical information from chemical transport model (GEOS-Chem) simulations significantly improves R 2 by 20% globally. Global per-pixel uncertainty quantification indicates that this dataset provides NO 2 estimates with median relative uncertainty of 35% and absolute uncertainty of 1.81 ppb. This 19-year fine-resolution global NO 2 dataset with a consistent methodology, process-based information, rigorous validation and uncertainty quantification offers a valuable resource for quantifying the magnitude, spatial patterns, long-term trends and impacts of global NO 2 exposure.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A daily 0.025° gridded column-averaged carbon dioxide dataset for terrestrial Europe from 2019 to 2023
abstract: High-resolution, continuous monitoring of atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) is essential for assessing regional carbon dynamics and tracking the effectiveness of climate mitigation policies such as the European Green Deal. Here, we present a daily, 0.025° × 0.025° column-averaged dry-air CO 2 mole fraction (XCO 2 ) dataset covering terrestrial Europe (12°W–40°E, 34°N–72°N) from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2023. The dataset is generated using a categorical boosting model that integrates Orbiting Carbon Observatory satellite retrievals, CarbonTracker 2025, and meteorological, land surface, and anthropogenic emission data. Independent validation against six European Total Carbon Column Observing Network stations yields a coefficient of determination of 0.95 and a root-mean-square error of 1.06 ppm. Comparison with the independent Greenhouse Gases Observing Satellite product shows accuracy comparable to mainstream products, with high-XCO 2 regions more clearly resolved. Feature-attribution diagnostics indicate that the learned relationships align with known atmospheric processes. This dataset is designed to advance regional carbon monitoring in Europe and support the evaluation of climate policies like the European Green Deal.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A single-cell RNA sequencing dataset of kidney and peripheral blood mononuclear cells from Dahl salt-sensitive rats under high and low salt diets
abstract: Hypertension is a major global health burden, with high dietary sodium intake being a key environmental risk factor. The Dahl salt-sensitive (SS) rat is a well-established model for studying salt-sensitive hypertension and renal damage. To facilitate research into the cellular mechanisms of salt-sensitivity, we generated a single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset from the kidney and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) of Dahl SS rats. Male rats were fed either a high-salt (4% NaCl) or low-salt (0.4% NaCl) diet for three weeks. We profiled high-quality cells from kidney tissue and from PBMCs. This dataset captures the cellular diversity of these tissues, including immune, epithelial, and endothelial cell populations, under different dietary conditions. This resource provides a foundation for investigating how high sodium intake influences cellular composition, gene expression, and cell-cell communication at single-cell resolution. As the Dahl SS rat remains one of the most widely used models for hypertension research, this dataset offers a valuable reference for exploring cell-type-specific responses to salt and generating hypotheses for future mechanistic studies.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Large-Scale Standardized Pediatric Normal Electrocardiogram Dataset
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) is a widely used non-invasive method for diagnosing cardiovascular diseases. ECG signal characteristics vary markedly across age groups, with pediatric recordings differing substantially from those of adults. Establishing a reliable baseline for defining a “normal” pediatric ECG across developmental stages is essential prior to designing algorithms for abnormality detection. Existing ECG databases are predominantly composed of adult data and lack comprehensive age stratification, while a few pediatric ECG databases are only from hospitalized children, resulting in a scarcity of large-scale, publicly available pediatric datasets that accurately reflect typical cardiac physiology of children. To address this gap, we present a large-scale, standardized pediatric normal ECG dataset comprising recordings from children aged 0-6 years. The dataset was compiled from a larger collection acquired at the Children’s Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, between 2019 and 2023. It includes 58,672 standardized 12-lead ECG recordings, each 10 seconds in duration and sampled at 500 Hz, all annotated as “NORM” by experienced pediatric cardiologists. This resource aimed to serve as a high-quality reference baseline for pediatric ECG research and algorithm development.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A database of second-order rate constants for reactions of eight environmentally relevant oxidants with pollutants
abstract: Second-order reaction rate constants are critical for quantifying oxidants’ reactivity and modeling contaminant transformation. However, such data are widely scattered across the published literature and public databases, and their reuse is severely limited by inconsistent chemical identifiers, non-uniform metadata, and heterogeneous reporting formats. Here, we constructed a curated database of second-order reaction rate constants for reactions between pollutants and eight environmentally relevant oxidant/radical including hydroxyl radical ( • OH), sulfate radical (SO 4 •− ), carbonate radical (CO 3 •− ), chlorine radical (Cl • ), dichlorine radical (Cl 2 •− ), ozone (O 3 ), hypochlorous acid/hypochlorite (HOCl/OCl − ), and singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ), containing 11,579 individual records. The dataset was systematically compiled from peer-reviewed publications, experimental kinetic studies, and public repositories including the NIST database. Chemical identifiers were standardized to CAS Registry Numbers and SMILES strings, metadata were unified across entries, and duplicate or inconsistent records were resolved using a rigorous multi-step quality control process. The final dataset is deposited in Figshare as machine-readable CSV files for direct download and reuse. This integrated resource will advance research in oxidation kinetics, comparative reactivity analysis, and data-driven applications in environmental chemistry and water treatment.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A high-quality chromosome-level genome assembly of a swimming sea cucumber Hansenothuria sp. from a deep seamount in the Western Pacific Ocean
abstract: Sea cucumbers are an important echinoderm lineage for studying the evolution trajectory and environmental adaptability. However, the limited availability of high-quality chromosomes for sea cucumbers from deep sea ecosystems has hindered a thorough understanding of mechanisms underlying their adaptive evolution. In this study, we reported the first chromosome-level genome assembly in the order Persiculida, Hansenothuria sp. M1226 from a deep seamount in the Western Pacific Ocean, which was sequenced on the PacBio Sequel II platform using the CLR (continuous long reads) mode. The Hansenothuria sp. M1226 genome assembly has a total length of 3.52 Gb with a scaffold N50 length of 133.1 Mb, encompassing 23 chromosomes, highlighting high genome continuity. Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologs (BUSCO) assessment yielded a completeness estimate of 85.0% for the genome assembly and 90.6% for its gene set. We predicted a total of 32,054 protein-coding genes (PCGs), with 27,273 functionally annotated. The availability of this high-quality chromosome-level genome of Hansenothuria sp. M1226 contributes to our understanding of the origin and evolution of sea cucumbers.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Reference Dataset of 66 High-Quality Plastid Genomes across Three Algal Phyla
abstract: Algae represent a diverse group of photosynthetic organisms, and their plastid genomes provide valuable molecular resources for investigating plastid evolution, photosynthetic adaptation, and phylogenetic relationships. However, algal plastomes exhibit remarkable evolutionary diversity, with substantial variation in genome structure and organization across different lineages. Currently, high-quality algal plastid genomes and a standardized and reliable workflow for generating high-quality algal plastid genomes is still lacking. To address these challenges, we successfully assembled 66 high-quality, complete algal plastid genomes, including 7 green, 19 brown, and 40 red algal genomes. During this process, we developed and established a standardized workflow for plastid genome assembly and quality assessment. Notably, these newly assembled genomes enrich existing NCBI resources by contributing 29 species, 13 genera, four families, and one order for the first time, offering both expanded taxonomic coverage and a standardized foundation for subsequent comparative and evolutionary analyses.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Full-ocean-depth EM124 mapping of the Challenger Deep by R/V Hakuho-maru and depth-estimate sensitivity tests
abstract: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is the deepest known point on Earth, yet recent depth estimates still differ by several meters because of environmental and instrumental uncertainties. Here we present a new full-ocean-depth multibeam bathymetric dataset collected with a Kongsberg EM124 echosounder aboard R/V Hakuho-maru during the KH-23-9 cruise in 2023. The survey comprises east–west and north–south lines acquired at vessel speeds of 4–15 kt. Five seawater sound velocity models were constructed from contemporaneous XCTD data, historical full-depth CTD data, and a recent full-depth reference profile to test the sensitivity of depth estimates. After ping-by-ping editing and gridding, the preferred KH23XCTD+KH92CTD solution resolves three basins deeper than 10,900 m, with maximum depths of 10,926, 10,912, and 10,927 m in the western, central, and eastern basins, respectively. Alternative sound velocity models yield maximum depths from 10,914 to 10,932 m, illustrating the meter- to >10-m-scale sensitivity of full-ocean-depth multibeam estimates to the applied sound velocity structure. Cleaned point soundings, gridded bathymetric surfaces for each sound velocity model, and the gridding script are provided. The dataset enables assessment of how sound velocity structure, survey speed, and beam-footprint geometry influence depth estimates in full-ocean-depth multibeam mapping, and provides a new reference for cross-comparison of Challenger Deep bathymetry.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Mass balance of the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets from the 1970s to 2023
abstract: The Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets are major drivers of global mean sea level rise and are predicted to continue to do so in the future. However, they also represent the largest source of uncertainty in projections of future sea level rise making robust estimates of observed ice sheet mass changes critical. Here, we compare and combine 42 independent estimates of ice sheet mass balance derived from satellite observations of temporal changes in ice sheet flow, volume, and gravitational attraction to determine the ice sheet mass balance from 1972 (Greenland) and 1979 (Antarctica) until 2023. We then use regional climate models to partition the total mass balance into contributions associated with surface mass balance and ice dynamical imbalance. The ice sheets lost 11,309 ± 565 billion tonnes of ice between 1979 and 2023, with glacier dynamical imbalance driving 84% of the ice loss and surface mass balance the remainder. This dataset can be used to track the contribution of the ice sheets to sea level rise and constrain projections of future sea level rise.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Single-cell transcriptomes of mouse prostate cancer models and human blood after irreversible electroporation
abstract: Irreversible electroporation (IRE) is a focal ablation approach for localized prostate cancer. We generated a data resource comprising single-cell RNA-sequencing profiles from subcutaneous and orthotopic RM-1 mouse tumors collected 7 days after IRE or sham intervention and paired peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) samples from five patients collected before and 7 days after IRE. All three components were prepared from whole-cell suspensions. This Data Descriptor documents cohort design, sample processing, sequencing, computational quality control, integration diagnostics and cell-annotation evidence for 20 sequencing libraries (six subcutaneous tumors, four orthotopic tumors and ten PBMC samples). Per-sample quality-control summaries, software and parameter records, sample composition tables and canonical-marker panels support independent assessment and reuse of the datasets.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A national fish pond dataset for Nigeria generated using automated detection and segmentation
abstract: Fish and other aquatic foods are a vital source of nutrients and livelihoods around the world, and with the stagnation of capture fisheries, countries have increasingly turned to aquaculture. While the geographic expansion of aquaculture is evident from national statistics, much less is known about subnational patterns of growth. Notably, the spatial extent of smallholder aquaculture ponds is poorly understood, limiting our ability to ask basic questions about local risks and benefits stemming from aquaculture investments. To begin to address this, we develop a national dataset of open-air fish pond boundaries for Nigeria using an open-source automated segmentation pipeline to systematically delineate individual fish ponds. As Africa’s most populous nation and third-largest fish producer, Nigeria plays a crucial role in regional food security. With its diversity of geographies and fish production systems, Nigeria offers the ideal case for developing automated approaches to fine-scale fish pond mapping. First, we use georeferenced point labels of fish pond locations to manually delineate fish pond boundaries and create a labeled dataset (N = 14,021). Combining these labels with high-resolution satellite imagery, we then train a national segmentation model and perform predictions across the entire country (precision: 86.3%; recall: 87.9%). We then train a post-processing random forest classifier to distinguish fish ponds from false positives (overall F1: 96.9%, with a per-state F1 mean of 63.5 ± 36.8%). Applying this approach, we identify a total of 246,786 fish ponds throughout Nigeria. Our scalable approach offers a flexible means for fine-scale tracking of smallholder aquaculture patterns, potentially applicable across other smallholder-dominated geographies. Such data are central for food system monitoring and informing interventions to bolster smallholder productivity and market access.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Cantonese speech corpus with picture-based and topic-based discourse tasks across the adult lifespan
abstract: This report introduces CanSpeak , a multi-task, multi-age speech corpus centered on Cantonese, with supplementary Mandarin samples from multilingual speakers. The corpus includes standardized topic-based and picture-based discourse tasks completed by younger and older adults, enabling analyses of speech production and discourse across the lifespan. CanSpeak provides orthographic transcriptions, fine-grained native-speaker annotations of disfluencies and errors, time-aligned annotations, and a range of discourse-level measures indexing fluency, lexical diversity, syntactic complexity, and speech organization. Participant demographic information and cognitive assessment scores are provided, including global cognitive status, processing speed, working memory, and depression scales. Annotation reliability was supported through intra-coder reliability assessment. The dataset was further validated by examining cross-age sensitivity in discourse measures, and cognitive–linguistic associations via relationships between speech features and global cognitive status as measured by the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). By combining cross-generational coverage, task diversity, fine-grained annotation, and cognitive profiling, CanSpeak constitutes a valuable research resource for psycholinguistics, neurolinguistics, aging research, and natural language processing, with particular significance for the study of Cantonese speech production and discourse.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Cyber-Attack Detection Dataset for Distribution Systems Generated from a Scaled Cyber-Physical Testbed
abstract: Modern power distribution systems, characterized by deep integration with communication networks, are increasingly susceptible to cyber threats. A critical challenge for attack detection research lies in the scarcity of authentic datasets derived from physical hardware testbeds. To address this critical need, an open dataset, termed CPDS-AD, is established for cyber-attack detection in cyber-physical distribution systems. This dataset is generated utilizing a developed laboratory-level scaled testbed, which emulates the steady-state operating and cyber-measurement processes of a 13-node three-phase unbalanced medium-voltage-type radial distribution feeder and a three-layer cyber architecture. It captures both normal-operation data and data recorded under various realistic cyber-attacks, including multiple types of false data injection and denial-of-service attacks. Raw communication messages are meticulously recorded and processed into synchronized, time-aligned measurement data. The quality and effectiveness of the dataset for developing data-driven attack detection methods are demonstrated through technical validation, employing dimensionality reduction and unsupervised machine learning models.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: High-resolution European soil property maps based on LUCAS and AlphaEarth Foundations satellite embeddings
abstract: High-resolution soil property maps have a wide range of applications, e.g. policymaking and precision agriculture. Previously published maps covering the EU-27 plus the UK range in resolution from 250 to 30 metres depending on the soil property. In this work, we produced 10 m resolution maps for soil texture (clay, silt, sand), coarse fragments, pH and bulk density. They are the products of a machine-learning workflow trained on LUCAS soil datasets and using AlphaEarth Foundations satellite embeddings as predictors. We performed hyperparameter tuning and training on Random Forests (RF) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). The best-performing models were ANN, with R 2 values ranging from 0.21 for coarse to 0.69 for pH. The best-performing ANN hyperparameters for each soil property were used to produce soil property maps over Europe as well as uncertainty estimate maps obtained from Monte Carlo dropout. The generated maps aim to close the resolution gap for the EU-27 + UK and provide a promising baseline for precision agriculture, soil health assessment at field scale and spatial planning.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Harmonised climate and Aedes albopictus arboviral vector mosquito surveillance datasets for the European continent
abstract: We present two harmonised datasets linking Aedes albopictus mosquito surveillance observations with standardised climate variables, designed to support benchmarking and reproducible modelling of mosquito distribution and abundance across Europe. The first dataset pairs polygon-level presence/absence records from the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) with ERA5-Land and CORDEX climate grids, yielding 157,918 and 79,398 spatially explicit grid points respectively, of which 34,482 and 20,832 carry confirmed presence labels. The second dataset combines 15,374 trap-level observations from 1,648 trap locations across western and southern Europe (AIMSurv v2.3) with ERA5-Land daily and monthly climate variables aligned to sampling periods. Both datasets are generated through transparent, documented preprocessing pipelines with explicit quality-control criteria, relying exclusively on open data sources. Rather than introducing new primary surveillance observations, this secondary data resource provides a reproducible transformation of public surveillance and climate sources into common, analysis-ready benchmark datasets. Together, they provide a consistent foundation for methodological benchmarking and reuse across ecological and epidemiological applications. Both datasets are publicly available via the JRC Data Catalogue.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Long-read metagenomic and metatranscriptomic datasets from marine plankton
abstract: Short-read sequencing (SRS) technologies, when applied to the study of environmental communities, present significant limitations that long-read sequencing (LRS) technologies are increasingly overcoming. However, the application of LRS for the integrated study of eukaryotic metagenome and metatranscriptome remains underexplored. Here, we present long-read metagenomic and metatranscriptomic sequencing datasets from four marine plankton samples collected during the Tara Pacific expedition. The metatranscriptome was characterized using high-depth poly(A)-selected cDNA-based Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) PromethION sequencing, and the metagenome using PacBio Revio (HiFi) sequencing. These long-read datasets represent among the first publicly available resources to combine accurate metagenomic datasets with deeply sequenced metatranscriptomes from marine eukaryotic plankton, providing a valuable resource to study their transcript diversity and functional gene expression.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Fused Geospatial Dataset Linking Climate Hazards and Road Infrastructure for Victoria, Australia
abstract: This Data Descriptor presents a fused geospatial dataset linking road infrastructure attributes with climate hazard indices for Victoria, Australia. The dataset integrates publicly available road network records from DataVic (traffic volume, pavement condition, and road configuration) with gridded climate hazard indices obtained from the Australian Climate Service (ACS) Hazard Insights Explorer. These hazard indices are derived from dynamically downscaled Climate Modelling Intercomparison Project 6 (CMIP6) projections processed by the Bureau of Meteorology Atmospheric Regional Projections for Australia (BARPA) and CSIRO Cubic Conformal Atmospheric Model (CCAM) regional climate models and provided for multiple global warming levels. All input datasets were harmonised to a common spatial reference and schema to support reproducible climate risk and infrastructure resilience analyses. Quality control procedures included schema validation, topological checks, and sample-based verification. The dataset is openly published on Zenodo under a CC-BY 4.0 licence, with accompanying metadata and reproducible processing scripts to facilitate transparent reuse.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Dataset for Visual Detection of Litchi Fruit Borer Infestation and Anthracnose
abstract: The litchi industry has long been severely plagued by the litchi fruit borer ( Conopomorpha sinensis ) and litchi anthracnose ( Colletotrichum gloeosporioides ). Despite the rapid development of deep learning in agricultural monitoring, there is currently no public dataset that supports the simultaneous detection of these two stresses, let alone a systematic simulation of variable lighting conditions in real postharvest environments. To address this issue, we constructed LitchiPestDisease—the first multi-illumination image dataset dedicated to the detection of litchi fruit borer infestation and litchi anthracnose. This dataset contains images collected from the core production areas in Maoming, Guangdong, China, during 2024 and 2025. To support the simulation of realistic grading scenarios, the dataset includes the original images and three systematically enhanced illumination variants (front lighting, back lighting, and side lighting) generated following the protocol described in this paper. All these images are provided in the public repository. The pest subset includes 3,061 original images, all annotated with bounding boxes for borer damage holes. The disease subset consists of 3,644 original images, a portion of which are additionally annotated with polygon instance segmentation, where each lesion is labeled by its severity (mild, moderate, severe). The corresponding enhanced images under three lighting conditions are fully provided in the public repository. Benchmark experiments based on YOLOv12n validated the effectiveness of the dataset: severe anthracnose detection reached near-perfect mAP50 levels, while pest detection achieved an mAP50 of 0.6539 under mixed lighting conditions. Comparative analyses across different lighting conditions and disease severity levels revealed the robustness and limitations of the model (e.g., the recall rate for mild disease under side lighting dropped to 0.878). Furthermore, benchmark experiments on instance segmentation revealed the performance variation of segmentation models under different lighting conditions, jointly providing a multi-task evaluation benchmark for algorithm optimization. LitchiPestDisease provides an important benchmark resource for the intelligent detection of fruit quality in real-world scenarios.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A gridded standardized precipitation evapotranspiration index dataset for China spanning the past millennium
abstract: The lack of reliable, spatiotemporally-completed and millennium-long drought dataset for China has limited a full-field and accurate understanding of drought variability over the past millennium. Here, we present a millennium-long gridded dataset of summer (June-August) Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) for China at 1.875° spatial resolution and annual temporal resolution. This dataset was generated using the paleoclimate data assimilation (PDA) approach by assimilating an expanded proxy network comprising 186 tree rings, 69 historical documents, three stalagmites and two ice cores from China and adjacent regions - addressing the limitations of previous gridded drought reconstructions that lacked proxies in eastern China and had sparsely-distributed proxies in northwestern China. Validation indicated that this dataset exhibits substantially-improved reliability compared to model-only calculations and previous PDA-based reconstruction. As a significantly-improved, millennium-long gridded SPEI dataset for China, this product provides essential support for elucidating the spatiotemporal evolution of drought variability over the past millennium, contextualizing current droughts within that period and evaluating climate model performance in simulating long-term drought events.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Global Warming and Frequency Amplification of Extreme Sea Levels
abstract: Extreme sea level (ESL), a major driver of coastal flooding, is widely used as a benchmark for coastal engineering design, coastal zone management, and risk assessment. With global warming, ESL events are projected to become more frequent and intense along most of the world’s coastline. Previous work has estimated the minimum global warming level (GWL) and timing at which the present-day 100-year ESL becomes an annual event along the global ice-free coastline. Comparable information for other return periods—such as 10-, 20-, 50-, 100-, and 200-year events—relevant to broader applications remains unavailable. Here, we present global datasets describing the minimum GWL and timing at which multiple present-day ESL return levels transition to annual occurrence. The datasets are derived using a multimethod framework, combining multiple global datasets of present-day ESL and projections of relative sea level change, while accounting for uncertainties. The resulting datasets provide a consistent global reference for assessing how the frequency of ESLs changes across return periods and GWLs, supporting applications in large-scale coastal impact assessment, planning, and risk analysis.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Daily intercity human mobility estimates across Chinese cities from 2020 to 2025
abstract: Intercity human mobility data are essential for regional resource management, ecological footprint assessment, and public-health research. However, existing datasets are often constrained by a trade-off between public accessibility and fine spatiotemporal resolution. To address this gap, we developed the Multi-scale Anchor-Calibrated Mobility (MAC-Mobility) framework, which integrates relative mobility indicators with official national aggregate mobility statistics published by the Ministry of Transport of China (MoT) to estimate daily intercity mobility networks. Through multiscale calibration, benchmarking, and model selection, MAC-Mobility combines 110 directly observed daily national totals, nine monthly aggregate constraints, and spatial allocation constraints derived from the Baidu Migration Index (BMI). The resulting dataset, Daily Intercity Mobility Networks for Chinese Prefecture-Level Cities (DIMNet-CPC), provides directed daily intercity mobility networks with estimated trip volumes from 2020 to 2025, covering 366 administrative units in China. The CatBoost model selected by MAC-Mobility achieved a weighted absolute percentage error (WAPE) of 4.74% and an R 2 of 0.899 in held-out validation at the national aggregate scale. Independent validation of the resulting dataset at the provincial aggregate, prefectural aggregate, and origin–destination (OD) pair scales yielded WAPEs of 14.37%, 25.45%, and 26.52%, respectively, with R 2 values exceeding 0.8 at all three scales. This open-access resource fills an important gap in intercity mobility data and provides an empirical foundation for multidisciplinary research on urban-system resilience, carbon dynamics, public health, and socio-ecological sustainability.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: The Corpus of English–Tagalog Code-switching: an integrative corpus of linguistic contact effects
abstract: The Corpus of English–Tagalog Code-switching (CEnTaCS) is a new corpus designed to document naturalistic English–Tagalog bilingual speech. Locally referred to as Taglish, it is a widely-used yet understudied contact variety in the Philippines. Recorded in 2025 in Metro Manila, the corpus comprises three interrelated datasets: individual story retelling recordings, cognitive control data based on the Arrow Flanker task, and sociolinguistic questionnaire data. CEnTaCS offers fine-grained data on code-switching across clausal, lexical, and morphemic levels, with particular attention to intra-word code-switching, a salient but still insufficiently documented feature of Taglish. Beyond code-switching, the corpus captures a broad range of language contact phenomena, including borrowing, calquing, convergence, and interference. By making these data systematically available, the corpus supports an integrated account of mixed-language practices that brings together structural, cognitive, and sociolinguistic perspectives. CEnTaCS thus enables researchers to investigate how contact-induced structures are constrained linguistically, how they relate to bilingual processing, and how they index social meaning and identity in a community where bilingualism is deeply embedded in everyday life.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Comprehensive Multimodal Gait Dataset for Lower-Limb Wearable Robotics in Indoor and Outdoor Environments
abstract: Daily walking locomotion exhibits variability, asymmetry and ground constraints. Recording and analyzing real-world locomotion data is essential for expanding the application scenarios of wearable robots such as exoskeletons and prostheses. However, most existing gait datasets are collected with specialized equipment under predefined laboratory conditions, lacking visual information from natural walking environments and annotations for transitional states across different surfaces. To address this problem, we collected walking data from 17 healthy participants across diverse indoor and outdoor environments, including kinematic data from seven inertial measurement units (IMUs), foot pressure data from force sensing resistors (FSRs) with 96 points, and visual data from three front-facing cameras with 1280 × 720 resolution. All modalities are time-synchronized, with 448 clips and 243607 data frames in total. Full annotations are provided, covering 16 classes of lower-limb locomotion states (8 steady states, 8 transitional states), bilateral gait phases and bilateral coordinates of the center of pressure (COP). This dataset can be utilized for exploring the applications of machine learning in locomotion state recognition and intelligent control of lower-limb wearable robotics.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Labelled Dataset of Healthy and Diseased Maize from Tanzania
abstract: Early detection of crop diseases is essential for improving maize productivity and strengthening food security, particularly in regions where agriculture is the main source of livelihood. This paper presents a labelled image dataset of healthy and diseased maize leaves collected in Tanzania to support the development of machine learning models for crop disease diagnosis. The dataset includes data on: healthy leaves, and diseased leaves of Maize Lethal Necrosis (MLN) and Maize Streak Virus (MSV) which are among the most significant threats to maize production in the country. All images are annotated to support tasks such as image classification, object detection and image segmentation. The dataset comprises a total of 243,539 labelled images covering multi-season, making it one of the largest publicly available maize image datasets from Tanzania. It serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners advancing artificial intelligence applications in agriculture.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Long-term high-frequency hydro-salinity dataset across an intermittent Mediterranean river-estuary continuum
abstract: Estuaries, acting as interfaces between the land and the sea, provide vital ecosystem services, considered as biodiversity hotspots. Within a Mediterranean climate, they undergo strong hydroclimatic variability, receiving variable riverine inputs from no freshwater to flash floods and being intermittently connected to the sea. We present a ready-to-use dataset, including quality-controlled surface and groundwater measurements along the Fiume Santu, a small Mediterranean temporarily closed estuary. Salinity, temperature and water level were measured hourly for three to seven years, from 2014 to 2022, using multi-parameter probes. Multi-annual recordings highlight the intermittency of connection between aquatic compartments and the buffering role of the estuary, recording recurrent extreme events such as floods, estuarine mouth closures or hypersalinity. The long-term high-frequency hydrological recording of the associated surface and groundwater measurements of a temporarily closed estuary, being scarce, offers a new medium for a broad panel of scientists and environmental managers to expand and further develop in terms of environmental conditions considered in coastal and estuarine studies.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A pediatric ultra-widefield fundus image dataset for artery-vein segmentation
abstract: Retinal artery-vein segmentation has emerged as an important task in medical image analysis, given the close associations between retinal vascular parameters and a wide range of systemic biomarkers and health outcomes. Although several public datasets have been established, important gaps remain due to the lack of pediatric data and the scarcity of ultra-widefield (UWF) fundus imaging, a novel modality capable of capturing richer features across a broader field of view. In this study, we present a Pediatric Ultra-Widefield Fundus image dataset for Artery-Vein segmentation (PUWF-AV), comprising 60 UWF fundus images annotated for artery-vein segmentation by professional ophthalmologists. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first UWF fundus image dataset for artery-vein segmentation in a pediatric population. Technical validation demonstrates the reliability of the dataset, highlighting its potential to advance the development of artery-vein segmentation methods for UWF fundus images in children.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A spatially and temporally aligned contrast-non-contrast cardiac CT dataset of pigs
abstract: Traditionally, cardiac CT imaging relies on the use of contrast agents. However, in some cases such agents cannot be used, and there is a need to develop novel AI-based algorithms to accurately segment cardiac structures from CT images, recorded without the use of contrast agents. To address this challenging problem, we have collected a spatially and temporally aligned cardiac CT dataset of pigs with and without the use of contrast fluid. This dataset consists of 10 different pigs, CT-scanned multiple times between 15 and 130 kg to cover a wide set of body weights. A subset of the dataset is manually labelled, to enable development of supervised learning-based segmentation techniques.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Semantically Annotated Ex Vivo Orthopedic Hyperspectral Imaging Dataset for Surgical Tissue Segmentation
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is an emerging medical imaging modality that provides dense spatial and spectral information for tissue characterization. Despite its growing interest in surgical research, the lack of publicly available, semantically annotated hyperspectral datasets has limited the development and validation of data-driven methods for surgical tissue segmentation. Here, we present HIST-Seg, a semantically annotated hyperspectral imaging dataset designed for surgical tissue segmentation in an orthopedic context. The dataset comprises 220 hyperspectral acquisitions obtained from ten ex vivo bovine specimens using a snapshot hyperspectral camera system. Each datacube has a spatial resolution of 608 × 968 pixels and covers the visible and near-infrared spectral range from 402 to 998 nm. Pixel-level annotations are provided for five orthopedic-relevant tissue classes (bone, cartilage, ligament, fat, and flesh), as well as for surgical instruments and operative-field background. A comprehensive technical validation, including spectral consistency analyses and baseline segmentation experiments, confirms the reliability of the hyperspectral data and annotations. HIST-Seg provides a high-quality reference dataset for the development and benchmarking of machine-learning methods for surgical tissue segmentation. In addition, the dataset may serve as an independent resource for the external evaluation of models developed on other hyperspectral datasets. The source code is publicly available on GitHub.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Grid2Text Dataset Aligning Meteorological Grid Data with Expert Reasoning Chains
abstract: Accurate meteorological forecasting is fundamental to public safety and economic stability, but it heavily relies on numerical weather prediction (NWP) models, whose complex outputs are often inaccessible to non-experts. Although large language models (LLMs) show potential in translating structured data into natural language to automate forecast reporting, progress has been constrained by a critical scarcity of datasets that bridge the modality gap and capture the implicit reasoning of human experts. To address this, we present Grid2Text , a rigorously developed dataset aligning ERA5 meteorological grid features with expert-verified textual forecasts, encompassing explicit reasoning chains for temperature trends, wind vector transitions, humidity ranges, and precipitation types. Furthermore, we establish validation benchmarks derived from a human-in-the-loop workflow to ensure the physical consistency and logical accuracy of the data. We anticipate that this open-access dataset will catalyze the development of interpretable LLM approaches for weather forecast discussions, ultimately advancing the field of scientific text generation.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A U.S. inventor–patent linkage dataset for National Inventors Hall of Fame inductees
abstract: Elite inventors are important subjects for studying technological change, inventor careers, and innovation networks. However, honorary institutions usually list only representative inventions or seed patents, and general-purpose patent databases do not directly provide audited inventor-level portfolios for externally defined recognition-based inventor groups. Here, we present a U.S. inventor–patent linkage dataset for inductees of the National Inventors Hall of Fame (NIHF). Starting from official NIHF records and U.S. induction-related seed patents, we construct an NIHF–PatentsView public baseline and combine it with broad retrieval of U.S. patent candidates from InCoPat, record-level evidence variables, PatentSBERTa-based semantic clustering, and manual adjudication. The final curated release contains 28,330 inventor–patent links representing 27,155 unique U.S. patent identifiers and covers 638 NIHF inductees. Compared with a public baseline based only on NIHF seed patents and PatentsView inventor identifiers, the dataset retains most baseline links while substantially expanding inventor and patent coverage. The dataset supports studies of NIHF inventors’ U.S. patent portfolios, patenting careers, technology trajectories, collaboration networks, and innovation activities, and can be linked to external patent metadata through standardized patent identifiers.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Dataset of Temporally Consistent Instance Annotations for 4D Plant Phenotyping
abstract: Spatio-temporal 4D plant phenotyping requires high-quality datasets with precise and temporally consistent annotations. However, such datasets are currently limited due to the substantial effort required for data acquisition and manual annotation. To address this limitation, we present Sugar4D, a publicly available 4D plant phenotyping dataset of sugar beet acquired using a terrestrial LiDAR scanner. The dataset comprises 768 point clouds from 48 individual plants representing twelve genotypes, recorded semiweekly across 16 consecutive time points during the growing season. All point clouds are provided with temporally consistent, pointwise instance annotations at the organ level, enabling the tracking of individual leaves over time. Sugar4D includes 6778 annotated leaves corresponding to 675 unique leaf instances. In addition to the annotated point cloud data, we provide 58 plant- and five leaf-related morphological parameters for each plant and leaf at each time point, validated using a 3D-printed plant reference model and invasive manual reference measurements. Sugar4D supports the development and evaluation of methods for plant instance segmentation, temporal registration, organ tracking, and spatio-temporal morphological analysis.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: UCOD: A Near-Field Benthic Organism Dataset for Underwater Visual Camouflage and Multi-Task Analysis
abstract: Accurate near-field underwater visual perception plays a crucial role in marine ecological monitoring and benthic resource exploration. However, the superimposition of the biomimetic characteristics of benthic organisms and the optical degradation caused by the water medium frequently induces significant underwater visual camouflage phenomena. This causes the target foreground and the background to become highly fused in terms of color, texture, and structure, thereby severely limiting the performance of underwater vision algorithms in core tasks such as object detection, image segmentation, and 3D reconstruction. Existing public datasets predominantly focus on salient targets in clear water or under simple backgrounds, lacking comprehensive multi-task benchmarks explicitly tailored for visual camouflage scenarios. To address this gap, we constructed an Underwater Camouflaged Object Dataset (UCOD) for near-field benthic organisms, designed for multi-task analysis to jointly support image enhancement, object detection, pixel-level segmentation, and 3D scene reconstruction. The dataset comprises 7,000 high-resolution RGB images, including 3,500 images with detection annotations, 3,500 images with segmentation masks, and 16 reconstruction sequence folders for 3D reconstruction. It covers six categories of benthic organisms exhibiting typical camouflage characteristics: scallops, fish, conches, abalones, starfish, and sea cucumbers. During data acquisition, calibrated underwater imaging equipment was employed, and the kinematic parameters of the acquisition platform were controlled to improve the stability and spatial consistency of the collected data. The dataset provides useful training data and an evaluation basis for underwater multi-task perception research under visual camouflage conditions, while offering complementary data support for studies on underwater optical sensing and intelligent exploration.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Refined annotations of intrahepatic portal and hepatic veins from thin-slice CT images
abstract: Accurate segmentation of intrahepatic vessels in contrast-enhanced CT is limited by spatial resolution, variable contrast timing, and the complexity of peripheral vascular anatomy. Public datasets such as the Medical Segmentation Decathlon Task 08 include annotations of hepatic structures but provide incomplete delineation of small-caliber portal and hepatic veins. This work describes HVA-CT (Hepatic Venous Annotations CT), a dataset derived from the contrast-enhanced thin-slice CT volumes of the Medical Segmentation Decathlon Task 08, in which intrahepatic venous structures were re-annotated with more complete anatomical delineation. The dataset comprises refined three-dimensional segmentations of portal and hepatic venous systems generated through a structured workflow combining baseline model outputs, AI-assisted vessel branch identification, and expert review. For each case, updated venous segmentation masks, liver segmentations, and a standardized tool for intrahepatic vessel extraction are provided. The dataset is intended to support the development and evaluation of automated methods for hepatic vessel segmentation and analysis.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: SARD: A Large-Scale Synthetic Arabic OCR Dataset for Book-Style Text Recognition
abstract: Arabic Optical Character Recognition (OCR) plays a critical role in converting extensive Arabic print media into digital formats. The development of modern OCR models, particularly advanced vision-language models, is hindered by the lack of large, diverse, and well-structured datasets that accurately replicate real-world book layouts. Most existing Arabic OCR datasets focus on isolated words or lines and are limited in scale, typographic diversity, or structural complexity representative of books. To address this limitation, this paper introduces SARD (Large-Scale Synthetic Arabic OCR Dataset). SARD is a synthetically generated dataset specifically designed to simulate book-style documents, comprising 2,621,075 document images and 794.6 million words rendered in six fonts: Sakkal Majalla, Arial, Calibri, Scheherazade New, Amiri, and Traditional Arabic. Unlike datasets derived from scanned documents, SARD is free from real-world noise and distortions, providing a clean and controlled environment for model training. Its synthetic nature enables exceptional scalability and precise control over layout and content variation. This study describes the dataset’s composition, generation process, and technical validation, and presents benchmark results for several traditional and deep-learning OCR models to highlight the challenges and opportunities associated with the dataset. SARD serves as a valuable resource for developing and evaluating robust OCR and vision-language models that can process diverse Arabic book-style texts.

title: A High-Resolution UAV Color and CHM Dataset for Bamboo Forest Segmentation and Mapping
abstract: Accurate mapping of bamboo forests is essential for effective management, sustainable utilization, and enabling reproducible research in forest remote sensing and ecological monitoring. To support this, we present a high-resolution unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) dataset for bamboo mapping in unmanaged forest environments. The dataset consists of co-registered RGB orthomosaics and a canopy height model (CHM) derived from UAV LiDAR point cloud data, providing centimeter-level spatial resolution. A total of 76 images were manually annotated to support supervised learning tasks. To facilitate reuse, we also provide baseline methods for training bamboo segmentation models using either a single data source or fused multimodal data. The dataset offers a reliable and scalable resource for forest science and remote sensing communities, particularly for developing and benchmarking methods for bamboo detection, multimodal data fusion, and UAV-based forest mapping in structurally complex, unmanaged landscapes.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Mapping EU biological medicines’ regulatory guidance through contributors and documents (1990/2026)
abstract: European Union Legislation in the sector of biological medicines is complemented by a substantial volume of guidance documents which are essential for strategic choices regarding biologicals development from lab to patients, especially authorisation processes as regards to quality, safety, and efficacy aspects. This corpus of guidance documents has historically been underutilised for research. Hence, the I-BioLex project has focused on both documents and actors, in a genealogical perspective. The two datasets presented in this paper gather all guidance documents relevant to this field, with comprehensive metadata, as well as a list of all contributors to public consultations conducted during the process of adoption or revision of these guidance documents in the field of biologicals at the EU level from 1990 to 2026. It constitutes an original foray into interdisciplinary research at the crossroads of social sciences (law, sociology,…) and biomedical sciences (medicine, pharmacy,…) in order to better understand how guidance documents are shaped and who is influencing them, in the field of biologicals.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Synchronous EEG-fNIRS Motor Execution and Imagery Dataset
abstract: In the field of motor imagery brain-computer interfaces (MI-BCI), researchers have developed multimodal BCI systems that leverage the complementary spatiotemporal characteristics of electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). This integration has been shown to substantially improve the accuracy and robustness of decoding movement intentions. However, publicly available synchronous EEG-fNIRS datasets for motor imagery tasks remain scarce. Such scarcity severely constrains the development of multimodal fusion algorithms. To address this gap, we introduce and openly release the Synchronous EEG-fNIRS Motor Execution and Imagery Dataset (SEFMEID), a concurrent hybrid EEG-fNIRS motor imagery dataset collected from 50 healthy participants. The dataset includes resting baseline, left-right hand motor execution (ME), and left-right hand motor imagery (MI) conditions, with each subject performing 25 trials for the right task and 25 trials for the left task. We also provide single-modality and multimodal classification results, as well as neurovascular coupling analyses, to validate the usability and quality of the dataset. In the deep learning results, the multimodal fusion algorithm achieves an improvement of approximately 10% over the best-performing unimodal approach. The public release of SEFMEID aims to serve as a valuable resource for advancing multimodal MI-BCI algorithms, investigating neurovascular coupling mechanisms underlying motor imagery, and accelerating clinical translation in neurological rehabilitation.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: The ParlLawSpeech Parliamentary Text Data Collection > 3 Million Parliamentary Bills, Laws, and Speeches from 8 Legislatures
abstract: Parliamentary texts are central sources for studying democratic representation, policy-making, and institutional decision-making, and they also constitute a highly valuable domain for natural language processing research. Despite their importance, access to comprehensive, clean, and machine-readable parliamentary corpora remains limited. This paper introduces the ParlLawSpeech (PLS) collection, a large-scale, curated corpus comprising more than three million documents from eight European parliaments, each covering over two decades. PLS extends existing parliamentary text resources in two key ways. First, it integrates full texts and metadata not only for parliamentary speeches but also for legislative bills and finally adopted laws. Second, it provides systematic data linkage across these document types, enabling researchers to trace the full parliamentary decision-making process from draft legislation through debate to adoption. Covering seven national parliaments and the European Parliament, PLS offers a uniquely rich resource for political science and advanced NLP research.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A spatiotemporally harmonized dataset of utility-reported power outages and NWS VTEC weather warnings for the contiguous United States (2015–2024)
abstract: Power grids across the United States are increasingly exposed to weather-related disruption, yet reproducible analyses are limited by differences in the spatial and temporal structure of outage and meteorological records. This Data Descriptor presents a harmonized, event-based archive linking county-level customer power-outage records from the U.S. Department of Energy EAGLE-I platform with National Weather Service watches, warnings and advisories encoded through the Valid Time Event Code system. The archive spans the contiguous United States from 2015 through 2024. The primary released file contains hourly indexed, positive processed outage observations that overlap at least one VTEC warning and include event identifiers, matched warning types, and source-record availability diagnostics. Companion files provide the consolidated warning archive, daily county-level EAGLE-I source-record availability and sensitivity summaries evaluating missing-record treatment, temporal aggregation, and recovery persistence. Technical validation quantifies the consequences of preprocessing assumptions and documents spatial, temporal and warning-matching consistency. The dataset supports reproducible analysis of spatiotemporal co-occurrence between reported power disruptions and operational weather warnings while explicitly retaining limitations associated with the underlying outage record.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Chinese Historical Epidemic Dataset
abstract: Epidemics represent high-impact events within the spectrum of human catastrophes, and China preserves a rich record of such occurrences. However, standardized, spatially explicit datasets with long-term temporal coverage remain limited. This study presents Chinese Historical Epidemic Dataset (CHED), a spatiotemporal database of epidemic events in China from 1056 BCE to 1949 CE. Derived primarily from A Compendium of Chinese Epidemic Disaster Records over Three Millennia , the dataset contains 32,389 annually resolved records with county-level spatial granularity and six core variables: time, location, cause, effect, category, and response. This systematic design enables source traceability, multi-granular querying, and precise spatiotemporal localization. As one of the longest-term and most spatially detailed historical epidemic dataset for China available, CHED is designed to support research on the historical globalization of infectious diseases and the long-term evolution of environment–health interactions.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: TCM4NSCLC: A real-world dataset and benchmark for Chinese-medicine reasoning on non-small-cell lung cancer
abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains one of the most burdensome malignancies worldwide. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) holds promise for stabilizing disease progression, alleviating symptoms, and improving quality of life. However, current evidence is predominantly derived from small-scale randomized controlled trials, which are inherently limited in capturing the complexity and longitudinal dynamics of pattern-based individualized care in real-world clinical settings. To address this gap, we present TCM4NSCLC—a standardized, computable, and shareable real-world dataset documenting TCM care for NSCLC. The dataset aggregates expert outpatient records from a senior TCM physician and comprises 3,790 structured cases with multiple visits. It encompasses demographic information, Western diagnoses and staging, pathology and laboratory tests, key imaging findings, clinical symptoms, tongue and pulse features, as well as original decoction prescriptions and Chinese Patent Medicines. We provide fine-grained annotations across ten named-entity categories, including diseases, drugs, investigations, tongue features, pulse signs, and symptoms. All data have undergone rigorous de-identification, denoising, deduplication, and quality control procedures. Multi-angle validation—including quality metrics, baseline modeling, and expert review—confirms the dataset’s internal consistency, usability, and clinical interpretability. TCM4NSCLC serves both as a digital repository of expert clinical knowledge and as a formalized knowledge representation that facilitates the integration of TCM into precision oncology. It supports (i) syndrome differentiation and prescription generation, (ii) real-world effectiveness assessment and subgroup discovery, and (iii) multimodal integrative decision-making and the development of intelligent clinical tools. The resource will be released with a unified schema, data dictionary, and usage guidelines to provide a reusable infrastructure for evidence-driven and intelligent TCM research in NSCLC.As a single-expert longitudinal corpus, TCM4NSCLC offers a uniquely coherent therapeutic philosophy and consistent clinical reasoning paradigm, providing a foundational resource for interpretable modeling while establishing a template for future multi-expert expansions.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: The m6A epitranscriptomic landscape of Setaria viridis and the domesticated foxtail millet (S. italica)
abstract: N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) is a pivotal epitranscriptomic modification that post-transcriptionally regulates RNA metabolism and contributes to plant growth and immune responses. However, the evolution and roles of m 6 A modifications in plant domestication remain largely unexplored. This study combined RNA-seq and MeRIP-seq data to compare m 6 A modifications profiles between foxtail millet ( Setaria italica , Yugu1) and its wild ancestor S. viridis (A10). Peak calling analysis identified 6,928 m 6 A peaks associated with 6,407 protein-coding genes in Yugu1 and 6,274 m 6 A peaks in 5,858 genes in A10, respectively. Comparative analysis revealed numerous differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and differentially methylated peaks (DMPs), whose functions were elucidated by GO and KEGG enrichment analyses. Integration of DMPs paired with DEGs, we found 209 hyper-methylated peaks associated with upregulated transcription levels, and 90 hypo-methylated peaks associated with downregulated transcription levels. This dataset provides valuable resource for further investigating the roles of m 6 A modification in crop domestication.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Citizen science dataset of urban heat perception and environmental measurements in outdoor public spaces across climate-vulnerable neighborhoods in the Barcelona metropolitan area
abstract: We present a dataset generated to investigate urban heat and thermal perception across five neighborhoods in the Barcelona metropolitan area. In collaboration with 14 non-academic partner organizations, we conducted a series of citizen science campaigns involving 439 residents as co-researchers engaged throughout all stages of the research process. Participants—residents of areas classified as highly or very highly climate-vulnerable—identified 210 public outdoor sites relevant to their daily lives. These locations were subsequently characterized using a range of spatial and environmental indicators pertinent to urban heat island effects, urban health, and climate resilience. Over the course of 48 thermal walks, participants carried portable, low-cost sensors that continuously recorded air temperature, relative humidity, and geolocation, resulting in 296 286 processed microclimatic data points. At pre-defined sites, individuals completed standardized surveys to report their Thermal Sensation Votes and Thermal Comfort Votes, yielding 5 169 self-reported entries. Sociodemographic data were also collected to further contextualize participants’ responses. The resulting dataset integrates objective environmental measurements with subjective perceptions of heat, enabling point-by-point analysis of thermal experience within the urban fabric. It offers a novel, multi-dimensional resource to support research on heat, thermal inequality, and the experiential dimensions of climate vulnerability, and is intended to inform evidence-based decision-making in urban planning, public health, and climate adaptation.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Chromosome-Level Genome Assembly of the Hybrid Grouper Epinephelus fuscoguttatus × Epinephelus lanceolatus
abstract: We present a chromosome-level genome assembly for the hybrid grouper ( Epinephelus fuscoguttatus ♀ × Epinephelus lanceolatus ♂). PacBio HiFi sequencing generated 5,951,738 reads totaling 122.82 Gb, with a read N50 of 21.55 kb. The 1.12-Gb primary assembly comprised 89 contigs with a contig N50 of 45.74 Mb, of which 1.08 Gb was anchored to 24 chromosomes. Two phased companion assemblies, Haploid 1 and Haploid 2, each contained 24 chromosome-scale sequences and spanned 1.085 and 1.088 Gb, respectively. Because parental ancestry was not assigned, these labels do not indicate maternal or paternal origin. BUSCO analysis using the actinopterygii_odb10 dataset recovered 97.80% complete orthologs. Repetitive sequences accounted for 44.24% of the genome. We identified 28,310 protein-coding gene models with a combined gene span of 604.72 Mb. The corresponding all-isoform set contained 124,025 predicted protein sequences representing translated coding transcripts rather than additional gene loci. Functional annotation was conducted at the protein-sequence level, with 122,472, 80,031, 64,401, and 74,117 sequences annotated against NR, KOG, GO, and KEGG, respectively. The principal features of this resource are its chromosome-scale organization, high contiguity, high BUSCO completeness, and phased companion assemblies. Because no genome-wide comparison with parental species or other groupers was performed, these features should not be interpreted as hybrid-specific or evolutionarily distinctive. This assembly provides a reference for future ancestry-aware comparative genomics and molecular breeding in groupers.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the mangrove-dwelling bivalve Enigmonia aenigmatica (Pectinoida: Anomiidae)
abstract: Enigmonia aenigmatica is a unique mangrove-dwelling bivalve species with remarkable ecological and morphological adaptations, yet its genomic background has remained unexplored. In this study, we combined PacBio HiFi long reads, WGS short reads, Hi-C data, Oxford Nanopore long-read transcriptome sequencing, and Illumina short-read transcriptome sequencing to assemble and annotate a high-quality reference genome for E. aenigmatica . We obtained a chromosome-level genome assembly with a total genome size of 465.97 Mb, comprising 8 chromosomes. The assembly exhibits exceptional contiguity, with a scaffold N50 of 58.83 Mb. Comprehensive gene annotation identified 17,728 protein-coding genes. This chromosome-level genome of E. aenigmatica provides a valuable genomic resource for future studies on mangrove-associated bivalves, molluscan evolution, and ecological adaptation in intertidal environments.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A whole-genome resequencing dataset of Kecai yaks from China
abstract: Endemic to the northeastern edge of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, the Kecai yak, a geographically distinct local yak population, serves as a useful resource for exploring the molecular mechanisms underlying high-altitude adaptation. In this study, we described a whole-genome resequencing dataset for Kecai yaks. Initially, 49 unrelated adult animals (25 males and 24 females) were sampled from Kecai Town, Xiahe County, Gannan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Gansu, China, across elevations of 3200–3800 m. We generated roughly 3.09 TB of raw sequencing data, with an average sequencing depth of 20.11×. We mapped clean reads to the yak reference genome, yielding an average alignment rate of 99.09%. Strict variant filtering identified 23.41 million high-confidence single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). This genome-wide SNP dataset can support studies of the genetic origins and high-altitude adaptation of Kecai yaks and provide genomic evidence to aid the conservation and practical use of this local yak germplasm.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: AS-OCT dataset with anatomical structure segmentation and scleral spur localization in cataract and glaucoma
abstract: Anterior Segment Optical Coherence Tomography (AS-OCT) provides high-resolution, non-invasive visualization of the anterior eye and is widely used for clinical diagnosis and surgical planning. However, automated analysis of AS-OCT images remains limited by the lack of publicly available datasets with comprehensive anatomical annotations and disease labels. Here we present the AS-OCT Multi-Structure and Disease Classification Dataset (ASOCT-MSDC), a curated dataset designed for anatomical structure segmentation and disease classification. The dataset contains 1106 AS-OCT images from 1106 eyes of 627 individuals across four clinical categories: normal, glaucoma, cataract, and glaucoma-cataract comorbidity. Each image underwent stringent quality assessment, and three standardized image quality scores—eyelid obscuration, black-line anomaly, and central light artifact—are provided as metadata. Expert-validated annotations include segmentation masks for the anterior chamber, iris, lens, and nucleus, together with scleral spur localization points. By combining anatomical annotations, disease labels, and image quality metadata, ASOCT-MSDC supports research on anatomical segmentation, disease classification, and image quality assessment in anterior segment OCT images.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Telomere-to-Telomere Genome Assembly and Graph-Based pan-genome Construction of Grifola frondosa (Maitake)
abstract: Grifola frondosa , also known as the “Maitake,” is a large fungus with both edible and medicinal value. Through whole-genome sequencing, we newly assembled five high-quality genomes from 36.7 to 39.6 Mb in size, with the scaffold N50 lengths of 2.8–3.2 Mb, including one telomere-to-telomere assembly (HT01). Together with five publicly available genomes, we constructed the pan-genome of G. frondosa , which contains 17,874 protein-coding gene clusters. Among these, 47.41% were core, 5.9% soft-core, 27.92% dispensable, and 18.78% private gene clusters, respectively. Using the T2T genome as a reference, we identified 3,741 nonredundant structural variants (SVs) and constructed a reference-based graph-based pan-genome of 46.9 Mb and a reference-free graph-based pan-genome of 62.6 Mb, respectively. This comprehensive pan-genome resource will provide a useful resource for breeding and genomic studies of G. frondosa .
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: The Dresden Dataset for 4D Reconstruction of Non-Rigid Abdominal Surgical Scenes
abstract: The D4D Dataset provides paired endoscopic video and high-quality structured-light geometry for evaluating 3D reconstruction of deforming abdominal soft tissue in realistic surgical conditions. Data were acquired from six porcine cadavers using a da Vinci Xi stereo endoscope and a Zivid structured-light camera, registered via optical tracking and manually curated iterative alignment methods. Three session types (whole deformations, incremental deformations, and moved-camera sessions) probe algorithm robustness to non-rigid motion, deformation magnitude, and out-of-view updates. Each clip provides rectified stereo images, per-frame instrument masks, stereo depth, start/end structured-light point clouds, curated camera poses and camera intrinsics. In postprocessing, ICP and semi-automatic registration techniques are used to register data, and instrument masks are created. The dataset enables quantitative geometric evaluation in both visible and occluded regions, alongside photometric view-synthesis baselines. Comprising over 300,000 frames and 369 point clouds across 98 curated sessions, this resource can serve as a comprehensive benchmark for developing and evaluating non-rigid SLAM, 4D reconstruction, and depth estimation methods.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: The Ostrya virginiana (Mill.) K. Koch [Betulaceae] genome: a chromosome-level assembly for a foundational understory tree in eastern North America
abstract: Ironwood ( Ostrya virginiana (Mill.) K. Koch) is an ecologically important tree species in temperate forests and holds significant horticultural and economic value. Despite its importance and the recent emergence of a threatening foliar rust disease, genomic resources for this species have been largely lacking. To address this gap, we present a high-quality, haplotype-phased, chromosome-level diploid genome assembly using a combination of PacBio HiFi long reads and Hi-C scaffolding. The finalized assembly successfully resolves into 8 pseudo-chromosomes per haplotype, with a total size of approximately 325 Mb each and an estimated heterozygosity rate of 1.15–1.18%. Genome annotation identified 45.71% and 45.57% repetitive content, along with 21,978 and 22,050 protein-coding genes in haplotype 1 and haplotype 2, respectively. Furthermore, BUSCO assessments indicated exceptional assembly quality, with approximately 99% completeness for the genome assemblies and 90% completeness for the predicted protein-coding gene sets. Functional characterization, assessed through homology-based assignments against the SwissProt, Pfam, and Gene Ontology (GO) databases, demonstrated that 92% of predicted proteins received at least one functional annotation. This robust reference genome provides a vital foundational resource for future research in forest ecology, phylogenomics, and host-pathogen interactions.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: An observation-based daily gridded precipitation dataset for forecast verification
abstract: As numerous artificial intelligence (AI)-based weather forecasting models are trained by climate reanalysis, there is an urgent need for independent observation-based datasets for forecast verification. Mainly based on the Global Historical Climatology Network (GHCN), this paper develops the GHCN daily gridded precipitation (GHCNdgp) dataset, covering the period from 2020 to 2025. Specifically, two daily station-based observation datasets–GHCN daily and Global Surface Summary of the Day–and three subdaily datasets–GHCN hourly, Integrated Surface Database and Integrated Global Land surface Dataset–are integrated to enhance global station density and spatial coverage. The spatiotemporal consistency checks are combined with integrity and reporting time checks to identify anomalous observations and infer stations’ reporting times. Furthermore, the GHCNdgp is compared against three existing precipitation products using Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC), i.e., the Integrated Multi-satellitE Retrievals for Global Precipitation Measurement (IMERG) V07 Late, the Multi-Source Weighted-Ensemble Precipitation (MSWEP) V2.8 and the Global Precipitation Climatology Centre (GPCC) First Guess Daily product. The results show that more than 90% of the anomalous observations come from identical values and duplicate sequences. The median PCC for stations with daily accumulation periods shifted by 24 hours is generally below 0.25. The quality control checks improve the median PCC from 0.46 to 0.62 under the IMERG, from 0.54 to 0.71 under the MSWEP and from 0.33 to 0.47 under the GPCC. These findings indicate that the GHCNdgp dataset effectively mitigates mismatches in observation reporting times and aligns with the grid resolution of 0.25° × 0.25° common in AI weather forecasts. This dataset is publicly available on Zenodo in the Network Common Data Form format, providing essential ground-truth precipitation observations specifically for benchmarking AI weather forecasts.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Multi-omic landscape of a porcine SCID model with a single-codon RAG2 deletion
abstract: Severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) research requires models that closely mimic human physiology. This study presents a comprehensive multi-omics dataset from a porcine model of RAG2bKO SCID, characterized by minimal genetic editing and extended survival. We generated a precise in-frame single-amino-acid deletion (p.His109del) in RAG2 using transcription activator-like effector nuclease (TALEN)-mediated editing. The dataset includes: (1) genomic sequencing data confirming the mutation and computational predictions of its structural impact on the RAG2 protein; (2) flow cytometry data quantifying the near-complete absence of mature adaptive lymphocytes; (3) histopathological images demonstrating thymic aplasia and splenic hypoplasia; (4) RNA-seq transcriptomic profiles from the thymus, spleen, and lymph nodes; and (5) ChIP-seq data for H3K4me3 histone modifications. This multi-layered and comprehensively characterised dataset provides a resource for studying SCID pathophysiology, comparative immunology, and benchmarking of therapeutic interventions in physiologically relevant large-animal models.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Small RNA sequencing dataset from muscle, gills and skin of Orestias ascotanensis obtained during winter and summer seasons
