abstract: Orestias ascotanensis is an endemic teleost inhabiting the spring-fed streams of the Ascotán salt pan (~3,700 m a.s.l.), in the Chilean Altiplano. This environment is characterized by variable water chemistry and high-altitude stressors, including hypoxia and ultraviolet radiation. Due to these unique ecological pressures, O. ascotanensis represents a valuable model system for studying molecular mechanisms of environmental adaptation. Among gene regulatory layers, microRNAs play a central role in fine-tuning gene expression by forming complex regulatory networks with mRNAs and long non-coding RNAs, ultimately shaping phenotypic responses to environmental change. This dataset provides small RNA expression profiles from three tissues of O. ascotanensis , to support characterization of its tissue-specific microRNA repertoire and seasonal expression patterns. The dataset comprises 42 sequencing libraries generated from gills, skin, and skeletal muscle of 14 wild adult individuals captured during winter (n = 7) and summer (n = 7). Raw sequencing data are accompanied by sample metadata and technical validation metrics to support data reuse and integrative analyses with existing genomic and transcriptomic resources.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A near telomere-to-telomere genome assembly of the freshwater pearl mussel Margaritifera dahurica
abstract: Margaritifera dahurica (Middendorff, 1850) is an ecologically and evolutionarily significant freshwater pearl mussel species belonging to the ancient family Margaritiferidae. Despite its critical role as a bio-indicator for ecosystem health, the lack of a high-quality reference genome has hindered research into its complex life cycle and conservation biology. Here, we present a near-complete telomere-to-telomere (near-T2T) genome assembly of M. dahurica generated by integrating high-depth PacBio HiFi (~90×), Nanopore ultra-long (~37×), and Hi-C data (~113×). The final assembly spans 2.86 Gb across 19 pseudo-chromosomes, with a scaffold N50 of 152.68 Mb and a contig N50 of 138.90 Mb. The successful identification of telomeric repeats at multiple chromosome ends confirms the assembly’s near-completeness. Genome annotation identified 1.98 Gb of repetitive elements (69.11% of the genome) and predicted 36,112 protein-coding genes, of which 93.95% were functionally assigned. Technical validation demonstrated high assembly quality, with a BUSCO completeness score of 98.55% and high consensus quality (QV) values. This near-T2T genome provides a foundational genetic resource for investigating the evolutionary history, specialized parasitic mechanisms, and conservation strategies of this endangered bivalve.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: SRAD: A Multibeam Acoustic Dataset for Submerged Reef Detection in a Laboratory-Recreated Seafloor Environment
abstract: Multibeam sonar is an important sensing modality for submerged reef detection, with potential applications in ROV operations, navigation safety, and offshore engineering. However, dedicated public acoustic datasets with object-level annotations for submerged reef or reef-like target detection remain limited, restricting the development and evaluation of relevant algorithms. To address this gap, we present SRAD, a multibeam acoustic dataset for submerged reef detection in a laboratory-recreated seafloor environment. The dataset contains more than 3,650 8-bit grayscale sonar images with corresponding ground-truth bounding-box annotations, together with native Oculus sonar logs and supporting data-processing tools. Data were collected in a controlled basin within a large-scale ocean engineering laboratory, where seafloor-related materials, including sand, gravel, natural rock reefs, algal reef materials, shell reefs, and simulated coral structures, were physically arranged to recreate a laboratory seafloor environment. To improve data consistency, an Oculus M750d multibeam sonar mounted on an ROV was used under consistent acquisition settings, and the ground-truth annotations were subjected to expert review and additional consistency checks. The resulting dataset provides labeled multibeam sonar images for the development, validation, and testing of submerged reef detection methods under controlled laboratory conditions, while the native Oculus sonar records and supporting processing tools enable further acoustic-data analysis and reuse.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Beyond built-up land: Mapping complete settlement footprint in China from 1990 to 2020 with Landsat imagery
abstract: Accurate mapping of human settlements is vital for understanding urbanization, human-environment interactions, and sustainable development. Existing medium-resolution products often underestimate the real spatial extent of settlements by focusing solely on built-up cores. Here, we present the China Settlement Footprint 1990–2020 (CSF30) dataset, a nationwide product depicting complete human settlement footprints from Landsat imagery at five-year intervals. CSF30 was generated using an Entity-Based Image Analysis framework integrated with a deep learning architecture. To ensure spatio-temporal generalizability and boundary accuracy, the model was trained via a two-stage strategy utilizing a built-up area dataset and a newly annotated settlement footprint dataset. Comprehensive validation demonstrates that CSF30 achieves a mean F1-score of 0.91 across the 30-year period, showing distinct advantages in representing rural and peri-urban areas compared to existing products. CSF30 provides a critical, high-quality baseline for diverse applications, including investigating settlement trajectories, assessing ecological and environmental impacts, and monitoring progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Four-Decade Dataset of Cotton Phenological Dynamics from the Agrometeorological Network in Xinjiang of China
abstract: This study presents a four-decade dataset (1981–2024) of cotton phenological dynamics, derived from 37 agrometeorological stations across China’s primary cotton production zone, the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region (hereinafter referred to as Xinjiang). The dataset comprises a total 22,274 records (589 MB (uncompressed); 364 MB (compressed)) documenting 9 key phenological periods—sowing, emergence, three-leaf, five-leaf, squaring, flowering, boll crack, open boll, and physiological maturity—and 5 derived growth phases. It integrates historical paper-based records with modern electronic archives, ensuring continuity and reliability through a multi-tiered quality control process. Advanced analytical methods, including kernel density estimation and univariate linear regression, were employed to characterize spatial distributions, interannual variability, and long-term trends in phenology. Application of these methods revealed a significant advancing trend in most phenological stages across the region, highlighting a clear response of cotton growth to climate change. This dataset offers a robust resource for investigating crop-climate interactions, validating process-based models, and informing climate adaptation strategies in arid and semi-arid agricultural systems. Its high spatial and temporal resolution supports diverse applications in agronomy, ecology, climatology, and agricultural policymaking. The dataset is publicly accessible via the Science Data Bank, providing a valuable benchmark for future studies on cotton phenology and sustainable crop management under changing climatic conditions.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: High-resolution dataset of core needle prostate biopsies with expert pathologist annotations
abstract: We present an expert-labelled image dataset designed to support automated analysis of image-guided prostate core needle biopsies (CNBs) in the context of prostate cancer diagnosis. The dataset includes 37 whole slide images (WSIs), corresponding to 60 CNBs stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E), from 32 patients. The dataset contains 15480 manual expert annotations, covering benign glands, tumor, stromal tissue, adipose tissue, nerves, nerve ganglia, blood vessels, muscle, and inflammatory cells. Additional recorded features include stromal retractions, normal and abnormal glandular secretions, and tissue or digital image artifacts. These annotations represent the normal findings that pathologists encounter in routine diagnosis. The annotations were performed by two experienced uropathologists with final labels determined by consensus; immunohistochemical techniques were used as guidance. This dataset provides a foundation for training and benchmarking machine learning models for prostate biopsy assessment and is openly available to facilitate reproducibility and further research.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A dataset of biomass burning emissions from multiple sources in China covering 1980 to 2024
abstract: Biomass burning (BB) is an important source of atmospheric carbonaceous aerosols and trace gases, exerting significant impacts on air quality, climate, and human health. However, a nationwide, long-term, and integrated BB emission dataset for China remains limited. Here, we construct a monthly gridded BB inventory for China covering 1980–2024. The dataset quantifies emissions of black carbon (BC), organic carbon (OC), sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ), carbon monoxide (CO), and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) from seven source categories, including forest fires, shrub fires, grassland fires, in-field straw burning, domestic straw burning, firewood burning, and livestock-manure burning. Emissions from domestic BB and in-field straw burning are reconstructed for 1980–2024 and are spatially allocated using rural-residential population and cropland proxies, respectively. Forest, shrub, and grassland fire emissions are estimated from satellite observations for 2001–2024 and aggregated with the other sources to a common 1 km grid. Parameter and reconstruction uncertainties are quantified using Monte Carlo and bootstrap methods, while key structural assumptions are evaluated through sensitivity analyses. Comparisons with published studies and global fire-emission inventories show broadly consistent magnitudes and temporal variations. The dataset supports analyses of long-term emission trends, source attribution, atmospheric modelling, and environmental assessment.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Multivariate Electrical Measurements of Household Appliances with Synchronized Zone Occupancy Tracking
abstract: Home energy management systems can reduce electricity consumption and operating costs, leading to environmental benefits. Their effective operation relies on accurate information about real-time and long-term appliance usage, which can be obtained via nonintrusive load monitoring (NILM). Progress in NILM, including fair benchmarking of algorithms, critically depends on well-documented, high-quality datasets. Here, we describe a multimodal dataset comprising synchronized recordings of 12 commonly used household appliances and radar-based zone occupancy data tracking occupants’ presence across zones during appliance operation. The dataset provides voltage and current waveforms sampled at 20 kS/s, harmonic components up to the 50th order, power measurements at 200 ms resolution, and radar-derived zone occupancy data at 1 s resolution. By combining rich electrical measurements with radar-based contextual information, the dataset supports research on multimodal NILM, activity-aware disaggregation, and context-informed energy management. This publicly available dataset combines a broad set of electrical features with synchronized radar-based zone occupancy context.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A multisensor dataset of energy use and activity in Dutch social housing
abstract: This research introduces the HOMESENSE dataset, comprising indoor environmental quality data from 11 social-rental dwellings in Limburg, the Netherlands, together with available electricity and gas measurements over 366 consecutive local calendar days ending in November 2025. Released files use a common 10-minute publication grid rather than uniform native resolution. This interval is native to the principal room-environment and thermostatic-valve streams, supports aggregation of faster streams, and aligns slower and event-driven streams using documented bounded-gap rules. Each measurement is paired with a quality-control (QC) field distinguishing observed , interpolated , reset-imputed , and missing values. The release also includes Maastricht weather records. Data are provided as comma-separated value (CSV) files with source code and Jupyter notebooks for reproducible loading, analysis, and release processing. The dataset supports research on activity patterns, heating control, indoor thermal conditions, low-frequency load attribution, and coarse-resolution non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) using appliance-level measurements alongside whole-dwelling grid exchange.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Vineyard RGB-D, LiDAR and GNSS/RTK datasets for grapevine segmentation and localisation to enable autonomous robotic pruning
abstract: Agricultural robotics is becoming increasingly relevant for executing arduous tasks where human labour is scarce. Grapevine pruning is a seasonal task that, when performed manually, requires a worker to perform selective cutting of the grapevine canes. For a robot to conduct this type of task autonomously, it needs to navigate the vineyard rows without colliding with the grapevines, as well as retain information regarding each grapevine to perform the operation. This work presents datasets collected in a vineyard, comprising RGB and depth images, LiDAR and GNSS/RTK data, acquired using both a handheld device and a mobile robot. Furthermore, 494 RGB images obtained from the handheld device recordings were annotated with segmentation masks in YOLO format. The datasets support the development and evaluation of computer vision, localisation, mapping and sensor fusion algorithms for autonomous robots. Technical validation demonstrates the consistency and usability of the annotated data for training deep learning models.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A high-resolution global flood susceptibility dataset derived from multi-source earth observation and geospatial data
abstract: Floods are among the most damaging disasters worldwide, necessitating high-resolution modeling of where terrain and environmental conditions predispose societies to flooding. While geospatial data are invaluable for flood susceptibility mapping, comprehensive and globally consistent datasets remain scarce. We present the Global Flood Susceptibility Map (GFSM v1), a globally harmonized 30 m flood susceptibility dataset produced by incorporating multi-source flood conditioning factors accounting for topographic, hydrological, meteorological, and anthropogenic characteristics within a machine learning framework. A gradient-boosted tree model was trained on ~17,000 curated grid tiles with ~30.45 million training samples, using a global flood inundation dataset as training labels and nine conditioning factors (elevation, slope, aspect, wetness index, vegetation index, height above nearest drainage, water/roads proximity, and rainfall frequency). The model was deployed based on geopolitical and climate strata (units n = 192) to generate global pixel-level susceptibility. Rigorous cross-validation indicates strong model predictive accuracy (median area-under-curve ~0.95), and the output captures localized flood-prone regions worldwide. GFSM v1 offers a global open-source, high-resolution resource to support informed flood risk management, particularly in data-sparse regions.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Global monthly diurnal temperature cycle parameters over land at 0.1° resolution for 1990–2024
abstract: We describe a global gridded dataset of monthly climatological diurnal temperature cycle parameters over land at 0.1° resolution for 1990–2024. Using hourly 2 m air temperature from ERA5-Land, we fitted a dual-harmonic model to the multi-year mean hourly climatology for each eligible ERA5-Land grid cell and calendar month. The archive stores monthly mean temperature, the amplitudes and phase parameters of the 24 h and 12 h harmonics, fitted diurnal temperature range, fitted hours of daily minimum and maximum temperature, and quality-control diagnostics. Together these variables provide a compact description of local diurnal temperature shape that can be used for hourly reconstruction, temporal disaggregation, and gap filling when only daily summaries or sparse intra-day observations are available. Technical validation against ERA5-Land and NOAA hourly station observations shows that the parameterised diurnal template reproduces the main amplitude and timing structure across most land regions. In the full 2015–2020 NOAA evaluation, supplying observed daily range in addition to daily mean reduced pooled hourly RMSE from 2.24 to 1.94 °C. Under strict anchor-only held-out evaluation, fixed 12 UTC one-point and clipped fixed 00/12 UTC two-point reconstruction achieved pooled RMSE values of 3.045 and 2.976 °C, respectively. The dataset is publicly available through Zenodo and provides a compact, globally consistent prior for reconstructing sub-daily temperature variation from daily summaries or sparse observations.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: CTX-UXO: Contextual visual dataset for localisation, classification and identification of unexploded ordnance
abstract: Unexploded Ordnances (UXOs) are explosive weapons that failed to detonate during deployment, posing significant threats to civilian safety and post-conflict recovery. The Contextual Vision for Unexploded Ordnances (CTX-UXO) dataset addresses this challenge by providing 3520 high-resolution RGB images, median size 2124 px square, containing UXOs collected over four years across all seasons and weather conditions. The dataset encompasses 15 449 annotated instances labeled as UXOs, with twelve subcategories for identification tasks, in which mortar bombs, projectiles and grenades constitute the predominant classes, supporting systems research and development in UXO classification, detection, instance segmentation and related applications, and providing multiple labelling formats such as YOLO and COCO. For the detection task including binary classification, an end-to-end solution for training, validation and testing is available as a reference by presenting a neural network optimized for edge deployment, Faster-RCNN with MobileNet V3 backbone, deployed for real-time inference with reduced costs on Nvidia Jetson Orin, achieving up to 23 frames per second with 62.18% Ap50 for UXO localisation and binary classification.

title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the model organism Lumbriculus variegatus (Lumbriculidae: Clitellata)
abstract: Aquatic oligochaetes (~10% of annelids) are important of pollutant toxicity assessment but lack genomic resources. We report the first chromosome level genome of Lumbriculus variegatus (a model organism for toxicity accumulation experiment) by using long-read sequencing data, short-read sequencing data, Hi-C, and RNA-seq. The 1.15 Gb assembly has contig N50 2.01 Mb, with 98.98% sequences anchored onto 17 chromosomes (scaffold N50 67.05 Mb), and high completeness (BUSCO 97.0%, a short-read mapping rate 99.49%, and a long-read mapping rate 98.94%). The QV values based on short- and long-reads were 57.45 and 61.21. Repetitive elements comprise 56.27% with LINEs accounting for 17.21%. We annotated 24,754 protein-coding genes with a BUSCO of 97.3% (96.56% functionally assigned) and 16,288 non-coding RNAs. This genome provides a crucial resource for studying cryptic speciation, genome evolution, adaptation, and toxicological mechanisms in annelids.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: The FunAqua dataset of global fungal biodiversity in aquatic ecosystems
abstract: Advances in high-throughput DNA sequencing technologies have accelerated research on aquatic microorganisms, their diversity, and ecological functions. This has also significantly advanced research on fungi that shape aquatic ecosystems and food webs. Here, we present the FunAqua dataset, which describes global fungal biodiversity in aquatic ecosystems based on eukaryotic long-read metabarcoding data from 1,076 sediment and 1,299 filtered water samples collected across 1,452 sampling sites in 87 countries. We targeted the internal transcribed spacer (ITS) region. In total, 50,152 fungal OTUs were recorded. The sequencing data is accompanied by comprehensive sample metadata, including physicochemical data of water and sediments. The FunAqua dataset provides a new resource for analysing and better understanding the biodiversity of fungi in different types of aquatic habitats across biogeographical regions. The dataset described in this data paper will be periodically updated with additional metabarcoding data.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: CCF Database: A Machine-Learning-Annotated Corpus of 283,964 Canadian Climate Articles (1978–2026)
abstract: News media shape how societies perceive and respond to climate change, yet fine-grained analysis remains hindered by fragmented corpora and ad hoc coding schemes. The Canadian Climate Framing (CCF) database answers both with a large-scale bilingual annotated corpus and a generalizable annotation framework. It covers 283,964 climate-related articles from 22 Canadian news outlets (1978–2026), processed into 9,908,776 two-sentence units (83.4% English, 16.6% French). Each unit carries 65 hierarchical binary annotations spanning eight main frames, actors, events, solutions, tone, geography, and urgency, produced by 128 BERT and CamemBERT classifiers trained on 4,000+ expert-coded sentences. Against a 1,000-sentence gold standard double-coded by an independent annotator (Cohen’s κ = 0.596, Krippendorff’s α = 0.698, Gwet’s AC1 = 0.894), the classifiers reach a pooled macro F 1 of 0.866 (mean per-category macro F 1 = 0.773), and every category carries an A/B/C reliability tier. The database—sentence-level annotations, per-article aggregations, and 10,192,740 BAAI/bge-m3 embeddings in six relational tables—is openly released on Zenodo (CC-BY 4.0) as a PostgreSQL edition and an Apache Parquet mirror, refreshed roughly every six months by the CCF Observatory.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: ACEL-Eval: A Benchmark Dataset for End-to-end Entity Linking in Classical Chinese
abstract: As premodern texts become increasingly accessible in digital form, a major obstacle to their computational analysis is the lack of structured resources for identifying and normalizing historical entities. This challenge is especially evident in Classical Chinese, where standardized benchmarks for end-to-end entity linking remain limited. To address this need, we present ACEL-Eval, a benchmark dataset for evaluating entity linking in Classical Chinese. ACEL-Eval is derived from the Shiji and covers six entity categories that frequently occur in classical historical writing: person , location , state , official title , book , and time . The dataset supports end-to-end entity linking by combining named entity recognition over six entity categories with entity disambiguation for person mentions. To facilitate person referent normalization, we provide a person-oriented knowledge base containing core attributes such as personal names, aliases, and state affiliation. We conduct baseline experiments on the two target tasks to validate dataset usability and to establish reproducible reference results for future comparison. ACEL-Eval is designed to serve as a benchmark resource for Classical Chinese entity linking and as a reference for related computational studies of premodern Chinese historical texts.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Long-term seasonal ruminant livestock distribution datasets in China’s grazing production systems
abstract: Accurate spatial distribution data of grazing livestock are essential for rangeland management and sustainability assessments, yet existing global datasets lack production system differentiation and seasonal resolution. We present China’s Long-term Ruminant Livestock Distribution in Grazing Livestock Production Systems (CLRD-GLPS) dataset, providing seasonally resolved distributions of cattle, sheep, and goats across China’s grazing systems from 2000 to 2021. The dataset was generated using a stacking ensemble machine learning framework integrating Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, and Extra Trees, combined with interpretable machine learning for livestock segmentation. CLRD-GLPS includes 1-km resolution gridded maps distinguishing warm-season and cold-season distributions, with CV-based model-uncertainty layers. Model validation on independent test data achieved R 2 values of 0.954–0.961 for cattle and 0.896–0.915 for sheep/goats. External validation at city level yielded R 2 of 0.74–0.81, supporting dataset reliability across spatial scales. The dataset addresses critical gaps in livestock distribution mapping by separating grazing from non-grazing systems and capturing seasonal dynamics, supporting applications in forage-livestock balance assessment, climate impact studies, and evidence-based policy development.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A dataset of multichannel broadband recordings of sounds and vibrations acquired from arteriovenous fistulas via a novel force sensor array
abstract: Arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) are the preferred vascular access for hemodialysis in end-stage renal disease patients. AVFs generate vibrations and sounds due to the peculiar blood flow. Frequent monitoring of these signs is essential for early diagnosis of stenoses, which are the main complication of AVFs. Existing datasets contain only recordings of AVFs bruit sounds acquired via electronic stethoscopes. This paper presents the “Fistula Sounds and Vibrations (FiSaV)” dataset, the first ever publicly available dataset of broadband vibrations and sounds recordings from radio-cephalic AVFs that comprise sphygmic pulses, thrills, and bruits sounds. Signals were acquired by means of an array of broadband force sensors placed onto patients’ skin along the cephalic vein from the anastomosis to the elbow crease. An electrocardiographic lead was simultaneously acquired to provide heartbeats reference. The dataset contains recordings of at least 3 minutes, acquired from 59 patients, 40 with stenosis and 19 without stenosis, comfortably seated with their forearms resting on a table. For some patients, recordings include an additional occlusion test. The open accessibility of the FiSaV dataset aims to facilitate advances in non-invasive monitoring of AVF function by providing objective support for physical examination. The data may promote the development of innovative diagnostic tools and algorithms to detect AVF dysfunction and hemodynamic alterations for a better surveillance and management of hemodialysis patients.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A harmonized European database of education, telework, labour market and earnings from three Eurostat surveys
abstract: VSET is a harmonized cross-survey profile-space resource documenting the alignment of education, occupation, labour-market, telework, establishment size, and earnings variables from three Eurostat surveys. It combines three Eurostat microdata sources accessed under an approved research proposal: the Adult Education Survey (AES) 2022, the Labour Force Survey (LFS) 2023, and the Structure of Earnings Survey (SES) 2018. The final harmonized database contains data for 22 countries, 1,440,134 unique demographic profile cells, 39 variables, and a summed profile multiplicity of 3,249,634. Occupations are standardized using ISCO-08 at the 2-digit level, educational attainment is harmonized into four ISCED-based groupings, and SES earnings are converted to euros before aggregation. The integration workflow uses sequential outer joins and deterministic coalescing of overlapping variables. The final rows describe harmonized profiles rather than linked individuals. The N_instances variable records the multiplicity of identical rows combined during final profile compression. The release has no integrated survey weight. Its rows represent harmonized profile combinations rather than linked respondents or population units, and the dataset is intended for inspecting category mappings, profile coverage, merge compatibility, and reproducible cross-survey processing rather than for population inference.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Pan-European Multimodal Dataset Linking Field Photos with Satellite Image Time Series for Agricultural Mapping
abstract: AgroFusion is a continental-scale, multimodal, pixel-based reference dataset designed to support rigorous evaluation and reproducible research in agricultural remote sensing and geospatial Artificial Intelligence (AI). Built upon the 2018 and 2022 Land Use/Cover Area frame statistical Survey (LUCAS), the dataset integrates 211,483 field observations (107,642 in 2018 and 103,841 in 2022), each linked to field photos (four cardinal views, point centered view, and a close-up), LUCAS land-cover and land-use annotations, with monthly pixel-based Satellite Image Time Series (SITS) from Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, and Landsat-8, agrometeorological data from ERA5-Land, topography from the Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, soil properties from AI4SoilHealth, and annual embeddings from AlphaEarth geo-foundation model. AgroFusion is the first continental-scale resource for pairing geo-tagged field photos with pixel-based SITS, semantically rich agricultural covariates, and precomputed foundation model embeddings. This combination will enable a wide range of applications, including multimodal and multiscale crop type classification and phenology retrieval, and the interpretation of satellite-derived agricultural products using ground-level visual context.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A curated comprehensive dataset of asymmetric organocatalytic Mannich reaction
abstract: The asymmetric organocatalytic Mannich reaction is one of the key methods for constructing chiral β-aminocarbonyl moieties that occur in the structures of many biologically active compounds, including drugs. The selection of a catalyst and reaction conditions that ensure high enantioselectivity for specific substrates remains a largely empirical task. The scarcity of structured, openly available data hinders the application of machine-learning methods to enantioselectivity prediction and rational catalyst design. We present a dataset of 4015 reactions manually extracted from 153 publications spanning 2000–2025 and covering 468 unique organocatalysts. The structures of the reagents and catalysts, the reaction conditions, and the target values ( ee , ΔΔG‡) are provided in a machine-readable form suitable for training AI-models.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Benchmark Dataset of Simultaneous Pickup-Delivery Instances for Demand-controlled and Emission-aware Routing
abstract: Vehicle routing with simultaneous pickup and delivery is a routing problem in which a customer may receive goods from the depot and return goods to it during the same visit. It is the routing structure underlying reverse logistics, the circulation of reusable containers, and circular supply chains. The benchmark instances available for this problem are comparatively small, cover a narrow range of customer counts, and provide little systematic control over the balance between pickup and delivery demand, the tightness of vehicle capacity, or the severity of the time windows. We present SPIDER (Simultaneous Pickup-Delivery Instances for Demand-controlled Emission-aware Routing), a collection of 1,152 instances generated from a complete factorial design over six customer-size levels, three spatial layouts, four pickup-to-delivery demand-ratio strata, four vehicle-capacity levels, and four time-window regimes. Instances range from 50 to 1,000 customers. Each instance specifies depot and customer coordinates, delivery and pickup demands, service times, time-window bounds, and optional load-dependent emission parameters. A master index, a parser, and a distance utility accompany the data, so that instances can be selected or regenerated by design factor.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Renewable generation and electricity consumption datasets for energy market models generated with artificial intelligence
abstract: Analysis of future energy scenarios requires comprehensive and reliable input datasets. Open-access datasets increase transparency and reduce barriers to entry in modeling. In our study, we use artificial neural network models to transform 43 years of weather reanalysis data into hourly resolution, nationwide time series of renewable energy production (solar, onshore and offshore wind) and electricity consumption datasets. During our research, we developed a data quality control procedure for the ENTSO-E hourly-resolution database based on heat maps, histograms, and z-score values, thereby ensuring that our artificial intelligence models learn from high-quality data. Modeling was performed for all European countries with sufficient data quantity and quality to train machine learning models. The proposed neural-network-based database combines the widest spatial coverage among the reviewed datasets with accuracy that in most cases exceeds existing solar, wind, and electricity consumption databases, making it a valuable complement for European electricity system modelling. The open-access data series created can be used directly as input data for electricity market models, e.g., in unit commitment, network load distribution and pricing studies, and are also particularly suitable for analyzing the frequency, duration, and regional overlap of periods of low renewable energy production (Dunkelflaute events).
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: PRIME-CVD: Paired Synthetic Cohort and Structured EMR-Style Data Assets for Education in Cardiovascular Risk Modelling
abstract: In recent years, progress in medical informatics and machine learning has been accelerated by the availability of openly accessible benchmark datasets. However, patient-level electronic medical record (EMR) data are rarely available for teaching or methodological development due to privacy, governance, and re-identification risks. This has limited opportunities for students from healthcare and clinical backgrounds to gain hands-on experience in coding, data management, and cardiovascular risk modelling. Here we introduce PRIME-CVD, a parametrically rendered informatics medical environment designed explicitly for medical education. PRIME-CVD comprises two openly accessible synthetic data assets, each representing 50,000 adults undergoing primary prevention for cardiovascular disease and parameterised to reproduce the statistical characteristics of a derivation cohort from the Australian New South Wales Lumos linked-data resource. The datasets are generated entirely from a user-specified causal directed acyclic graph parameterised using characteristics of the reference cohort, publicly available Australian population statistics and published epidemiologic effect estimates, rather than from patient-level EMR data or trained generative models. Data Asset 1 provides a clean, analysis-ready cohort suitable for teaching exploratory analysis, stratification, statistical coding, and survival modelling, while Data Asset 2 systematically transforms the same cohort into a structured relational, EMR-style database with deliberately introduced data-quality challenges, including missingness, heterogeneous terminology, inconsistent measurement units, and cross-table linkage requirements. Together, these complementary assets enable healthcare and clinical learners to develop practical skills in coding, data cleaning, harmonisation, cohort reconstruction, and cardiovascular risk modelling without exposing sensitive information. Because all individuals and events are generated de novo, PRIME-CVD preserves realistic subgroup imbalance and risk gradients while ensuring negligible disclosure risk. Although the released PRIME-CVD cohort represents adults with no prior history of cardiovascular disease undergoing primary-prevention risk assessment, the complete data-assembly pipeline is provided through the dedicated GitHub repository. Educators may adapt the supplied code, parameters, and data-generating assumptions to construct alternative synthetic cohorts suited to their own teaching objectives. PRIME-CVD is released under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence to support reproducible and scalable health data science education.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Nationwide annual agricultural land-use maps of Germany from 1990 to 2023 derived from satellite imagery
abstract: We present German-wide annual agricultural land-use maps from 1990 to 2023, created from Landsat and Sentinel-2 images using a deep learning approach. Based on farmers’ declarations from 2006 to 2022, we extracted annual training samples for 13 crop classes and one grassland class. These samples were used to train a multi-year one-dimensional convolutional neural network, which was subsequently applied to generate the annual land-use maps. Between 2010 and 2022, overall map accuracies ranged between 85% and 93%. When averaged over time, dominant classes like grassland, rapeseed, winter cereals, sugar beet, and maize were detected with high accuracy (≥90%). Conversely, minor classes such as fallow land and plantation were predicted with low accuracy (≤52%). Comparison of map areas with agricultural statistics over time revealed high correlations for most classes, particularly maize ( r = 0.978). The presented maps provide an essential basis for analyzing long-term trends in agricultural land-use. They can be used to fill temporal gaps in national agricultural statistics and to disaggregate those statistics to higher spatial units.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A dataset of strong dependency and conflict graphs generated from Boolean formulas encoding the variability of highly configurable software systems
abstract: Variability models describe the configuration options of highly configurable software systems and the direct constraints between them. The dependencies and conflicts those constraints indirectly cause are hidden in the model and too hard to check manually, making it difficult to analyze very large systems like the Linux kernel. This Data Descriptor documents a dataset of 5,709 records that makes those indirect relationships explicit. Each record includes two graphs based on the Boolean formula that represents the variability model of one configurable system: a strong dependency graph and a strong conflict graph. We created each record from publicly available Boolean formulas that other researchers made from variability models and shared under an open license, using our own tool: a C++ program that runs two algorithms based on step-by-step satisfiability solving. The resulting graphs range from 99 to 35,907 options, with a median of 2,874. Provided in the Pajek NET format with clear documentation, and released with the input formulas and the code that builds and checks the graphs, the dataset helps test configuration and sampling methods and supports research on conflict detection, impact analysis, and automated reasoning.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A harmonized cross-national dataset of digital sectors
abstract: Digital sectors have emerged as a key driver of firm innovation, productivity and economic growth. Building on the OECD framework, the United Kingdom introduced a digital sector classification in 2015. China has likewise developed its own digital sector classification as part of its broader effort to define and measure the digital economy. However, the absence of a harmonized correspondence between these classification systems constrains cross-country comparisons and empirical research, particularly when Chinese datasets are integrated with international data involving digital inputs and outputs. To address this gap, we construct a concordance dataset linking the Chinese and UK digital sector classifications. Using nearly 15 million firms from the Orbis database, we document differences in the coverage and distribution of digital sectors across geographies, countries, and industries under the three classification frameworks. The dataset enables researchers to evaluate how alternative definitions influence the measurement of the digital economy at the firm, industry, and aggregate levels, providing a valuable resource for comparative research and evidence-based policy-making.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Chromosome-level reference genome assembly of the Fusarium avenaceum
abstract: Fusarium avenaceum is a widely distributed fungal species that includes polyphagous plant pathogens, some of which produce mycotoxins of concern to agricultural production and food safety. Here, we present genome sequencing data and an RNA-seq dataset generated to support gene annotation for F. avenaceum strain XZ-22-127, which was isolated from highland barley. PacBio HiFi reads and Hi-C data were used to generate a 42.26-Mb assembly comprising nine chromosomes, with a scaffold N50 of 5.07 Mb and a GC content of 47.97%. BUSCO analysis identified 99.9% of the expected BUSCOs as complete. Compared with the previously available chromosome-level assembly of F. avenaceum strain WV21P1A, the XZ-22-127 assembly had a slightly higher scaffold N50 (5.07 versus 4.96 Mb) and BUSCO completeness (99.9% versus 99.7%), while the two assemblies were similar in genome size, GC content, and chromosome number. The deposited resources include the raw sequencing reads, chromosome-level assembly, protein-coding gene models, repeat annotations, predicted transcript, coding-sequence and protein files, and InterProScan and eggNOG-mapper functional annotation files. These datasets provide a complementary genomic resource for F. avenaceum and related fungi.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A global 60 m land cover dataset with a fine classification system for 1975 and 1980 derived from Landsat MSS observations
abstract: Long-term land cover datasets are essential for understanding human-environment interactions and global environmental change, yet global land cover information pre-1985 remains scarce because of limited availability of early satellite observations. Here, we present GLC_FCS60, the first global 60 m land cover dataset with a fine classification system for 1975 and 1980, derived from Landsat Multispectral Scanner (MSS) observations. Specifically, an improved comprehensive change detection method with an adaptive thresholding strategy was applied to identify changed and unchanged land-cover pixels. The detected changed areas were then updated using high-confidence temporally stable training samples and locally adaptive classification models on the Google Earth Engine platform. The updated land cover maps were further optimized through post-processing to mitigate potential spurious changes, after which the GLC_FCS60 time-series maps were generated. Finally, using 71,983 globally distributed validation samples, we assessed the accuracy of GLC_FCS60, achieving overall accuracies of 80.13% and 80.08% for the 10 basic classes in 1975 and 1980, respectively, while a dedicated change/no-change validation achieved an overall accuracy of 78.61%. Therefore, GLC_FCS60 fills a critical gap in global land cover observations prior to the mid-1980s and provides a valuable baseline for investigating long-term land cover dynamics from the mid-1970s to the present.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Multi-Center, Multi-Modal Chest CT and Clinical Dataset for Differentiating Pulmonary Aspergillus from Non-Aspergillus and Non-Fungal Infections
abstract: Pulmonary Aspergillus infection (PAI) presents a critical diagnostic challenge due to its clinical management differing significantly from that of pulmonary non- Aspergillus fungal infection (PNAFI) and pulmonary non-fungal infection (PNFI). While Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a promising solution for rapid triage, its development is currently severely bottlenecked by data scarcity. Existing studies primarily rely on small, private, and single-center datasets, which hampers the generalizability of models and precludes reproducible research. To date, there is no publicly available, multi-center benchmark dataset that integrates imaging with key host immune factors for this domain. To address this critical gap, we present the first comprehensive, open-access dataset of its kind, collected from 569 patients across 4 hospitals in China. This dataset comprises: (1) standardized volumetric chest CT scans in NIfTI format; (2) a curated clinical record containing definitive diagnostic labels, demographics, and critical laboratory variables (e.g., lymphocyte counts, D-dimer). Technical validation was conducted for two binary tasks: Task 1, Fungi vs Non-Fungi, and Task 2, Aspergillus vs non- Aspergillus . This study introduced three models for classification: a clinical model using clinical variables, an imaging model based on CT images, and a fusion model combining both clinical variables and CT images. Model performance was evaluated through receiver operating characteristic analysis, with sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and area under the curve (AUC) reported as key metrics. As a rare and versatile resource, this dataset supports not only the development of robust AI classification algorithms but also facilitates clinical prediction modeling, the investigation of the predictive role of host variables (e.g., age, comorbidities), decision-making regarding invasive interventions, and radiological education, thereby accelerating precision medicine in pulmonary infectious diseases.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Multiproxy dataset for the Holocene sedimentary record of the Sado Valley, southwest Portugal
abstract: Paleoenvironmental characterization and studies of the environmental evolution of coastal basins (e.g. lagoons and estuaries) are based on information retrieved from sedimentary records through the analysis of diverse environmental proxies. This information is often presented only in figures, illustrations, and graphics in published papers, while the raw data are difficult to access. Nevertheless, this information is valuable for (i) increasing resolution (adding more data) within the same sedimentary basin, both vertically (i.e., in-depth; through time) and horizontally (i.e., spatial analyses); (ii) comparing results among similar coastal systems, and iii) analyzing different responses to diverse forcings in coastal systems located elsewhere. This dataset provides the results of sedimentological and paleoenvironmental (texture, magnetic susceptibility, total organic matter, organic carbon and total nitrogen content, C/N elemental ratios, and C and N stable isotope ratios) proxy analyses in sediment cores collected in the lower Sado Valley (Portugal).
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A dataset of full-length transcripts for the giant freshwater prawn (Macrobrachium rosenbergii)
abstract: Macrobrachium rosenbergii is a major global aquaculture species, but its large (~3-4 Gb), highly heterozygous and repeat-rich genome has resulted in fragmented draft assemblies, limiting accurate gene annotation and functional genomics. High-quality, isoform-resolved full-length transcripts are therefore essential for gene discovery and downstream applications. Here, we present a dataset of full-length transcripts generated from seven tissues of an adult female M. rosenbergii (i.e., hemolymph, antennal base, eyestalk, gill, brain, intestine, and abdominal ganglion), producing 4,131,688 circular consensus sequences and 38,955 non-redundant full-length transcripts (N50 = 3,383 bp) using PacBio Iso-Seq. Functional annotation was assigned to 32,275 transcripts using multiple public databases, and 17,696 candidate long non-coding RNAs were predicted, including 2,712 high-confidence lncRNAs supported by four complementary tools. The reliability and reusability were independently validated by mapping Illumina short-read RNA-seq data from nine libraries constructed from brain tissues of three male morphotypes to the Iso-Seq reference transcripts, achieving 72.44% overall mapping rates. This dataset provides a comprehensive, reference-quality full-length transcripts for M. rosenbergii , enabling improved genome annotation, isoform-level expression analysis, and comparative transcriptomics.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A paediatric dataset of non-dermoscopic skin images for dermatological AI research
abstract: This paper introduces DermoPed, a non-dermoscopic dermatology dataset composed almost entirely of paediatric patients’ images. The long-term goal is to advance research in automated dermatological image analysis with a specific focus on non-dermoscopic images, i.e., those captured using consumer-grade cameras, thereby promoting accessible diagnosis for underprivileged and underserved populations. However, this objective is often challenged by the limited availability of data and the heterogeneous quality of clinical images, issues that are discussed in detail in this work and carefully addressed during the preprocessing phase. The resulting dataset comprises more than 46,000 medium-to-high quality images from 229 distinct patients, the majority of whom are paediatric. In addition, we release a separate “challenging” subset of lower-quality crops with automatically computed image-quality labels, intended to support the study of model robustness under realistic acquisition conditions.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Monthly Coal Mine-Level Methane Emission Dataset for China from 2018 to 2024
abstract: Coal mine methane (CMM) is a major source of methane emissions in the energy sector and plays a significant role in global climate change. However, existing CMM emission inventories are typically limited to national or provincial scales and lack long-term, high spatial resolution datasets at the coal mine level. To address this gap, this study develops a comprehensive methane emission dataset covering over 3,000 coal mines across China (excluding Taiwan) from 2018 to 2024. The dataset systematically integrates multi-source coal production data and applies a hybrid estimation framework combining IPCC Tier 1, 2 and 3 methodologies. It includes detailed information on mine name, administrative location (province and prefecture-level city), geographic coordinates, production capacity, mining type, methane emission factors, and monthly emissions. Uncertainty in emissions is quantified using Monte Carlo simulations. National CMM emissions increased overall from 25.10 Mt CH 4 in 2018 to 32.87 Mt CH 4 in 2024, despite a slight decline from the 2023 peak. The estimated uncertainty ranges from 8.93% to 14.74%, indicating that the results remain within an acceptable level of uncertainty. Multi-scale comparisons indicate that the dataset applies more localized emission factors, provides more accurate source locations, and captures broadly reliable temporal trends. This dataset provides a robust foundation for analyzing the spatiotemporal patterns of CMM emissions, assessing mitigation potential, and improving greenhouse gas inventories, thereby supporting methane mitigation efforts in China and globally.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: High temporal-resolution microclimate and photovoltaic power dataset for sustainable rooftop design in subtropical humid city
abstract: This paper presents a high resolution microclimate monitoring dataset designed to explore rooftop microclimate responses to different rooftop configurations within a subtropical humid campus setting. The dataset comprises measurements from seven rooftops representing five roofing types: bare roof, bare roof with HVAC units, green roof, PV roof, and PV integrated green roof (PVIGR). The dataset is based on data collected over a one-and-a-half-year period on a university campus in Hong Kong. Microclimate data were collected using various sensors, including temperature and relative-humidity sensors, anemometers, and pyranometers. In addition, the dataset also provides PV power generation data, which supports studies of PV performance and the microclimate impacts of PVIGR designs. Lastly, weather data from a nearby weather station were also included in this dataset for future reference. This dataset addresses a significant gap in existing literature that primarily focuses on conventional roof types and supports the evaluation of alternative rooftop designs under comparable campus-scale conditions. This paper provides a comprehensive description of the rooftop sites, data collection methods, records, and validation processes. Potential applications encompass analyzing microclimate characteristics, supporting validation or benchmarking of computational fluid dynamics models under comparable rooftop conditions, optimizing photovoltaic conversion efficiency, and informing sustainable rooftop design studies.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A knowledge graph and dataset of natural cell-penetrating peptides
abstract: Cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) are short sequences characterized by their ability to translocate across cell membranes without significant damage. This property allows CPPs to function as molecular carriers that facilitate the intracellular delivery of bioactive cargoes. Despite their potential, the discovery of new CPPs relies on time-intensive experimental validation. In silico methodologies offer an alternative; however, existing tabular databases hinder the extraction of relational biological context. Consequently, this data structure may restrict the capacity of computational models to learn biologically meaningful relationships. To address this gap, we structured experimentally validated CPP data into a knowledge graph that explicitly represents this relational biological context. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first knowledge graph that integrates cell-penetrating peptides with their associated cellular uptake mechanisms, cell lines, cargo molecules, and subcellular delivery locations. To establish a functional biological context, we linked the specific uptake mechanisms to regulatory genes and chemical inhibitors. To construct this resource, we collected 5,288 peptide sequences from CPPsite3, processed the annotations through a normalization workflow, and used a graph retrieval-augmented generation method (Graph RAG) for ontology mapping. We mapped annotations such as uptake mechanisms, subcellular locations, cell lines, and cargo types to the Gene Ontology (GO), Cell Line Ontology (CLO), and Chemical Entities of Biological Interest (ChEBI) to ensure interoperability. We serialized the dataset as a Resource Description Framework (RDF) graph and applied the Semanticscience Integrated Ontology (SIO) as an upper-level ontology. The complete dataset and knowledge graph are openly available from Zenodo ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21031596 ); in addition, we provide an interactive, queryable version at https://cppkg.bio2vec.net/ .
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: An objective hourly dataset of typhoon remnant vortices affecting China (1980–2024)
abstract: This study presents an objectively identified and hourly resolved dataset of Typhoon Remnant Vortices (TRVs) affecting China during 1980–2024. Based on the tropical cyclone best-track dataset and ERA5 reanalysis, we developed an automated identification and tracking algorithm to detect and follow TRVs after the dissipation of their parent typhoons. The dataset covers 15°N–55°N, 95°E–140°E, including vortices located within 200 km of the Chinese mainland. A total of 341 TRVs, comprising 11,728 hourly records, were identified and tracked. For each TRV, the dataset provides a more objective and temporally continuous description of TRVs affecting China, including geographic position, 850 hPa stream function, relative vorticity, wind speed, extratropical transition status, and termination category. Climatological analyses reveal pronounced seasonality, with activity concentrated from June to November and peaking in August. Spatial analysis indicates that TRVs predominantly form in low-latitude coastal regions of South China and subsequently propagate inland toward mid–high latitude regions. With long-term coverage, hourly resolution, and standardized dynamical parameters, this dataset provides a consistent and reproducible foundation for TRV climatology, extreme rainfall attribution, and numerical modelling studies.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A standardized collection of human stool and fermented food microbiomes from the Launch Phase of the Microbiota Vault Initiative
abstract: The human gut microbiome and traditional food systems are threatened by lifestyle changes linked with industrialization. The gut microbiome plays a key role in human health, yet publicly available microbiome data lack global representation. Similarly, while fermented foods serve as an important nutritional and cultural resource, the microbial diversity of traditional fermented foods remains relatively unexplored and is equally at risk. Here we present a collection of human gut and fermented food microbiota profiles generated during the Launch Phase of the Microbiota Vault Initiative (MVI). This dataset includes standardized metadata and the 16S rRNA-based amplicon sequencing data from human stool (N = 767) and fermented food samples (N = 157) deposited into the MVI by researchers across Asia, Africa, Europe and Latin America. These data are broadly compatible with other public microbiome datasets and are readily reusable, provided that appropriate attribution is given to the local researchers who maintain ownership of these collections. We anticipate that this resource will facilitate future comparative studies and meta-analyses across diverse human populations and fermented food systems, promoting more representative microbiome research.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: An fMRI dataset of verbalized spontaneous thought with annotated transcripts and self-report trait measures
abstract: Spontaneous thought is pervasive in everyday human cognition, yet datasets capturing its neural dynamics under minimally interrupted conditions remain limited. The current dataset was acquired from a think-aloud functional MRI experiment in which 118 participants continuously verbalized their spontaneous thoughts during 10-minute scanning sessions. The raw MRI data and verbal transcripts with sentence-level timestamps were previously released and analyzed in our prior study examining neural activity associated with thought transitions. Building on that release, we additionally provide preprocessed MRI data, speech transcriptions with word-level timestamps aligned to image acquisition, large language model-generated ratings of transcribed thoughts across emotional and sensory dimensions, and self-report survey measures assessing personality, mental health, and cognitive abilities. Validation analyses demonstrated activation in expected cortical regions associated with speech production and sensory content identified from transcript annotations, agreement between language model and human ratings, and adequate internal consistency of survey measures, supporting the dataset’s overall quality. This dataset enables reuse for investigations of spontaneous thought, speech generation, and individual differences using naturalistic functional MRI data.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A clinical brain MRI dataset of naturally occurring motion artifacts with paired artifact-free images
abstract: Motion artifacts remain a major challenge in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), degrading image quality and compromising diagnostic reliability. Although deep learning–based retrospective correction methods have advanced for brain MRI, their development is constrained by training datasets dominated by synthetic or task-induced motion artifacts, which do not adequately represent real-world clinical motion. We present a brain MRI dataset of naturally occurring motion artifacts derived from routine examinations at a large medical center. The dataset comprises 5,143 paired 2D slices (4.0–6.7 mm slice thickness) derived from 747 paired volumes across 731 patients, and 147 paired 3D volumes (0.67–1.1 mm slice thickness) from 146 patients, spanning T1-weighted, contrast-enhanced T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery sequences. Data were curated through a five-step pipeline comprising deep learning–based prescreening, sequence filtering and acquisition categorization, rigid registration, automated screening, and manual quality control. Each motion-corrupted/artifact-free pair is annotated with objective image quality metrics (PSNR, SSIM, MS-SSIM, and LPIPS) and subjective artifact severity scores, enabling the development and evaluation of clinically applicable motion correction methods.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: The State of Scientific Poster Sharing and Reuse
abstract: Scientific posters are one of the most common forms of scholarly communication and contain early-stage insights with potential to accelerate scientific discovery. We investigated where posters are shared, to what extent their sharing aligns with the FAIR principles, and how commonly they are reused. We identified 86 platforms hosting posters, with many not assigning persistent identifiers. A total of 150k posters are shared as of 2024 on the 43 platforms where we were able to count, which is relatively low. Looking in more detail at posters shared on Zenodo and Figshare, we found that repositories are not always supporting structured metadata critical for poster discovery, like conference information, and that researchers are not providing such metadata even if they are supported. We also observed that while there is some engagement with posters in terms of views and downloads, citing posters is not yet a common practice. These gaps mean valuable early-stage insights are being lost to the scientific community, pointing to a need for clearer guidelines and stronger incentives for FAIR poster sharing and reuse.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Spatially Explicit 1-km Gridded Multi-sector Carbon Emission Dataset for China (2000–2020) with an Extension to 2021–2023
abstract: Integrating carbon mitigation into territorial spatial governance can facilitate the achievement of emission reduction targets. High-resolution datasets with detailed spatiotemporal and sectoral information enable more precise and effective spatial planning and management of carbon emissions. Taking territorial space as the fundamental carrier of carbon emissions, this study constructs- differentiated spatial proxy-factor weighting layers based on the emission characteristics of different sectors. Sectoral emissions are then allocated to the corresponding territorial spaces through an iterative mapping process using these weighting layers. Based on this approach, this study develops a 1 km × 1 km gridded carbon emission dataset for China’s agriculture, mining, industry, transportation, commercial services, and residential sectors at five-year intervals from 2000 to 2020 and extends the dataset annually to 2021–2023 using 2020 as the baseline. This spatially explicit carbon emission dataset integrates comprehensive spatial coverage, sectoral detail, and high spatial resolution, providing a robust foundation for carbon management within territorial spatial governance and supporting the formulation of spatial planning strategies for emission reduction.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Longitudinal Vestibular Schwannoma Dataset with Consensus-based Human-in-the-loop Annotations
abstract: Accurate segmentation of vestibular schwannoma (VS) on MRI is essential for clinical management, yet large-scale, high-quality annotated datasets remain scarce. We present a publicly available longitudinal VS dataset comprising 534 contrast-enhanced T1-weighted scans from 184 patients across 15 or more clinical sites, hosted on The Cancer Imaging Archive. To generate trustworthy annotations at scale, we developed a human-in-the-loop framework combining a bootstrapped 3D nnU-Net model with multi-round consensus-based expert review and correction. This methodology, rather than the model itself, is the primary contribution, offering a reproducible and resource-efficient protocol for annotating complex longitudinal imaging data. The framework reduced annotation time by approximately 37.4% compared to conventional manual approaches. Segmentation accuracy on the internal test set improved across bootstrapping rounds (DSC: 0.9141 to 0.9687), while performance on external datasets remained stable, demonstrating cross-domain robustness. Expert radiological review further revealed nuanced failure cases, underscoring the necessity of human oversight in annotation pipelines for heterogeneous clinical data.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Brain 18F-FDG template using images from a new brain-dedicated positron emission tomography scanner
abstract: 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography ( 18 F-FDG-PET) may be a useful tool as a biomarker of neurodegeneration. However, commercial brain templates may differ substantially from the PET images generated in new scanners in terms of resolution. We aimed to build an 18 F-FDG-PET image template using images acquired in a brain-dedicated PET to enable normalization optimization. A total of 167 patients underwent an 18 F-FDG-PET study on a brain-dedicated PET system. The images were automatically co-registered in Pmod 4.1, followed by iterative deformable registration in ANTs (Advanced Normalization Tools) to build the template. We obtained an 18 F-FDG-PET brain template with 1-mm 3 voxels and a 268 x 268 x 152 matrix to use as a reference for PET image normalization. In addition, we generated a map with 66 regions of interest (ROIs) manually adapted from the Automated Anatomical Labeling (AAL) ROI map for quantification of the normalized images and a mask to exclude extra-parenchymal regions. The development of a brain template with images acquired on the dedicated brain PET is of great utility for application in new scanners with improved resolution.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Genome assembly and gene annotation of Babesia ovis Israeli strain (Piroplasmida: Babesiidae) using PacBio HiFi sequencing
abstract: Babesia ovis is a unicellular parasite of sheep and goats transmitted by the tick Rhipicephalus bursa . B. ovis infection is widespread and can be lethal, and therefore there is need for a deeper understanding of its biology and pathogenesis. There is currently a single genome available for a clinical isolate of B. ovis , and no laboratory strains have been sequenced so far. In this study we have sequenced and assembled the genome of the Israeli laboratory strain of B. ovis using highly accurate long-read sequencing (PacBio HiFi). The resulting assembly has high contiguity, with the four largest contigs comprising 96% of the assembly and representing putative near-complete chromosomes. Annotation identified 3,549 genes, of which 3,046 (85.6%) could be functionally annotated. BUSCO analysis on the annotated genes revealed 95.5%, 98.8% and 100% completeness of the Aconoidasida, Apicomplexa, and Alveolata lineages, respectively. Comparative analysis with other annotated piroplasmida genomes reveals the vast majority of predicted genes clustered in orthogroups. The availability of a high-quality genome assembly for a tractable laboratory strain could prove impactful in unlocking more basic and applied research avenues to be pursued for this important parasite system.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Genome-wide DNA methylation profiling of the zebrafish forebrain
abstract: The zebrafish forebrain is a central hub for cognitive and social behaviors, yet a comprehensive, region-specific DNA methylation reference for this tissue is not available. To address this gap, we generated a genome-wide methylation map of the adult zebrafish forebrain using Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) long-read sequencing. Forebrains from six individuals were profiled, enabling direct detection of multiple DNA base modifications at single-base resolution. The resulting dataset includes CpG-associated 5-methylcytosine (5 mC) and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5 hmC), as well as non-CpG 5 mC and candidate N6-methyladenine (6 mA) signals, with 96.8% genome coverage. CpG methylation was widespread, with 64.2% of CpG sites classified as highly 5 mC-modified. In contrast, 5 hmC and non-CpG methylation were markedly less abundant, and 6 mA was detected at very low levels and showed poor reproducibility across replicates. CpG islands showed a bimodal distribution of methylation, promoter regions displayed elevated variability compared to gene bodies, and CC-context non-CpG methylation exhibited significant strand asymmetry. This resource provides a high-resolution epigenomic baseline for the adult zebrafish forebrain.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A chromosome-level genome assembly of the Ornamental Amaranth (Amaranthus caudatus)
abstract: Amaranthus caudatus L. is an ornamental and pseudocereal species of the Amaranthus genus, notable for its striking pendulous panicles and vibrant crimson coloration. Despite its distinctive morphology and economic value, its genome has remained uncharacterized. Here, we present a high-quality chromosome-scale genome assembly of A. caudatus totaling 426.72 Mb, with 93.68% of sequences anchored onto 16 chromosomes. The assembly comprises contigs with an N50 of 12.64 Mb. The genome contains 26,343 predicted protein-coding genes, 95% of which were functionally annotated. This high-quality genome provides a valuable resource for elucidating the genetic basis of its ornamental traits, pigment biosynthesis, and domestication.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Strengthening Rare Disease Data Readiness: a semantic approach to cross-registry interoperability
abstract: Rare diseases affect an estimated 446 million people worldwide, yet reliable epidemiological data are scarce due to insufficient data sources and lack of standardization. The German National Registry for Rare Diseases (NARSE) aims to establish a comprehensive epidemiological data basis and enable data availability for research. However, limited interoperability between clinical and epidemiological data sources restricts secondary use and cross-registry research. This study assesses the semantic interoperability between NARSE and two core data sets: the German Medical Informatics Initiative (MII) core data set and the European Rare Disease Registry Infrastructure (ERDRI) core data set. Using a formal consensus process, mapping categories (exactMatch, closeMatch, broadMatch, narrowMatch, relatedMatch) were defined, analyzed, and evaluated for information loss using a heuristic scale. Most NARSE elements aligned with the MII core data set, while mapping to the ERDRI core data set revealed more challenges due to undefined value sets and inconsistent coding systems. These findings highlight the importance of consistent application of coding standards to safeguard information value and improve interoperability in rare disease research.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A genus-labeled dataset of individual trees outside forests in Baden-Württemberg, Germany
abstract: Detailed data on individual trees growing outside forests (TOF) are essential for arboriculture, biodiversity assessment, ecosystem services assessment, climate adaptation, and environmental health research. However, existing datasets are often incomplete and seldom provide taxonomic information beyond publicly managed trees in cities of Germany and other countries where maintaining a tree cadaster is a legal requirement. Here, we present for the first time a statewide dataset of individual TOF in the state of Baden-Württemberg, Germany, including tree locations, crown geometry, height, and genus-level labels. We mapped trees from high-resolution multi-spectral aerial imagery and height data using deep learning, with terrestrial LiDAR surveys used to create training labels within the URBORETUM project. The released dataset includes ten genus-level classes, including the aggregate categories “Other Deciduous” and “Coniferous” where assignment from aerial imagery is uncertain. The final ten-class genus model achieved a mean average precision (mAP) of 0.382 at an intersection-over-union (IoU) threshold of 0.5 (mAP@0.5) and a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.627 for taxonomic class assignment, while a separately trained one-class tree detector achieved an mAP@0.5 of 0.647, indicating stronger reliability for crown detection than for taxonomic classification. The final inventory contains 16.3 million predicted trees across the mapped non-forest domain of Baden-Württemberg. Beyond providing a statewide dataset, this work offers a scalable vision and operational blueprint for an evolving tree inventory that can be systematically improved over time through better imagery, richer local reference data, and targeted retraining.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A haplotype-resolved chromosome-scale genome assembly of the triploid Boechera sierraensis (Brassicaceae)
abstract: Boechera sierraensis is a recently described apomictic triploid species (Brassicaceae) endemic to the high-elevation granitic slopes of the Sierra Nevada, USA. It displays extraordinary tolerance to heat, drought, and high light stress, making it an important emerging model for understanding plant adaptation to extreme alpine environments and rapid climatic change. Despite its physiological and ecological significance, no genomic resources have been available for this taxon, limiting investigation into the genetic basis of its stress resilience, apomictic reproduction, and complex hybrid origin involving B. lemmonii , B. paupercula , and B. retrofracta . To address these gaps, we generated a haplotype-resolved, chromosome-scale assembly of the B. sierraensis genome (2n = 3x = 22) using a combination of long-read and short-read sequencing. The assembly fully phased the three parental subgenomes, yielding assembled sizes of 210.8 Mb, 198.6 Mb, and 213.2 Mb. Assembly contiguity was high, with scaffold N50 values of 28.2–31.1 Mb, and BUSCO completeness reached 99.5–99.8% across haplotypes. The phased nature of the assembly preserves subgenome-specific architectural features, including centromeric and pericentromeric regions, enabling comparative analyses of repeat composition and centromere-associated sequences. Repetitive elements constitute a substantial fraction of each subgenome and are dominated by long terminal repeat (LTR) retrotransposons, particularly Gypsy and Copia families. Using PacBio Iso-Seq and Illumina RNA-seq, we annotated 79,345 protein-coding genes across the three subgenomes, the majority of which received functional assignments through multiple annotation frameworks. This study provides a haplotype-resolved genomic resource for B. sierraensis , which can support studies of apomixis, hybrid triploidy, and the genetic basis of stress tolerance in this alpine species.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A single-cell RNA-seq dataset characterizing cellular diversity in healthy equine skin
abstract: The skin serves as the primary barrier tissue in horses and is frequently affected by immune-mediated dermatological conditions, most notably insect bite hypersensitivity (IBH). Yet, the cellular composition and transcriptional landscape of normal equine skin have never been characterized at single-cell resolution. Here, we present a single-cell RNA sequencing dataset of healthy equine skin comprising 85,574 high-quality transcriptomes from two horses, with one skin biopsy collected from each horse, divided into two portions for independent processing via manual or automated tissue dissociation. The dataset resolved 22 transcriptionally distinct cell populations, encompassing keratinocyte subpopulations that reflect discrete epidermal differentiation states, adnexal epithelial lineages, stromal and vascular compartments, and resident immune cell types. Cell-type identities are supported by marker gene expression, KEGG pathway enrichment analysis, and functional module scoring. This dataset constitutes the first single-cell transcriptomic reference of normal equine skin, enabling investigations into equine dermatological diseases, wound healing, immune responses and comparative skin biology.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: 16S rRNA Datasets of Gut Microbiota in Stent-Based Diverting Technique and Ileostomy from A Prospective, Open-Label, Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: Accumulating evidence implicates gut dysbiosis in postoperative complications and delayed intestinal recovery after rectal cancer surgery. Although stent-based diverting technique (SDT) and conventional ileostomy exert divergent impacts on gut microbial balance, high-quality comparative microbiome data from randomized trials are lacking. We report a 16S rRNA amplicon dataset from 80 patients randomized to SDT (n = 37) or ileostomy (n = 43), with fecal samples collected preoperatively and on postoperative day 90.
