We characterized phylum-level taxonomic composition, α-diversity and intergroup β-diversity across four subgroups, and identified discriminatory taxa via LEfSe. Functional prediction detected differential metabolic pathways after surgery. We additionally performed correlation analyses to link clinical covariates with microbial signatures. This public dataset enables independent reprocessing and cross-study comparisons, facilitating exploration of diversion-strategy-specific microbial remodeling and validation of SDT’s gut microbiota-preserving capacity.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Time series data with and without anomalies from a continuous distillation plant
abstract: Reliable detection of process anomalies remains a challenge in industrial chemical plants. The ability of machine learning (ML) to recognize patterns has triggered numerous research efforts to apply ML to anomaly detection (AD). Simulation-based benchmarks, such as the Tennessee Eastman process, are widely used to develop and train AD methods. Well-annotated real-world process data, which are crucial for meaningful research advancements, are lacking due to industry-wide proprietary limitations. To overcome this issue, we present an openly accessible dataset of time series generated from an industry-like continuous distillation mini-plant under constant operating conditions. The data generated have different complexities: water runs, a heteroazeotropic separation of n-butanol–water, and a reactive process to produce a fuel additive. Chemical systems, plant setup, and anomalies (whether encountered or manually induced) are described alongside the process data. The complete dataset, including sensor and actuator data, annotations marking anomalies, and other metadata, is available in open access via an online Zenodo repository. It serves as training and testing data for ML-based AD and other data-driven applications.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: An EEG dataset for multi-state memory processing in an associative word-pair task
abstract: Memory processing unfolds across successive cognitive states rather than within a single isolated phase, making multi-state neural recordings important for characterizing state-dependent brain dynamics. Here, we present an open-access electroencephalography (EEG) dataset from 41 participants collected during a structured associative word-pair memory protocol that included questionnaires, encoding, retrieval, re-encoding, and interleaved resting-state (RS) periods. The data include 28-channel EEG, 4-channel electrooculography, participant-level questionnaire measures, and trial-level behavioral annotations, including retrieval responses, reaction times, and subjective difficulty ratings. By combining interleaved RS and task phases within a single protocol, this dataset enables investigations of neural dynamics across successive cognitive states within a common experimental framework. It also supports analyses of behavior-linked variability at the trial level and may facilitate studies of individual differences in memory-related cognition.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: High-frequency eDNA metabarcoding survey data of coastal fish across the Japanese Archipelago
abstract: The Japanese archipelago, spanning over 3,000 km from subarctic to subtropical zones (approximately 24°N to 45°N), hosts a diverse array of coastal fish communities shaped by pronounced latitudinal gradients. Here, we present a high-frequency environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding dataset of coastal fishes collected across the archipelago. Using the MiFish primer set targeting a hypervariable region of the mitochondrial 12S rRNA gene, we conducted surveys at 211 sites, yielding 690 samples collected through one-time (annual), monthly, and biweekly sampling schemes. The inclusion of high-frequency sampling enabled the detection of fine-scale temporal variations in fish community composition. From January 2018 to March 2019, eDNA samples were collected along with metadata on geographic and environmental variables, including coastal structure, wave height, tide, currents, and water temperature. The resulting dataset comprises fish eDNA records for 1,477 species across 171 families. This dataset offers a valuable resource for investigating fish community structure, temporal dynamics, and biodiversity in the coastal ecosystems of the Japanese archipelago, supporting a range of applications in ecology, conservation, and eDNA-based research.

title: A multimodal synthetic 3D point cloud dataset of shoe uppers for robotic processing boundary segmentation
abstract: Robotic processing of shoe uppers requires accurate segmentation of thin processing boundaries in 3D point clouds. However, acquiring and annotating large collections of real-world scans is costly. We present a multimodal synthetic 3D point cloud dataset of shoe uppers for robotic processing boundary segmentation. The dataset contains 1,067 samples, including 1,000 synthetic point clouds and 67 real-world test scans for independent evaluation. The synthetic data generation pipeline includes texture and appearance augmentation, region-aware geometric deformation, and sensor degradation simulation. Both branches provide three-dimensional coordinates, RGB attributes, and pointwise binary processing boundary labels. The synthetic branch additionally includes panel identifiers, while the real-world labels were manually refined. Technical validation with standard point cloud segmentation backbones assesses dataset usability under a controlled synthetic-to-real evaluation protocol. The released point clouds form a complete, directly usable dataset. The accompanying code and assets support regeneration and adaptation of synthetic subsets.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Microscopic images of pollen germination under natural heat stress in four cucurbit species
abstract: We present a microscopy image dataset of pollen germination and tube growth from melon, watermelon, cucumber, and pumpkin cultivated under naturally occurring heat stress conditions. Beyond supporting computer vision research, the dataset is linked to two agronomic assays involving a diverse panel of cultivars, providing a phenotyping resource for studying pollen viability responses to warm cultivation conditions across cucurbit germplasm. The dataset comprises 3089 microscopy images accompanied by experimental metadata. A curated subset of 122 images includes instance-level annotations in COCO format distinguishing germinated grains, non-germinated grains, and pollen tubes, while a complementary subset of 639 images provides expert visual scores describing pollen abundance, germination level, and tube development. Additionally, 129 images are flagged for visual noise. Technical validation was performed by training and evaluating several semantic segmentation models on the annotated subset, demonstrating that the annotations support reliable automated pollen segmentation. The dataset provides a benchmark for developing and validating automated pollen analysis methodologies while supporting future studies on pollen viability under naturally occurring high-temperature conditions.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Curated Dataset for Chemical Characterization of Heated Tobacco Product Aerosol
abstract: We addressed the task of chemical characterization of the aerosol emitted by heated tobacco products (HTPs) and of the smoke emitted by conventional/commercial cigarettes, usually adopted as a reference. Emphasis was placed on quantifying constituents for enabling the identification of novel compounds through targeted and untargeted analyses, and the evaluation of reductions in toxicant exposure under standardized smoking regimens. We curated and harmonized experimental data across studies, addressing methodological inconsistencies in puffing protocols, analytical approaches, reporting formats, and treatment of detection limits. The dataset, named HTP-AeroChem, covers data from both industry-funded and independent investigations, offering an aggregated resource for critical comparison of experimental quality, reproducibility, and data reliability. By consolidating and standardizing findings, this work provides a valuable resource to support regulatory assessments and risk evaluations of HTPs in comparison to combustible cigarettes.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Global compilation of in situ particulate organic carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus concentrations in coastal and open ocean waters
abstract: We present a global compilation of in situ marine particulate organic carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus concentrations (POC, PON, and POP, respectively), from multiple sources to provide one of the most comprehensive collections of marine particulate organic matter (POM) to date. The dataset includes 155137 measurements (70586 POC, 69290 PON, and 15261 POP) from 25944 independent stations, more than doubling the number of previously available observations. Observations span more than three decades (1988–2025) and cover the global ocean from the surface to 6009 m depth. Notably, 52% of stations are located in shallow, coastal waters (<200 m bottom depth), enhancing coverage of productive nearshore regions and improving representation of dynamic coastal biogeochemistry. To address methodological heterogeneity among the compiled datasets, detailed metadata describing sampling strategies, filtration protocols, filter types, and analytical techniques were systematically assembled for each measurement whenever available. This dataset provides a resource for quantifying the spatial and temporal variability of POM distributions, and the elemental stoichiometry of marine particles, supporting biogeochemical modeling efforts. The dataset will also enable the development and validation of both bio-optical models and satellite-derived estimates of POM, including applications to the Sentinel-3 and the Plankton, Aerosol, Cloud, ocean Ecosystem (PACE) missions.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: PORTIA: A Large-Scale Port Acoustic Dataset with AIS-Grounded Annotations for AI-Based Vessel Monitoring
abstract: Monitoring underwater anthropogenic noise in busy commercial ports is critical for marine spatial planning, yet the development of AI-based tools is often limited by the scarcity of large-scale, annotated acoustic datasets from realistic high-traffic environments. We present PORTIA, a passive acoustic dataset collected over a 26-day campaign in the Port of Valencia, Spain. It comprises 260,932 three-second audio windows paired with synchronized Automatic Identification System (AIS) metadata. To facilitate direct reuse, we provide three task-oriented benchmarks: a Binary Detection subset (36,148 samples), a Single-Vessel Classification subset (39,125 samples), and a Multi-Label Monitoring subset (34,996 samples) explicitly designed to handle concurrent acoustic scenes and source proximity. All benchmarks were constructed using Maritime Mobile Service Identity (MMSI)-aware splitting to prevent identity leakage across partitions and utilized stratified sampling to preserve representative vessel-class distributions while remaining manageable for research. PORTIA serves as a realistic benchmark for vessel detection, typological classification, and proximity estimation in dense Mediterranean port soundscapes.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A multi-level dataset of China’s energy-transition policies from national to prefecture levels over 2000–2024
abstract: China’s energy transition has generated a vast and heterogeneous body of policy documents across multiple administrative levels. Existing datasets, however, remain largely confined to national-level analyses or single-domain applications and rely predominantly on proxy variables or keyword-frequency methods that may inadequately capture the substantive content of policy texts. To address this gap, this study constructs a title-anchored, multi-level inventory of China’s energy-transition policies spanning 2000 to 2024, based on an exact-match search of seven selected energy-transition-related terms in official policy titles, yielding 7,295 policy texts retrieved from PKULaw across national, provincial, and prefecture-level administrative tiers. Each policy is annotated with 14 structured metadata fields and classified according to a four-category objective typology with 16 sub-objectives and a three-category instrument typology with 9 subcategories. Multi-label classification allows each policy to carry multiple objectives and instruments simultaneously. The dataset is designed to support empirical research on policy mix composition, multi-level governance, and the drivers of energy transition outcomes at regional and firm levels.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A multi-phase shaking table dataset of reinforced concrete frames retrofitted with a timber–aluminium exoskeleton
abstract: A significant portion of the existing reinforced concrete (RC) building stock in Europe was designed according to outdated standards and is vulnerable both to earthquake damage and to poor energy performance. Retrofit solutions that integrate structural strengthening with envelope upgrading have therefore emerged as a promising strategy to address safety and decarbonisation objectives simultaneously. Within this context, the EU-funded Horizon Europe project Engineering Research Infrastructures for European Synergies (ERIES) supported the REsilient and SUstainable envelope for vulnerable buildings in seisMic affected areas at the time of climatE crisis (RESUME) project, which investigated the seismic response of RC frames strengthened with a hybrid timber–aluminium exoskeleton system incorporating prefabricated façade panels for thermal upgrading. To investigate seismic vulnerability, two geometrically scaled (1:3) two-storey RC frame specimens representative of non-ductile typologies were constructed and tested on a shaking table at the Institute of Earthquake Engineering and Engineering Seismology (IZIIS), North Macedonia. The experimental campaign comprised 66 shaking table tests conducted in three phases. The dataset includes synchronised time-history measurements of accelerations, displacements and strains, together with input ground motions and detailed metadata describing geometry, materials, instrumentation and testing sequence. The data support validation of numerical models and comparative assessment of structural retrofit configurations within an integrated retrofit framework.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A century-long provincial dataset of agricultural land use structure in China (1924–2024)
abstract: Long-term, large-scale data on agricultural land use are essential for understanding land-use transitions and human-environment interactions, yet century-scale, provincial-level datasets are lacking for China. To fill this gap, we constructed a provincial dataset of agricultural land use structure in China covering the period 1924–2024. The dataset integrates multi-source historical materials, including official statistics, historical archives, remote-sensing products, and international reconstruction databases. A consistent land classification system was defined (cropland, garden land, forest land, grassland, aquaculture and fishing water surface, facility agricultural land), and a backward anchoring reconstruction method was applied to fill early-period data gaps. The dataset provides annual areas (in 10 3 ha) for six agricultural land types across 31 provincial units. It can be used for studying long-term agricultural transitions, validating land-use models, and supporting sustainable land-use policy analysis. The dataset is available for peer review via a temporary link.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Multimodal 3D X-ray Topotomography Dataset of Slip Activity and Transmission in Ti-7Al
abstract: Plastic deformation in polycrystalline metals is usually primarily accommodated through dislocation glide, which often organizes into discrete slip bands. The evolution of plasticity is governed by the interactions of these dislocation structures with one another, as well as with grain boundaries and other microstructural interfaces or features. Traditional observations of slip bands are largely limited to free surfaces, constraining our understanding of their three-dimensional behavior within the bulk. The X-ray topotomography and diffraction contrast tomography (DCT) datasets presented here enable direct visualization of the three-dimensional morphology of slip bands in relation to the surrounding grain structure. These data reveal, for instance, in the investigated titanium alloy that slip transmission across grain boundaries is more prevalent at free surfaces, while in the bulk, transmission events are often driven by geometrically constrained regions, such as triple junctions, where elevated local stress heterogeneity promotes dislocation activity across interfaces. This dataset is shared with the community to facilitate broader access to and analysis of correlated 3D deformation and microstructure alloy datasets, which are expected to become increasingly prevalent in the near future.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: SEA-Driven OdorNet: A Large-Scale Standardized Molecular Olfactory Dataset Based on a Hybrid Semantic Taxonomy
abstract: The development of machine olfaction (digitization of odor) is currently hindered by data scarcity and the lack of standardization in descriptive labels. Datasets integration faces the challenges of descriptor-level conflicts, including cross-source labeling inconsistencies, synonym redundancy, skewed distributions, etc. To address the semantic confusion inherent in multi-source data, we developed a SEA (Statistical co-occurrence, Expert correction, and AI alignment) taxonomy framework that integrates statistical co-occurrence analysis, expert knowledge (perfumery taxonomy), and AI-assisted semantic alignment based on the definitions from both encyclopedia and odor-related scientific literatures. A unified-labeled olfactory dataset, namely OdorNet, is further presented, which is by far the largest molecule dataset with unified olfactory labels comprising over 20,000 entries and 9,000 unique molecules originated from academic literatures (1960–2021) and open databases. This process consolidates cluttered labels into a hierarchical system with the most extensively effective vocabulary coverage in the field to date. Technical validation demonstrates that a baseline model on OdorNet achieves a Macro F1 score of 0.42, substantially higher than the scores obtained on commonly used odor datasets and on OdorNet itself using the same model but without the SEA-based label taxonomy. This indicates that OdorNet allows to better capture learnable structure-odor relationships, laying a solid fundamental for digital odor editing and human-computer interaction.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Carneiro’s global dataset of cultural traits in ethnographic and historical societies: a digital edition
abstract: The late Robert L. Carneiro was a prominent anthropologist who devoted his life to the study of political evolution and the evolution of complex societies. In the 1960s and 1970s, he and his colleagues created a cross-cultural dataset for their Scale Analysis project, collecting ethnographic and historical data on hundreds of cultural traits in more than a hundred societies worldwide. Although Carneiro presented the results of the project in several papers, the dataset itself has not yet been published. Here we present a digital version of two editions of the dataset, based on Carneiro’s documentation stored in the archives of the American Museum of Natural History. The 4th edition contains 127 societies and 354 cultural traits, and the 6th edition features 74 societies and 618 traits. Both represent unique sets of coded cross-cultural information that can be used as a comparative source to other cross-cultural datasets, as a starting point for one’s own collection of cross-cultural data, and for quantitative testing of cultural evolutionary hypotheses.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Satellite-based Four-decade High-resolution Quasi-global Mesoscale Convective Systems Database
abstract: Mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) are fundamental to the global energy and water cycles and account for a large fraction of extreme weather events. Yet the lack of a temporally consistent, long-term observational record has hindered robust quantification of their variability. Here, we construct the longest-to-date global MCS database (1985–2024) by applying a widely used object-based tracking algorithm to two high-resolution satellite infrared brightness temperature datasets. To enhance temporal homogeneity, we implement a latitude-stratified, seasonally varying adjustment to reduce discrepancies between the datasets. The resulting database provides quasi-global (60°S–60°N), object-based records of MCS frequency, life cycle, size, intensity, and associated precipitation characteristics. Evaluation of key MCS features, comparisons with alternative tracking methods, and the use of flexible thresholds that support user-defined applications demonstrate the robustness of the tracking framework and long-term record. We anticipate that this extended global MCS database will facilitate the evaluation of MCS simulations and predictions, enable the detection of climate-driven changes in organized convection, and support assessments of their climatic impacts and associated weather risks.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A dataset on aging and characterization of Samsung INR21700-50E lithium-ion cells
abstract: This manuscript presents a data descriptor for a comprehensive lithium-ion battery dataset designed to support the development of rapid diagnostic protocols for estimating cell capacity. The dataset includes controlled aging experiments and extensive multimodal characterization of Samsung INR21700-50E lithium-ion cells. A total of 160 brand-new cells were aged under designed charge and discharge strategies at room temperature to generate a representative distribution of capacity values. Throughout the aging process, time-resolved voltage and current measurements were recorded, along with derived quantities such as power, charge, and energy. Capacity measurements were performed both prior to and following aging. After aging, the cells underwent further characterization using various diagnostic techniques, including a galvanostatic low-rate (C/48) cycle, static and dynamic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, electrochemical noise analysis, and short- and long-term current interruption tests.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Near telomere-to-telomere and gap-free reference genome assembly of the WuLi carp (Cyprinus carpio var. Quanzhounensis)
abstract: Cyprinus carpio var. Quanzhounensis (WuLi carp), a native fish from Quanzhou, Guangxi, China, is well-adapted to mountainous rice-fish farming systems, yet genomic studies on the strain remain scarce. This study presents the first near telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome and gapless assembly of C. carpio var. Quanzhounensis , generated using PacBio HiFi sequencing, ONT ultra-long reads, and Hi-C data. The final assembly, spanning 1.54 Gb across 68 contigs, features a contig N50 of 29.52 Mb, with 99.37% of sequences anchored to 50 chromosomes. A total of 49,781 protein-coding genes were annotated, and transposable elements account for 42.96% of the genome. The high-quality assembly provides a valuable genomic resource for conservation, germplasm evaluation, and future comparative studies of WuLi carp and related cyprinid fishes.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Global high-Resolution Friction Surface Dataset
abstract: Global physical accessibility analysis requires friction surfaces that are spatially detailed, transparent, reusable, and suitable for both on-network and off-network movement. We introduce the Global high-Resolution Updatable Friction Surface (GRUFS), a pair of global 30 m raster datasets representing movement cost in minutes per meter. GRUFS Foot models walking movement on roads, paths, ferries, and off-road terrain, while GRUFS Mixed models driving speeds on roads and walking movement off-road. The surfaces are generated from publicly available inputs, including OpenStreetMap transport and water features, GLAD land cover, FABDEM elevation, Copernicus GLO-30 elevation patches, and GAUL-derived country membership for road-speed assignment. The dataset is distributed as scaled integer raster surfaces with accompanying lookup tables, supporting inputs, production code, and validation materials. GRUFS is designed for accessibility analysis, facility catchment estimation, service coverage assessment, policy targeting, and scenario testing, particularly in data-scarce settings where consistent, high-resolution travel-time inputs are needed. The production workflow is designed to support annual, versioned releases as source transport and environmental data are updated, subject to available maintenance resources.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Global Major Water Transfer Projects Dataset
abstract: Water transfer projects (WTPs) profoundly alter water availability and have far-reaching effects on the environments, economies, and sustainable development in water donor and recipient regions, and along water conveyance corridors. Despite their growing importance, global assessments of WTPs remain constrained by fragmented records, inconsistent attribute definitions, and limited spatial representations of project components. By integrating multi-source WTPs reports and auxiliary geospatial data, we developed spatially explicit datasets that provied a global inventory of major water transfer projects (MWTPs). Organized within a standardized data structure, these datasets document the project characteristics, geospatial details, and functional attributes of 435 MWTPs, alongside spatial layers for water transfer routes, intake locations, and project-associated influence regions. By linking engineering attributes with point–line–polygon spatial features, the database supports a consistent comparison of major water transfer systems across regions. The dataset can provide unified information for global and regional hydrological cycle simulations, water environmental impact assessments, and sustainable water resource management practices.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A dataset of media multitasking, digital media use, and multifaceted cognitive control in Chinese adults
abstract: Media multitasking is pervasive in contemporary digital life, yet its association with cognitive control remains inconsistent across studies, partly owing to heterogeneous measurement of digital behaviors and limited task coverage. Here we present an open behavioral and psychometric dataset linking media multitasking, digital media use, and multifaceted cognitive control in Chinese adults. Data were collected online via the Naodao platform. Of 560 recruited participants, 492 were retained after questionnaire quality control; 280 of these contributed valid data to at least one behavioral task, and 220 completed all eight. Self-report measures cover media-multitasking habits, short-video, live-streaming, and gaming use and experience, and trait reinforcement sensitivity. Cognitive control was assessed with eight computerized tasks spanning cognitive-control capacity, working memory, cognitive flexibility, inhibitory control, conflict processing, and spatial attention. The repository provides raw questionnaire responses, trial-level behavioral logs, processed metrics, experimental materials, a codebook, and analysis code, supporting secondary analyses of cross-task cognitive profiles and of individual differences in cognitive control in the context of digital media use.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: UWB Channel Measurements and 3D Environmental Model for Wireless Channel Analysis in a Mine Tunnel
abstract: This study provides a multimodal dataset for underground mine tunnels to support the analysis and modeling of radio propagation for communication, sensing, and localization applications. Specifically, the dataset focuses on highly irregular mine-tunnel geometries where waveguide-like behavior is strongly influenced by rough surfaces, changes in cross-section, and discontinuities that cause strong multipath propagation and fading. The released dataset comprises three complementary parts designed to enable measurement-driven and simulation-driven research. First, a Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR)-derived 3D point cloud of the mine tunnel is provided, together with simplified polygon mesh models to support digital-twin reconstruction and deterministic simulation. Second, a Ultra-Wideband (UWB) measurement dataset includes complex Channel Impulse Response (CIR) samples and receiver-reported metrics collected at accurately defined transmitter and receiver locations, enabling studies of large-scale attenuation, temporal dispersion, multipath structure, and ranging-related performance. Third, ray-tracing simulation records are released, including the simulation setup based on the LiDAR-derived meshes, material and propagation parameters, and outputs containing link-level path loss and ray-level information to interpret dominant propagation mechanisms. This dataset aims to facilitate reproducible calibration and validation workflows that couple geometry, CIR measurements, and deterministic predictions, which are difficult to establish using measurements or simulations alone.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: SARice: A 10 m rice extent and cropping-frequency dataset for South Asia derived from Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 time series
abstract: Rice is a staple crop for more than one billion people in South Asia, where cultivation ranges from single- to triple-cropping under diverse monsoon-driven agroecosystems. However, spatially explicit and high-resolution information on rice extent and cropping frequency remains limited at the regional scale. We present SARice, a 10 m-resolution dataset of rice extent and cropping frequency across South Asia for 2020–2021. The dataset was generated using multi-temporal Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery analysed through a phenology expert-based unsupervised classification to distinguish rice from non-rice areas and identify cropping frequency based on temporal spectral signatures. The maps estimate a total rice extent of 47.35 million ha, comprising 36.04, 11.14 and 0.17 million ha under single-, double-, and triple-cropping systems, respectively. Pixel-level validation using 20,073 reference points yielded 96.15% pooled overall accuracy (country range: 93.75–97.84%), with F1-scores of 0.97 (rice) and 0.96 (non-rice). Rice harvested area estimates show an approximate 7% underestimation relative to official agricultural statistics. SARice is publicly available to support food security assessments, agricultural monitoring, and climate-related research.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A 30-m resolution dataset of forest cover dynamics in China from 1990 to 2020
abstract: Forests are a fundamental component of terrestrial ecosystems and play a crucial role in the global carbon cycle and climate regulation. China, accounting for approximately 5% of the world’s forest area, has experienced substantial forest expansion in recent decades. However, high-accuracy long-term forest cover datasets with consistent mapping standards remain limited. In this study, we produced a 30 m resolution forest cover dataset (FCD30) for China from 1990 to 2020 at 5-year intervals using Landsat time-series imagery and a weakly supervised deep learning classification method. An iterative label refinement strategy was applied to improve the reliability of historical samples. Multi-temporal classification results were further integrated to enhance the robustness and temporal consistency of the final maps. The resulting FCD30 achieved high classification accuracy (overall accuracy >90%) and showed strong agreement with the National Forest Inventory (NFI) statistics. Our results indicate a net forest gain of 97.66 million hectares over the past 30 years. This study provides an important data foundation for understanding China’s forest dynamics and supports applications in carbon accounting, ecosystem assessment, and sustainable forest management.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A high-quality chromosome-level genome assembly and annotation of a brown Upland cotton ‘Zhongmiansuo 81’
abstract: Brown cotton, a naturally pigmented variety, predates conventional white cotton, with roots in ancient American civilizations and early cultivation in China. Its genetic diversity is significant in agricultural history. By eliminating chemical dyeing, brown cotton reduces environmental pollution and is recognized for its skin-friendly, breathable, and anti-static properties. Additionally, it exhibits natural antibacterial effects, offers antioxidant benefits, and provides UV protection, making it a sustainable choice for textiles. This study presents a comprehensive chromosome-level genome assembly and annotation for brown cotton, resulting in a highly contiguous genome of 2.30 Gb. Notably, the assembly features a scaffold N50 value of 108.19 Mb, indicating a significant advancement in genome resolution and continuity. A total of 152 contigs were successfully anchored to 26 pseudochromosomes, resulting in a contig N50 of 108.07 Mb. The genome assembly achieved an annotation of 97.43% for the 79,272 protein-coding genes identified, while repetitive sequences account for 80.34% of the genome composition. Furthermore, the annotation includes 318 miRNAs, 2,653 tRNAs, 17,854 rRNAs, and 301 snRNAs. The chromosome-scale genome offers critical insights that enhance comparative genomic analyses within the Malvaceae family. This advancement is poised to expedite genome-guided breeding efforts and improve germplasm development in brown cotton.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A mitogenome dataset of Mesenchytraeus (Annelida, Enchytraeidae)
abstract: Mitogenomes provide valuable genomic resources for investigating the evolutionary history, phylogenetic relationships, and speciation, yet many taxonomic groups remain underrepresented in available mitogenomic datasets. Mesenchytraeus are important enchytraeid decomposers in terrestrial ecosystems but still poorly studied, with no mitogenome reported to date. The Changbai Mountain represents a natural laboratory for Mesenchytraeus , harboring exceptionally high diversity and endemism, with 19 recorded species (ca. 18% of the global total), 95% of which are endemic. Here, we present the first mitogenome dataset of Mesenchytraeus , comprising 14 individuals of 13 species, covering 68% of recorded species in this region. All mitogenomes were generated using a standardized workflow for sequencing, assembly, and annotation, resulting in complete circular genomes of 14,842–15,077 bp, containing the typical 37 genes and all encoded on the plus strand. Putative control regions located between ATP6 and tRNA-Arg across all specimens, representing a novel genomic feature in annelids. This dataset provides fundamental resource for further studies on phylogenetics, phylogeography, and population genetics, and contributes to broader investigations of evolution in Annelida.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Annual Migration Flow Estimates by Sex between all Countries since 1960
abstract: Global migration data are essential for understanding how human mobility shapes demographic, economic, social, and political dynamics worldwide. While migrant stock estimates remain a key resource, many research and policy applications benefit from data on migration flows, given their greater sensitivity to economic, political, and other changes. Inferring flows from stocks is not trivial, especially at a temporal resolution finer than the multi-year intervals of the stock data, which can be too coarse to capture migration responses to short-term events. Here, we present Flow , a global dataset of bilateral migration flows, consistent with available migrant stock data, covering 1960–2024 at annual resolution. We first estimate multi-year flows by linking stock-derived variables to recent global flow observations, and applying the model to harmonised historical data. We then downscale the results to annual resolution by aligning them with country-level annual net migration. While subject to limitations and uncertainties inherent to this spatial and temporal scale, Flow estimates provide a consistent and comprehensive resource for historical and forward-looking migration research, model development, and policy analysis, combining global coverage with annual resolution across more than six decades.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Chromosome-level haplotype-resolved genome assembly of the traditional Chinese medicinal plant Mu-Tou-Hui (Patrinia heterophylla)
abstract: Patrinia heterophylla (“Mu-Tou-Hui”) is a perennial herb valued in traditional Chinese medicine, as well as for its edible and ornamental properties. In this study, we present the first chromosome-scale, haplotype-resolved genome assembly of P. heterophylla , constructed by integrating PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing with Hi-C technology. The assembly consists of two haplotypes with sizes of 554.92 Mb (haplotype A) and 555.88 Mb (haplotype B). In total, 28,306 (26,260 functionally annotated) and 28,576 (26,516 functionally annotated) protein-coding genes were annotated in haplotypes A and B, respectively. Furthermore, we annotated 334.17 Mb of repetitive elements and 3,224 non-coding RNAs in haplotype A, compared to 347.57 Mb and 3,328 in haplotype B. Comparative analysis between haplotypes revealed 3,008,122 SNPs, 414,102 insertions, and 335,115 deletions. Additionally, haplotype A exhibited expansion and contraction in 331 and 274 gene families, respectively. This superior genomic resource is expected to facilitate future genetic investigations and biotechnological applications of P. heterophylla in medicine, food production, and horticulture.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Near telomere-to-telomere, chromosome-level haplotype-resolved genome assemblies of the dikaryotic edible mushroom Stropharia rugosoannulata
abstract: Stropharia rugosoannulata , a highly nutritious edible mushroom with strong lignocellulose-degrading capabilities, shows remarkable potential in agricultural waste valorization and sustainable food production. In this study, we performed PacBio HiFi sequencing, ONT ultra-long sequencing, and Hi-C sequencing on the dikaryotic strain SR18, and assembled two gap-free, chromosome-level haplotype genomes. The sizes of the two haplotypes were 47.59 Mb (SR_A) and 48.46 Mb (SR_B), respectively. Each haplotype comprised 13 chromosomes. We successfully resolved one or both telomeric ends for all 26 chromosomes, achieving near telomere-to-telomere (T2T) assemblies for chromosomes 1 A, 2A, 3A, 4A, 5A, 6A, 7A, 8A, 9A, 10A, 12A, 13A, 2B, 3B, 4B, 5B, 6B, 7B, 8B, 9B, 10B, 11B, 12B, and 13B. SR_A contained 20.80% repetitive sequences and was predicted to encode 14,101 protein-coding genes, of which 12,412 were functionally annotated. SR_B contained 21.82% repetitive sequences and was predicted to encode 14,365 protein-coding genes, with 12,602 receiving functional annotation. The high-quality dikaryotic genomes reported here represent a major advance in S. rugosoannulata genomics and provide an invaluable resource for future studies in genome biology, comparative genomics, basic biology, and molecular breeding of this species.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A multi-omics dataset of pancreatic cancer-associated cell lines under chronic hypoxia
abstract: Hypoxia is a prominent feature of the pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) tumor microenvironment and has been implicated in disease progression and chemoresistance. However, matched multiomics resources for profiling the molecular changes induced by chronic hypoxia across multiple pancreatic cell models remain limited. Here, we present a deeply characterized multiomics dataset generated from three PDAC cell lines, one pancreatic stellate cell line, and one non-malignant pancreatic ductal epithelial cell line, each cultured under normoxia and chronic hypoxia. Phenotypic validation supported hypoxia-associated changes in cell colony formation and gemcitabine response. The dataset includes matched transcriptomic (RNA-seq), proteomic, and phosphoproteomic profiles of triplicate biological samples in which 20,785 genes, 10,208 proteins, and 52,770 class I phosphosites were quantified, providing a unified view of the molecular landscape of chronic hypoxia. Consequently, this dataset provides a valuable platform for investigating hypoxia-mediated mechanisms, revealing biomarkers and identifying novel therapeutic vulnerabilities in PDAC.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Consolidated geographic and petrophysical dataset for potential underground hydrogen storage focusing on the Global South
abstract: As we move towards a green energy future, comprehensive site characterisation data for energy storage is critical for modelling, policy and guiding investment decisions. In this work, we present a dataset of 518 sub-surface formations spread across 34 countries with an emphasis on the under-explored Global South. Criteria relating to geological suitability and techno-economic feasibility from a wide range of data sources are collected from existing literature in a unified dataset. Scientific publications, industry reports, technical reports and national databases are all considered. Entries to the dataset are compiled with dates, source publications, geographic locations and operating statuses alongside site characteristics. The subsurface structures compiled include hydrocarbon fields, aquifers and salt caverns. Major limitations to consider are poor coverage in Africa & Northern South America, and restricted validation options. No assessments on site feasibility are made, and the data is entirely secondary in nature. This dataset aims to provide the groundwork for further studies in Underground Hydrogen Storage (UHS) adoption by providing input data for preliminary site selection frameworks, system modeling and policy decisions.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A telomere-to-telomere genome assembly of the fast-flowering mini-maize inbred line TX-40J
abstract: Flowering time and plant height are important target traits in maize genetic improvement. However, high-quality reference genomes for fast-flowering, short-cycle maize germplasms remain limited. Here, we integrated PacBio HiFi, Oxford Nanopore ultra-long reads, Hi-C, and Illumina short-read sequencing data to assemble a telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome for the fast-flowering maize inbred line TX-40J. The final assembly was 2.19 Gb, with a contig N50 of 233.88 Mb, and comprised ten complete chromosomes with intact telomeric sequences. Comparative structural variation analysis against the B73 reference genome identified 78,507 variants, primarily deletions and insertions, indicating substantial genomic divergence between the two maize lines. We also identified 8,664 TX-40J-T2T specific proteins, which were enriched in functional categories related to flowering time regulation, plant development, and growth-associated pathways. The TX-40J-T2T genome provides a high-quality genomic resource for investigating the genetic basis of early maturity and plant height variation in maize and supports future molecular breeding of early-flowering maize varieties.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: An open-access CT-based 3D anatomical dataset of extant sharks (Selachii) across all major lineages
abstract: Sharks exhibit extraordinary morphological diversity across a wide range of ecological niches, yet large-scale, high-resolution digital datasets of their internal anatomy remain limited. Here we present an open-access 3D shark anatomical repository derived from published X-ray computed tomography (CT) data, featuring manually segmented and systematically annotated models of the chondrocranium, visceral arches, axial skeleton, musculature, and viscera in standard STL format. The dataset comprises 117 individuals, representing 72 species across 25 families and all nine extant shark orders, with 115 full-body reconstructions and two head-only models. This open-access dataset offers a comprehensive resource for comparative anatomy, biomechanical simulations, evolutionary developmental biology and biomimetics research of extant sharks.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Estimated municipality-level electric vehicle and passenger vehicle fleet composition across 14 European countries, 2011–2024
abstract: We present a longitudinal dataset of passenger vehicle fleet composition at the municipality level for 14 European countries over 2011–2024. The dataset covers 71,715 Local Administrative Units (LAU) and disaggregates vehicle fleets into four categories: battery electric vehicles (BEVs), plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs), fuel-cell electric vehicles (FCEVs), and other vehicles. City-level stocks are generated by applying an XGBoost-based spatial prediction model to official national statistics, using municipality-level GDP per capita, population, and road-masked nighttime light intensity as spatial allocation features. National totals for each passenger vehicle type are sourced from official IEA statistics. Model validation against independently collected data using sub-national data from Eurostat and municipality-level data from Norway and Sweden confirms satisfactory spatial accuracy (R 2 = 0.82–0.98). The dataset enables comparative analysis of EV adoption geography, fleet electrification rates, and spatial disparities across European urban systems.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Full-body Motion Capture Dataset for Bilateral Weighted Shank Walking
abstract: Assistive devices are a promising tool for enhancing or restoring human walking. Weight is an important consideration when designing these devices, yet datasets for weighted human walking are scarce. We measured 13 healthy, young participants walking at their own pace in two conditions: normal, flat ground walking, and walking with bilateral weights attached to the shank. The weights were applied symmetrically and ranged from 1 kg to 5 kg in steps of 1 kg. Each task was repeated ten times. We recorded 3D positions of 58 optical markers, ground reaction forces and 16 surface electromyography signals from 8 bilateral, lower-limb muscles. Additionally, the dataset includes static pose and maximum voluntary contraction trials. Moreover, we also provide processed, gait-averaged joint kinematics, kinetics and powers, and OpenSim input files. Codes to process the data and run the OpenSim pipelines are also shared.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Scalable Framework for High-Resolution U.S. Building-Stock Data: Archetypes, Material Quantities, Embodied Impacts, and Energy Baselines for Indianapolis
abstract: We present a high-resolution, building-level data framework for the United States that integrates structure, foundation, envelope materials, archetypes, embodied-carbon factors, material quantities, and operational energy baselines with Indianapolis as a case study. Baseline attributes are drawn from the National Structure Inventory and georeferenced to individual buildings; missing envelope data are added using a bearing-based panorama–building matching of Google Street View and satellite-image segmentation. Buildings are grouped by a standardized archetype code (structure–foundation–wall–roof), each linked to 1,000-ft 2 Athena Impact Estimator models to provide scalable embodied-impact factors and material take-offs. Operational energy is estimated by harmonizing ResStock archetypes with our records and assigning energy-use intensities (electricity, gas, total) via a hierarchical matching and multi-model imputation framework (including Bayesian Ridge, Random Forest, Extra Trees, LightGBM, XGBoost, SoftImpute, and simple imputers). The release includes city-level table and a consistent data dictionary, with a workflow designed for national scaling. The dataset supports urban digital twins, building-stock modeling, retrofit targeting, and policy analysis that jointly consider embodied and operational outcomes.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A survey dataset on the adoption and readiness of artificial intelligence among enterprises in Slovakia
abstract: This dataset documents organisational adoption, readiness, attitudes, and perceived barriers related to artificial intelligence among enterprises operating in Slovakia. We collected data through an online CAWI survey administered in Slovakia between 18 August and 3 September 2025. Screening criteria restricted participation to organisations operating in Slovakia with at least 10 employees, an annual turnover of at least €200,000 and at least five years of operation. The study excluded state-owned enterprises and organisations but retained mixed-ownership organisations. The raw dataset contains 1,086 complete responses after screening, and the final analytical dataset contains 816 unique organisational records after deduplication. The questionnaire covers organisational and respondent characteristics, organisational AI maturity, corporate sentiment towards AI, adoption status, functional areas of AI use or planned use, and perceived implementation barriers. The published data package includes raw and cleaned tabular files, survey documentation, a skip-logic map, and a variable-level data dictionary. The dataset can support comparative research on AI adoption across sectors, analyses of organisational readiness and barriers, and secondary use in policy and business research.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A harmonized database of biosphere–atmosphere ammonia flux measurements across ecosystems and pollution regimes
abstract: Ammonia (NH 3 ) is a trace gas with detrimental effects on human health and ecosystems. Understanding and quantification of NH 3 exchange between the biosphere and atmosphere is essential for assessing ecosystem nitrogen budgets and critical load exceedances. Yet, uncertainty in these processes remains significant, due to the global scarcity of measurements. We created a database of more than 40,000 records of NH 3 flux measurements across ecosystems, including heathlands, peatlands, grasslands, forests, croplands, and dunes, in areas with varying ambient NH 3 and sulphur dioxide concentrations, using different measurement techniques from 1991 to 2024. A significant share of measurements originates from the Netherlands, reflecting its early deployment of a high-resolution NH 3 monitoring network. Fluxes are quality controlled and harmonized using consistent algorithms, with uncertainty estimates included. Fluxes were recalculated using consistent stability correction functions, ensuring comparability across sites. By providing this database, we aim to contribute to the understanding of the NH 3 biosphere-atmosphere exchange, its environmental controls, the validation and calibration of NH 3 exchange schemes, and the characterization of NH 3 fluxes across ecosystems.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Chromosome-level assemblies of complementary haploid genomes and population resequencing for the saprotrophic bolete Buchwaldoboletus xylophilus
abstract: Buchwaldoboletus xylophilus is a rare, non-ectomycorrhizal bolete with a saprotrophic lifestyle. Here we present reference genome assemblies for two compatible haploid strains (B06 and B07) derived from a cultivated fruiting body, together with Illumina resequencing and draft assemblies for a population set of 17 isolates comprising seven monokaryons and ten dikaryons. The submitted B06 and B07 assemblies are 30.69 Mb and 30.49 Mb, respectively, each containing 13 chromosome-sized sequences, with basidiomycota_odb12 BUSCO completeness of 97.7% and 97.9% and sample-specific Merqury QV values of 51.10 and 57.17. The resource includes structural and functional annotations, repeat annotations, mating-type-locus candidates, and CAZyme predictions. Raw reads are available through NCBI SRA under study accession SRP689425; assemblies are available through NCBI GenBank and NGDC/GWH; and annotation files and supporting results are available through Figshare.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Global Multi-Index Drought (GMID): a multiscalar high-resolution dataset from 1980 to near present
abstract: Drought assessment is an extremely complex task that relies on high-quality datasets, posing a major challenge for scientists and water managers. Here, we present the Global Multi-Index Drought (GMID), a multiscalar high-resolution dataset that includes five standardised drought indices: the Standardised Precipitation Index (SPI), the Evaporative Drought Demand Index (EDDI), the Standardised Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI), the Standardised Evapotranspiration Deficit Index (SEDI), and the Standardised Vapor Pressure Deficit Index (SVPDI). This dataset is available globally at multiple time scales (1- to 12-, 18-, 24-, 48-month) for the period 1980–2024, with high spatial (0.1°) and temporal (weekly and monthly) resolution. The GMID dataset contains two versions of the drought indices; one generated using a traditional single-distribution approach, and another using a new flexible-distribution approach allowing the selection of probability distributions providing the best-fitting normalised series in each case. GMID adds significant value to previous drought data products through its high resolution and flexible multi-index nature, representing a comprehensive and robust long-term dataset for drought (and flash drought) assessment at the global scale.

title: Hydrogeochemical, Microbial, and Rainfall Datasets for Anaerobic Dechlorination in Salinity-Gradient Aquifers
abstract: Climate change–driven sea-level rise and extreme rainfall events increase the risk of groundwater salinization of aquifers, posing challenges to in situ anaerobic bioremediation of chlorinated solvents. This dataset documents anaerobic reductive dechlorination across salinity gradients (electrical conductivity: 118–10,300 μS/cm) at three chlorinated solvent-contaminated sites in Taiwan, monitored from March to August 2019. The three sites represent contrasting salinity conditions and remediation strategies, including biostimulation and monitored natural attenuation. Measurements include multilevel hydraulic conductivity, time-series hydrogeochemical variables, volatile organic compounds, and microbial community data, including 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, quantitative analysis of Dehalococcoides and functional genes ( tceA , vcrA , bvcA , hupL ), and total bacterial counts, with propidium monoazide pretreatment applied to distinguish viable populations. Daily rainfall and temperature records from nearby meteorological stations are also provided. This six-month dataset provides a field baseline for assessing salinity effects on dechlorinating communities and for developing models linking hydrogeochemistry, seasonal hydrological variation, and microbial processes in salinity-impacted aquifers.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: LOCC-GER - A georeferenced local climate policy database for Germany
abstract: Local climate action has increased massively worldwide. Germany is a noteworthy case in this respect, as local measures have been strongly promoted by the federal system over the past two decades. However, studying policies, their determinants, and consequences at this scale has been difficult so far due to a lack of centralized data. This article introduces LOCC-GER, the largest existing dataset of georeferenced local climate policy-making in Germany. The dataset currently covers 26,142 measures from 5,033 municipalities, including detailed descriptions of employed measures, funding sum, and duration from 2008 to 2023. It is extended with important local context variables on public opinion and civil society activities, as well as detailed weather and climate indicators. We demonstrate how it can be used to map and analyze local governments’ actions on climate change. Finally, we discuss how LOCC-GER may be extended by academics and other users through our proposed workflow for user-specific linking with additional covariates, offering high spatial and temporal flexibility.

title: MECGEC: A Multi-Reference and Explainable Benchmark for Chinese Grammatical Error Correction
abstract: Driven by the rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), Chinese Grammatical Error Correction (CGEC) has made substantial progress in recent years. However, in Chinese as a Second Language (CSL) domain, existing CGEC datasets rarely incorporate learner-oriented design, i.e. providing correction rationales and more references, which hinders application of LLMs in Chinese language education. To address this gap, this paper introduces the MECGEC , a M ulti-Reference and E xplainable Benchmark for C hinese G rammatical E rror C orrection. MECGEC dataset contains 3,097 instances covering 4 major categories spanning character, word, sentence and punctuation amount to 14 fine-grained subcategories commonly found in authentic CSL learner compositions. In addition, each instance is equipped with multi references and explanation which are generated by LLMs and checked by Chinese language experts sufficiently. Besides, an extensive evaluation of state-of-the-art LLMs with strong Chinese understanding and reasoning capabilities are carried out based on the MECGEC dataset. With full and enough detailed information of authentic CSL learner errors, the MECGEC can be regarded as a comprehensive CGEC benchmark dataset in CSL domain.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Global dataset of plant water transport capacity
abstract: Whole-plant hydraulic conductance ( k plant ) quantifies the water transport capacity along the soil-plant-atmosphere continuum, and is a key trait determining plant water use and drought response strategies, as well as an essential parameter in ecosystem models. However, globally harmonised data are lacking. Here, we present the “KPLANT Dataset”, unifying data from 357 studies including 425 species, spanning 6 continents and multiple biomes, and comprising 3841 observations from 1970 to 2025. The dataset is dominated by woody species (90.71%), particularly trees (81.28%), but also includes graminoids (5.29%), and other growth forms (7 total growth forms). k plant values are given as originally reported, together with water flux and/or water potentials, plant-level dimensional and allometric traits (height, diameter, basal area, leaf area, sapwood area, Huber value) and stand characteristics (plant density, leaf area index, basal area). k plant values are additionally expressed on common normalisation bases, including leaf area, sapwood area, wood area and ground area, as well as on a non-normalised whole-plant basis. We describe the dataset, its strengths and limitations, and provide some examples of its potential uses.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Draft genome assembly and multi-tissue transcriptome of the venomous redfin waspfish Paracentropogon rubripinnis
abstract: Genomic resources for venomous fish remain scarce despite the pharmacological potential of fish venom toxins. No genome assembly is currently available for the family Tetrarogidae (waspfishes), a venomous lineage within the order Scorpaeniformes. We describe a draft genome assembly of the redfin waspfish Paracentropogon rubripinnis , generated using PacBio long-read and Illumina short-read sequencing. The assembly spans 919.8 Mb across 421 scaffolds, with a scaffold N50 of 4.92 Mb, a GC content of 40.43%, and a vertebrate gene set-based BUSCO completeness of 97.1%. Gene annotation identified 36,228 protein-coding genes, of which 31,407 were annotated. A phylogenomic analysis based on 1,178 single-copy orthologs across 16 fish species placed P. rubripinnis within the Scorpaeniformes clade. An eight-tissue RNA-seq analysis initially identified 900 toxin-homologous genes. Subsequent filtering against the UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot database retained 92 high-confidence toxin-like genes, 19 of which exhibited expression enrichment specific to the venom-producing dorsal spine. These include two genomic clusters of genes with homologies to nattectin and subunits of stonustoxin and neoverrucotoxin. The assembled genome and transcriptome data are available for reuse in comparative genomic and venom evolution studies focusing on Scorpaeniformes.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: CMIP6-driven deep-learning downscaling dataset of historical and future daily precipitation over the Loess Plateau, China
abstract: Under global warming, intensified droughts and rainfall extremes pose serious threats to water resources, ecosystems, agriculture, and geological safety in the semi-arid Loess Plateau. However, the coarse resolution and large systematic errors and uncertainties of global climate models (GCMs) limit their effectiveness for assessing regional precipitation changes and related impacts. This study employs a deep-learning (DL) downscaling approach by applying an attention-based Laplacian pyramid network to CMIP6 atmospheric variables to generate a high-resolution precipitation dataset over the Loess Plateau. The dataset provides daily precipitation at 0.1° spatial resolution for 1950–2100, based on historical simulations and two Shared Socioeconomic Pathway scenarios (SSP2-45 and SSP5-85) from four CMIP6 GCMs. Evaluation shows that the DL-downscaled data better characterize spatial details and extreme features in precipitation than the original GCM outputs, and successfully captures local probability density functions of daily precipitation across the region. With its long temporal coverage and fine spatial resolution, this dataset provides a crucial data foundation for projecting future regional precipitation changes and extremes, and for assessing the attendant impact.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Chromosome-level genome assembly and annotation of the Gobi argali (Ovis ammon darwini)
abstract: Argali ( Ovis ammon ) is an important wild relative of domestic sheep and an important ungulate species in the alpine mountain ecosystems of Central Asia and the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. Although chromosome-level genomes are available for several argali lineages, a chromosome-level reference genome specifically representing Gobi argali ( O. a. darwini ) has remained unavailable. Such a subspecies-specific reference is valuable for future comparative genomic, population genetic, and conservation studies of geographically differentiated argali lineages. In this study, we generated a high-quality chromosome-level genome assembly of Ovis ammon darwini using PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing, Hi-C chromatin conformation capture, and full-length transcriptome data. The assembly has a total size of 3.05 Gb, with a contig N50 of 81.89 Mb, and comprises 29 chromosome-assigned sequences, including 27 autosomes, the X chromosome, and a putative partial Y-chromosome sequence. Genome completeness assessment showed a BUSCO completeness of 98.5% and a quality value (QV) of 58.12, indicating high continuity and accuracy of the assembly. For structural and functional annotation, 20,074 protein-coding genes were identified, and repetitive sequences accounted for approximately 49.66% of the genome. This study provides a high-quality chromosome-level genome of Ovis ammon darwini , offering an important data resource for comparative genomics, population genetics, and conservation biology studies of Ovis ammon .
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A multi-view imaging dataset for Garden classification of femoral neck fractures
abstract: Accurate Garden classification of femoral neck fractures is essential for clinical decision-making and treatment planning. However, the lack of public, expert-annotated, multi-view imaging datasets has limited the development of reproducible artificial intelligence (AI) models and cross-institutional validation studies. Here, we present a fully anonymized, clinically validated multi-view imaging dataset for femoral neck fracture Garden classification, comprising 19,940 CT-derived images from 1,579 patients distributed across six image categories: axial CT views, coronal CT views, and three-dimensional volume-rendered (3D VR) views, each provided as paired original and internal-fixator-occlusion-removed images. The dataset was constructed from retrospective spiral CT examinations collected under ethics approval No. 2024 (Research)-024, with standardized inclusion and exclusion criteria, patient-level partitioning to prevent data leakage, and independent annotations performed by two senior orthopedic surgeons with discrepancies resolved by a chief orthopedic surgeon. We systematically document the imaging acquisition protocol, annotation workflow, preprocessing procedures, and technical validation, including high inter-annotator agreement (Cohen’s κ = 0.82, 95% CI: 0.78–0.86), balanced cohort characteristics across dataset splits, accurate occlusion-region segmentation (Dice = 0.962), and expert-confirmed anatomical plausibility of all occlusion-removed images. Benchmark classification experiments on the coronal-view occlusion-removed subset demonstrated that representative convolutional and transformer-based architectures achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values exceeding 0.96, confirming the discriminative utility of the dataset for automated Garden classification. The complete dataset is publicly available through Zenodo under a CC BY 4.0 license 1 . This resource fills a critical gap in publicly available orthopedic imaging data and provides a standardized foundation for the development, benchmarking, and clinical translation of AI-assisted femoral neck fracture classification systems.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Dataset of Equilibrium State Configurations of Adsorption in Zeolites
abstract: Zeolites are crystalline nanoporous materials widely used in adsorption, separation, and catalytic processes. Molecular simulations are commonly used to predict adsorption properties, but most high-throughput adsorption datasets report only ensemble-averaged quantities such as loadings or isotherms, rather than the molecular configurations from which these averages are obtained. Here, we present AdsZeo, a coordinate-resolved dataset of equilibrium methane adsorption configurations in aluminium-substituted, sodium-containing zeolite frameworks. The processed release contains 4,775 framework realisations derived from 191 zeolite topologies. Each framework realisation was simulated at 13 methane pressures between 0.1 and 100 bar at 298 K using grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations, giving 62,075 production simulations in total. In addition to scalar adsorption records, the dataset stores production-frame methane pseudo-atom coordinates, mobile Na + cation coordinates, framework atomic coordinates, per-frame loading and energy statistics, and simulation metadata in a processed DuckDB database. The release contains 12,415,000 saved production-frame records and 1,245,376,215 saved particle-coordinate records. AdsZeo provides coordinate-resolved adsorption data across variations in framework topology, aluminium content and distribution, sodium cation arrangement, pressure, and methane loading, enabling reuse for adsorption analysis, spatial statistics, density estimation, and machine-learning models for molecular configuration generation in charged zeolite pores.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Full-length transcriptome assembly and annotation for multiple genotypes of the dinoflagellate Coolia malayensis
abstract: Dinoflagellates are ecologically significant microeukaryotes in marine ecosystems, and benthic species are key contributors to toxin production and harmful algal blooms. Coolia malayensis , a globally distributed benthic dinoflagellate, produces multiple potent toxins and shows marked intraspecific diversity. In this study, we performed full-length transcriptome sequencing of two C. malayensis genotypes (DF364: Genotype 3; DF553: Genotype 1) with distinct physiological traits. Using SMRT sequencing, we generated 27,986 and 24,748 unigenes from DF364 and DF553, respectively. A total of 25,723 unigenes from Genotype 3 and 22,300 genes from Genotype 1 were annotated using the NT, NR, KOG, and KEGG databases. We further identified 245 and 201 long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), 19 and 23 putative transcription factor (TF) families, 6,012 and 19,336 simple sequence repeats (SSRs), and 28,477 and 25,515 protein-coding sequences (CDS) from Genotype 3 and Genotype 1, respectively. This work provides a comprehensive transcriptomic resource for the benthic dinoflagellate C. malayensis and lays a foundation for future studies in marine ecology, toxin biosynthesis, evolutionary biology, and environmental monitoring.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A relational dataset of international badminton singles matches with ranking and Elo measures, 2006–2025
abstract: International badminton competitions generate rich records of individual athletic performance; however, no publicly available dataset integrates match outcomes, rankings, and dynamic performance ratings across all competition tiers in a unified relational structure. This paper presents a relational dataset of 178,896 international badminton singles matches drawn from 1,847 Badminton World Federation (BWF)-sanctioned tournaments spanning 2006 to 2025. The match data encompass men’s singles ( n = 108,590) and women’s singles ( n = 70,306) from 172 national associations across all major competition tiers, with annual updates planned. Three linked tables—namely tournaments, players, and matches—support the longitudinal tracking of player careers and repeated rivalries. Each match record includes set-level scores, match duration, pre-match BWF world rankings, and Elo ratings constructed using a badminton-specific framework (Elo-rated favorites won 67.3% of all matches), with complementary predictive content relative to official rankings. This dataset fills a gap in publicly available longitudinal sports performance data and provides a foundation for large-scale research on athletic careers, competitive dynamics, and performance measurements across sports analytics, economics, and behavioral science.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Chromosome-level genome assembly and annotation of the white trevally (Pseudocaranx dentex)
abstract: Pseudocaranx dentex , as known as white trevally, a highly migratory marine pelagic fish with important economic value, is one of the candidates for intensive aquaculture in the far-reaching sea. However, the genetic structure and evolutionary history of white trevally remains largely unknown. Here, we performed de novo genome assembly for P. dentex using ‘2nd + 3rd’ generation DNA sequencing and Hi-C capture technique. The 636.71 Mb chromosome-level genome of white trevally was assembled, with a contig N50 length of 25.60 Mb and scaffold N50 length of 28.04 Mb. Approximately 99.16% of assembled sequences were anchored into 24 pseudo-chromosomes with the assistance of Hi-C reads. Furthermore, approximately 20.13% of the genome was composed of repetitive elements. In total, 23,208 protein-coding genes were predicted, of which 23,149 (99.75%) genes were functionally annotated. Highly accurate chromosome-level genome assembly and annotation are crucial for understanding the population genetic structure, adaptive evolution and speciation of white trevally.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Transcriptomic Dataset of Embryonic Mouse Telencephalon Revealing Sex-dependent Effects of Advanced Paternal Age
abstract: Advanced paternal age is a recognized risk factor for autism spectrum disorder (ASD), yet the molecular mechanisms linking paternal aging to early neurodevelopment remain poorly understood. Although ASD exhibits marked sex differences in prevalence and clinical presentation, whether paternal aging exerts sex-dependent effects on the embryonic brain has not been fully examined. Here, we generated a bulk RNA-sequencing dataset from embryonic day 14.5 mouse telencephalon derived from young (3-month-old) and aged (19-month-old) fathers. To minimize variability arising from developmental asynchrony, embryonic stages were rigorously matched using a hindlimb-based morphological staging method. Principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering revealed transcriptomic variation associated with both paternal age and sex. Notably, transcriptomic profiles of female aged father-derived embryos formed a distinct cluster and showed a tendency toward increased gene expression, suggesting a sex-biased transcriptional response to paternal aging. This dataset provides a well-controlled transcriptomic resource for investigating how paternal aging influences early brain development in a sex-dependent manner.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A chromosome-level genome assembly of Lucanus dybowski Parry, 1873 (Coleoptera: Lucanidae)
abstract: Stag beetles (Coleoptera: Lucanidae) are a charismatic and primitive group within the Scarabaeoidea, frequently utilized as models for evolutionary studies. Nevertheless, chromosome-level genomic resources remain limited to a few species, constraining our understanding of lucanid evolution. Here, we present the first chromosome-level genome assembly of Lucanus dybowski . The final assembly spanned 393.37 Mb with exceptional continuity (scaffold N50: 28.75 Mb), and the sequences were successfully anchored to 13 pseudo-chromosomes. The genome assembly showed a high level of completeness, achieving a BUSCO score of 99.0% (n = 1,367), which included 97.1% (1,327) single-copy and 1.9% (26) duplicated genes. Comprehensive annotation revealed a repeat content of 33.91% and identified a total of 12,704 protein-coding genes. Additionally, PSMC-based demographic analysis revealed a population history characterized by a significant expansion peaking in the Middle Pleistocene (~0.4–0.5 Mya), followed by a drastic decline during the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM). This high-quality genomic dataset offers invaluable resources for decoding stag beetle biology and will facilitate advanced comparative genomics research.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Multitasking EEG Dataset for Cognitive Workload Assessment with Controlled Task Difficulty
abstract: Cognitive workload impacts attention, memory, and decision-making. We introduce iNCog-EEG (Ideal vs. Noisy Cognitive EEG for Workload Assessment), an EEG dataset from 40 participants performing multitasking activities with varying difficulty levels. Participants completed four concurrent tasks: Math Problem, Memory Match (N-Back), Object (Visual) Tracking, and Inhibition Task (Click task), alongside a resting baseline. The dataset includes 30 clean recordings and 10 with natural artifacts, allowing the study of both artifact-free and noisy signals. It supports binary cognitive workload classification (No Workload vs. Workload) and hierarchical classification (Low, Moderate, High workload). Validation through correlation, time-frequency, and topographic analyses shows consistent neural patterns, such as increased frontal theta and decreased posterior alpha activity. Statistical validation using repeated-measures ANOVA confirmed significant neural differences across workload levels, while baseline MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron) and XGBoost (Extreme Gradient Boosting) models achieved up to 87.48% binary and 82.80% ternary classification accuracy, demonstrating reliable workload separability, even with noisy EEG. This dataset, freely available, supports cognitive workload classification, signal quality assessment, and adaptive BCI (Brain Computer Interface) development.

title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the endangered tree species Firmiana danxiaensis
abstract: Firmiana danxiaensis is a critically endangered, nationally protected tree uniquely distributed across both Danxia (acidic, nutrient-poor) and Karst (calcium-rich, alkaline) edaphic islands, valued for its ecological and ornamental significance. To support its conservation and elucidate its adaptive mechanisms, we present the first chromosome-level genome assembly of this species. Combining PacBio HiFi, Hi-C, and short-read sequencing data, we generated a high-quality genome of ~1.51 Gb, with a contig N50 of 69.08 Mb and 98.8% BUSCO completeness. Approximately 97.37% (1.47 Gb) of the assembly was anchored onto 20 pseudo-chromosomes. The genome is composed of 83.12% repetitive sequences, and we annotated 31,938 protein-coding genes, of which 97.75% were functionally annotated. This genome provides a foundational resource for conservation genomics and offers insights into the adaptation of F. danxiaensis to extreme edaphic island ecosystems.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: The chromosome-level genome of an invasive Australian population of the eastern mosquitofish (Gambusia holbrooki)
abstract: The Eastern mosquitofish, Gambusia holbrooki , is a small live bearing fish native to the southeastern United States that has been introduced globally and is now considered one of the world’s most invasive freshwater species.
