In Australia, established populations have undergone decades of adaptation to diverse thermal and ecological environments. Here we present a fully phased chromosome-level genome assembly of G. holbrooki from Townsville, Queensland, Australia, generated using PacBio HiFi long-read and Hi-C chromatin conformation sequencing. The assembly comprises 24 chromosomes and two haplotypes of approximately 676 Mb each, with contig N50 values of 26.0 Mb (HAP1) and 26.6 Mb (HAP2), and scaffold N50 values of 30.2 Mb (HAP1) and 29.2 Mb (HAP2). BUSCO completeness exceeded 98.4% for both haplotypes and Merqury quality values exceeded Q66. Telomeric repeat motifs were identified at both ends of 13 (HAP1) and 10 (HAP2) chromosome-scale scaffolds, with a further 9 (HAP1) and 7 (HAP2) chromosomes carrying signal at one end, indicating near-complete end-to-end assembly for most chromosomes. This resource provides a high-quality genomic reference for studying the invasion biology, local adaptation, sexual selection and evolutionary genomics of invasive fishes, and a foundation for future comparative analyses across globally distributed populations.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Chromosomal-level genome assembly of Cosmococcus erythrinae (Hemiptera: Coccoidea: Lecanodiaspididae)
abstract: Cosmococcus erythrinae is a potentially serious agricultural pest in southern China owing to its broad host range, high fecundity, protective wax covering, and lack of natural enemies. These biological traits raise important questions about the genomic basis of host adaptation, protective surface traits, reproductive success, and ecological persistence in scale insects. In this study, we present the first chromosome-level genome assembly of C. erythrinae , generated using Illumina, PacBio HiFi, and Hi-C sequencing technologies. The final assembly has a total size of 403.44 Mb, with 36.50% GC content, and is anchored to 17 chromosomes with a scaffold N50 of 23.97 Mb. BUSCO assessment indicated that the genome assembly achieved 91.1% completeness, including 87.2% complete single-copy and 3.9% complete duplicated. Genome annotation result showed that 58.43% (235.75 Mb) of the assembly was identified as repetitive elements, 220 ncRNAs were recognized. A total of 11,920 protein-coding genes were predicted, with an average gene length of 15,029.1 bp, of which 93.29% were functionally annotated. This high-quality genome assembly enriches genomic resources for the family Lecanodiaspididae and provides a foundation for subsequent researches on the biology, evolution, and pest management of C. erythrinae and related scale insects.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Dataset of DInSAR wrapped phase signals for AI-based automated detection and classification of mass movements
abstract: With the growing use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in remote sensing of mass movements, open and suitable datasets for model training and validation are increasingly needed. Although Differential Synthetic Aperture Radar Interferometry (DInSAR) is a widely used technique for studying mass movements, wrapped interferograms remain less exploited, and the importance of geomorphological expertise in their interpretation is not usually emphasised. In this work, we introduce a dataset of DInSAR wrapped phase signals designed to support the development of Deep Learning (DL) models for the automated detection and classification of active slow-moving mass movements. The dataset covers two selected wide areas in the Central European Alps and the Northern Apennines. It contains 4910 expert-annotated DInSAR wrapped phase signals derived from 92 Sentinel-1 interferograms with temporal baselines ranging from 6 days to 1 year, classified into nine distinct landslide and periglacial landform classes after careful geomorphological interpretation. This dataset is expected to support the scientific community in AI-based applications for mass movement research, while also serving as a benchmark for the generation of comparable datasets.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Chromosome-level genome assembly and annotation of the crinoid echinoderm Comaster schlegelii
abstract: A chromosome-level genome assembly was generated for Comaster schlegelii , a free-living comatulid feather star of the class Crinoidea, using an integrated strategy combining Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing, MGI DNBSEQ-T7 short-read sequencing and Hi-C chromatin interaction data. The assembled genome was 898.51 Mb in length, with both contig and scaffold N50 values reaching 63.84 Mb, and most of the assembly was anchored onto 12 pseudochromosomes. BUSCO analysis recovered 96.60% of conserved metazoan orthologs from the assembled genome. Genome annotation predicted 25,791 protein-coding genes, and BUSCO assessment of the predicted proteome showed 98.90% completeness. Among these genes, 23,277 (91%) were assigned functional annotations from at least one public database. This genome assembly expands the currently limited genomic resources for crinoids and provides a useful reference for comparative studies of feather star evolution, taxonomy and lineage-specific diversification.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A phased telomere-to-telomere genome of Rosa wichuraiana ‘Basye’s Thornless’, a key progenitor for modern rose breeding
abstract: Rosa wichuraiana ‘Basye’s Thornless’ (BT) is a critical diploid germplasm in rose genetics and breeding programmes, prized for its superior traits including thornlessness, disease resistance, and vigorous root-sprouting capacity. Here, we present a telomere-to-telomere (T2T) haplotype-resolved genome assembly of BT generated using PacBio HiFi long reads, Oxford Nanopore Technologies ultra-long reads, and Hi-C chromatin conformation capture data. The final assembly spans 978.2 Mb and is anchored to 16 contiguous scaffolds, representing 14 chromosome-scale sequences corresponding to two complete haplotypes of seven chromosome pairs with six gaps, alongside the chloroplast and mitochondrial genomes. The N50 values of contig and scaffold are 67.9 Mb and 68.1 Mb, respectively. Assessment of assembly quality revealed a BUSCO completeness score of 99.0%, a consensus quality value (QV) of 68.11, and functional annotation of 95.6% among 67,611 predicted protein-coding genes, collectively confirming a high-quality, reference-grade assembly. Repetitive elements constitute 60.1% of the genome, predominantly composed of long terminal repeat (LTR) retrotransposons. There are 25,475 syntenic homologous gene pairs with extensive structural variation detected between the two haplotypes including 1,089,143 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), 62 inversions, and 587 translocations. The BT genome features approximately 219 Mb of highly diverged regions, with chromosome 3 showing the highest genome heterozygosity by sequence length (~6.5%) and one 2.27 Mb inversion. These findings underscore both the high heterozygosity of the BT genome and the importance of haplotype-resolved assembly in capturing allelic diversity in roses.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A chromosome-level genome assembly and annotation of Dhole (Cuon alpinus)
abstract: The dhole ( Cuon alpinus ) is an endangered canid species that has experienced substantial population declines due to habitat fragmentation, human disturbance, depletion of prey resources, and pathogen transmission from domestic animals. Here, we present the first chromosome-level genome assembly of C. alpinus generated using a combination of Illumina short-read sequencing, Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing, and Hi-C chromatin interaction data. The final assembly spans 2.42 Gb, with a contig N50 of 41.42 Mb and a scaffold N50 of 63.77 Mb. A total of 97.03% of the assembled sequences were anchored onto 39 chromosomes. Genome completeness reached 98.10% based on BUSCO analysis. We predicted 20,247 protein-coding genes, of which 17,817 (90.00%) were functionally annotated. Repetitive sequences and transposable elements (TEs) account for 44.68% of the genome, with long interspersed nuclear elements (LINEs) being the predominant class. This high-quality genome assembly provides an important genomic resource for studies of canid evolution, population genetics, and conservation biology.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: 2016–2023 China’s land-sea environmental extended input-output dataset
abstract: China is a key driver of global marine economic growth, and a critical region for advancing the synergistic governance of pollution reduction and carbon mitigation. The environmentally extended input-output table serves as the core foundation for research on industrial environmental impacts. However, existing dataset do not effectively distinguish between land-based and marine industries, and thus cannot adequately support research on land-sea synergistic pollution and carbon reduction. To this end, this study constructs China’s land-sea environmentally extended input-output (CLSEEIO) dataset covering the period from 2016 to 2023. This dataset covers input-output data of 42 land-based industries and 13 marine industries. It integrates emission inventories of a total of 30 environmental pollutants, including greenhouse gases, 10 water pollutants and 19 atmospheric pollutants. It can provide standardized foundational data support for various studies related to land-sea environmental footprints and green low-carbon development.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: LIVE-GaitNeuroKids: A multimodal and Longitudinal Gait dataset with Inertial, Video and surface Electromyography in Neuromotor conditions and typically developing children
abstract: Precise characterization of gait patterns is essential for the clinical assessment of motor disorders, such as cerebral palsy (CP) and idiopathic toe walking (ITW). While laboratory-based motion capture remains the gold standard, its operational complexity often limits its use in daily clinical practice. In this work, we present a comprehensive, multi-modal dataset of pediatric gait comprising 59 participants: 22 with CP, 12 with ITW, and 25 typically developing (TD) controls. The dataset provides synchronized time-series of 3D kinematics, derived from a body-worn inertial measurement unit (IMU) system ( Xsens™) , and four-channel surface electromyography (sEMG) ( Delsys Trigno™ ) targeting the tibialis anterior and gastrocnemius muscles. Additionally, regular video recordings from three views (front left, front right, and sagittal) are provided as quality visual references. A distinguishing feature of this repository is the inclusion of pre- and post-treatment sessions for pathological cohorts, enabling the evaluation of clinical interventions over time. The records include (i) raw acquisition files, (ii) processed clinical joint angles and sEMG signals, and (iii) segmented gait cycles time-aligned across wearable sensors. This dataset facilitates the development of automated gait analysis algorithms, clinical decision-support methods, and digital gait biomarkers, bridging the gap between laboratory-based gait analysis and portable monitoring in pediatric clinical settings.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A telomere-to-telomere genome assembly of Pythium sp. P16-1 (Oomycota, Pythiaceae)
abstract: Pythium spp. include numerous important pathogenic species that affect both plants and animals, posing serious threats to agricultural production and to human and livestock health. Currently, high-quality genomic resources for these species are scarce, impeding the understanding of population evolution and the development of effective prevention and control strategies. Here, the first complete telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome of Pythium sp. was generated by integrating NGS, PacBio HiFi, ONT and Hi-C data. The genome had a total size of 59.9 Mb, with a scaffold N50 of 3.5 Mb. BUSCO assessment indicated that the genome assembly achieved 94.91% (n = 255) completeness. A total of 14,111 protein-coding genes were predicted, with 12,711 genes (90.08% of the total) annotated using functional databases. Additionally, we predicted 382 effectors. This T2T genome is an excellent resource for furthering the understanding of evolutionary history and pathogenic mechanisms of Pythium spp.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A dataset of snow avalanche activity in southeastern Tibetan Plateau
abstract: Snow avalanches pose a significant hazard on the Southeastern Tibetan Plateau (SETP), yet long-term and systematic observational datasets remain limited. Here, we present a comprehensive multi-source avalanche dataset for the SETP. The dataset integrates satellite imagery, field surveys, environmental data, and model outputs, and consists of four components: (1) a multi-temporal inventory of 25,458 manually digitized avalanche polygons derived from optical imagery; (2) a database of 381 avalanche hazard sites with geomorphic and impact attributes; (3) a set of 47 raster layers representing 17 avalanche predisposing factors, including topographic, vegetation, meteorological, and snowpack variables; and (4) monthly avalanche susceptibility maps at a 30 m resolution based on environmental conditions during the 2020/2021 snow season (December 2020–May 2021). Data quality was assessed through independent image interpretation by two analysts (Kappa = 0.82) and spatial consistency between mapped avalanches and susceptibility patterns. The dataset provides a standardised resource for avalanche research, hazard assessment, and model development in high-mountain regions.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A monthly 250 m Vegetation Drought Resistance Index (VDRI) dataset for China from 2000 to 2022
abstract: Global warming is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme droughts, threatening terrestrial ecosystem structure and function. However, existing indices often fail to provide a comprehensive representation of the water cycle, and high-resolution datasets for characterizing vegetation responses to drought remain limited. To address this gap, we first developed a monthly Vertical Composite Drought Index (VCDI) by integrating precipitation, surface runoff, soil moisture, and groundwater storage anomalies. This index summarizes multidimensional water constraints across the “atmosphere-surface-subsurface” continuum and captures cumulative effects of drought across multiple timescales. Furthermore, VCDI, land surface temperature, and vegetation greenness were combined to produce a monthly Vegetation Drought Resistance Index (VDRI) dataset for China at 250 m resolution from 2000 to 2022. Multi-source evaluations indicate that VDRI provides spatially detailed and temporally consistent information on vegetation conditions under concurrent hydroclimatic and thermal stress. The datasets support ecosystem assessment, ecological drought monitoring, wildfire risk analysis, and benchmarking for drought-impact studies and related ecological models.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Whole-transcriptome Sequencing Dataset from the longissimus dorsi Muscle of CD163/pAPN Double-knockout Pigs
abstract: Gene editing holds promise for improving disease resistance in livestock. We previously generated CD163/pAPN double-knockout (DKO) pigs that exhibit resistance to multiple viruses while maintaining normal production traits. However, broader application of gene-edited animals requires careful evaluation of potential molecular changes associated with genome editing. Here, we present a whole-transcriptome sequencing dataset generated from the longissimus dorsi muscle of DKO pigs and their wild-type (WT) counterparts. The dataset includes expression profiles of four major RNA classes: messenger RNAs (mRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), circular RNAs (circRNAs), and microRNAs (miRNAs). This resource provides transcriptomic data that may facilitate further investigation of gene-editing-associated molecular changes and contribute to the safety evaluation of genetically engineered livestock.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A High-Resolution Acoustic-Optical-Magnetic Multimodal Dataset for Underwater Environment Perception and Resource Exploration
abstract: Underwater environment perception requires complementary optical, acoustic, and magnetic sensing modalities. Here, we present UPED, a high-resolution multimodal underwater dataset integrating RGB images, multibeam sonar images, laser point clouds, and triaxial magnetic measurements. The dataset was collected in a controlled seawater tank under three representative scenarios, including benthic biota, mineral enrichment, and subsea pipelines. UPED contains 2,400 RGB images, 2,400 sonar frames, 22 laser point-cloud sequences, and 2,600 magnetic samples. Among them, 2,000 low-overlap RGB images were manually annotated with 5,742 target instances. The dataset covers controlled variations in illumination, turbidity, temperature, and sound speed, while preserving synchronized multimodal measurements and sensor metadata. We further provide baseline experiments for object detection, underwater image enhancement, multimodal recognition, and simulation-to-real transfer. UPED provides a reproducible benchmark for developing and evaluating multimodal underwater perception methods.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A human activity recognition dataset spanning multiple devices and body positions with cross-dataset evaluation
abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) seeks to classify physical activities from motion signals acquired in everyday settings, often using machine learning models trained on sensor data from ubiquitous devices such as smartphones. Despite significant advances, progress in the field is hindered by the fragmentation of publicly available datasets, which differ in protocols, devices, sensor placement, and labeling schemes. As a result, models that perform well on individual datasets often fail to generalize across populations, hardware, and real-world conditions. In this paper, we present the AICOS-HAR dataset, a large and diverse resource comprising 5,231 labeled activity acquisitions (101.4 hours) from 106 participants, collected using 87 smartphones and 17 wearable devices across multiple research initiatives, including both inertial and barometric signals. Earlier versions of this dataset have already enabled advances in position-invariant HAR, pedestrian navigation, and active learning, underscoring its utility. In addition to releasing the curated dataset, we provide 21 open-source parsers that transform existing publicly available HAR datasets into a unified schema, facilitating integrative analyses and systematic cross-dataset benchmarking. Together, these resources support the development and systematic evaluation of robust and generalizable HAR models, accelerating their translation into real-world applications in health monitoring and mobility analysis.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A modelled dataset of compute demand and service requirements for Chinese provinces
abstract: This Data Descriptor presents a transparent, reproducible and scenario-based modelled data product for provincial compute demand in China. The release provides online demand at one-minute resolution, batch demand at one-hour resolution and resource-occupancy distributions for 31 provincial-level regions over a full calendar year. Workload timing and task-size morphology are derived from the Huawei sir-lab 2023 Private serverless trace, while absolute national scale is normalised to the 962 EFlops computing-equipment capacity reported in the 2025 Advanced Computing and Computing Power Development Index Blue Paper. Four scenarios set national mean demand to 60%, 100%, 150% and 200% of this installed capacity; these ratios are provisioning and stress-test conventions, not claims about realised utilisation. Provincial means and diurnal shape modifiers are estimated from socioeconomic indicators, and each time-series record carries provenance and scenario metadata. The dataset is intended for queueing, scheduling, cross-region workload allocation and data-centre energy modelling where no measured public provincial compute-demand time series exists.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Oblique drone panoramic imagery for fine-scale human-induced land-cover change detection
abstract: High-Resolution Spatiotemporal Monitoring of Seasonal Land-Use and Land-Cover (LULC) Changes (HRST-MSLC) holds broad application prospects. However, existing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) change-detection benchmarks are predominantly based on nadir-view, bi-temporal imagery, providing limited lateral structural information and seasonal observations, while data-acquisition costs and multi-temporal registration constrain dataset construction. To address this, this paper introduces the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Oblique Multi-View Panoramic Change Detection Dataset (UAV-OMVCD) for fine-scale human-induced LULC change monitoring. It contains 864 panoramic observations acquired in four study areas across Nanjing, Hefei, and Tangshan using DJI Matrice 4D/4TD and Matrice 4E platforms. Each panorama is exported at 1448 × 7200 pixels, with nominal nadir-equivalent source-frame ground sampling distances (GSDs) of approximately 3.7–8.5 cm, yielding 2,181 paired 512 × 512 samples. UAV-OMVCD documents seasonal changes in impervious surfaces, engineering machinery, buildings, greenhouses, and piled soil, including structural additions/removals and morphological evolution. Its oblique views capture lateral facades and occluded areas while reducing seasonal pseudo-change interference. Five benchmark models achieved overall accuracies of 0.9429–0.9492, macro-averaged F1-scores of 0.8861–0.9007, and macro-averaged Intersection over Union (IoU) values of 0.8049–0.8266. UAV-OMVCD provides a standardized benchmark for fine-scale human-induced land-cover change detection using oblique drone panoramic imagery.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Curated peptide-HLA class I binding affinities with Rosetta structural ensembles
abstract: The interaction between peptide antigens and class I human leukocyte antigens (HLA) is a central determinant of CD8 + T cell recognition and a foundational target for cancer immunotherapy, vaccine design, and autoimmune disease research. Computational prediction of peptide-HLA (pHLA) binding has progressed rapidly with sequence-based machine learning, but structure-aware approaches remain limited by the scarcity of paired experimental affinity data and three-dimensional structural information. Here we describe a publicly released dataset combining curated quantitative binding affinity measurements from the Immune Epitope Database (IEDB) with computationally generated Rosetta FlexPepDock structural ensembles. The dataset spans 95 HLA-A, HLA-B, and HLA-C alleles, 25,622 unique peptides, and 112,561 peptide-allele pairs, each paired with a 25-decoy structural ensemble (2,814,025 decoy structures total, ~155 GB). We document the curation pipeline, the structure generation protocol, and two independent validation analyses to establish data quality. The resource is released under CC BY 4.0 on HuggingFace and is intended to support training and benchmarking of structure-aware pHLA binding affinity models.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: MIMIC-IV-Echo: An Echocardiography Dataset Integrated with the MIMIC-IV Ecosystem
abstract: MIMIC-IV-Echo is a publicly available dataset of echocardiographic imaging and structured quantitative measurements linked to the MIMIC-IV clinical database. The module includes more than 7,000 transthoracic echocardiogram studies in DICOM format acquired between 2017 and 2019, accompanied by over 200,000 structured measurement studies spanning transthoracic, transesophageal, and stress echocardiography from 2008 through 2022. Imaging files retain their original multi-frame structure and acquisition characteristics, while structured measurements provide clinician-reviewed quantitative parameters recorded during routine clinical interpretation. All records are deidentified and linked to the broader MIMIC-IV ecosystem through shared identifiers and date shifting, enabling integration with hospital, ICU, emergency department, laboratory, medication, and clinical note data. By providing both raw echocardiographic imaging and associated quantitative measurements, MIMIC-IV-Echo supports a wide range of research applications in cardiovascular imaging, multimodal learning, phenotyping, and clinical outcome modeling. The dataset is freely available on PhysioNet.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A global 0.1-degree gridded dataset of single and compound temperature and precipitation extremes from 1950 to 2025
abstract: Extreme weather and climate events are increasingly intensified by human-induced global warming, exacerbating risks to ecosystems and society. Yet many global extremes datasets remain coarse and fragmented, limiting local assessments of temperature and precipitation hazards. Here we introduce ERA5-EX, a global 0.1° gridded dataset of single and compound temperature and precipitation extremes from 1950 to 2025 derived from ERA5-Land. ERA5-EX provides 34 annual variables comprising 26 indices from Expert Team on Climate Change Detection and Indices, and eight bivariate metrics that quantify occurrence days for compound wet-hot, wet-cold, dry-hot, dry-cold, warm day-night, cold day-night, warm-heavy rain, and cold-heavy rain events. We also release the ERA5-EX tool, a Python workflow for tiled global or regional processing from daily inputs through index and compound event generation, feature extraction, and map and time series visualization. Technical evaluation is provided through intercomparison with observationally constrained gridded extremes products for single indices and with publicly available compound event datasets where definitions overlap. The ERA5-EX dataset and tool serve to support climate monitoring and risk assessment.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: The Encanto Neighborhood Field Experiments Dataset: Land–Atmosphere Interactions in Urban Phoenix
abstract: Urban environments exhibit strong spatial heterogeneity in surface properties and morphology, driving complex land–atmosphere interactions at neighborhood scales that remain poorly documented. The Encanto Neighborhood field experiments were designed to address this gap by collecting spatially dense, multi-dimensional and multi-parameteric observations across a ~3 × 3 km domain in Phoenix, Arizona. The dataset combines fixed, mobile, and balloon-borne measurements of atmospheric properties near the surface and at various heights in the column, as well as measurements of turbulent exchanges and land surface properties. This work also contributes a technique that transforms irregular mobile temperature measurements into continuous, high-resolution temperature fields, enabling separation of temporal evolution from spatial variability. The resulting dataset provides meter-scale maps of air and surface temperature, vertical profiles of thermodynamic and wind structure, and land–atmosphere exchange measurements. Technical validation demonstrates strong agreement between independent measurements and quantifies reconstruction accuracy under varying sampling conditions. This dataset supports process-level studies of urban microclimate, evaluation of high-resolution micrometeorological models, and the development of spatiotemporal reconstruction and data assimilation approaches.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Digitalization of the genotypic and phenotypic information retained within the FEM grapevine germplasm bank
abstract: The Fondazione Edmund Mach (FEM) maintains a grapevine germplasm bank consisting of 3,065 grapevine accessions that supports long-term conservation and utilisation of crop genetic diversity. In addition to acquisitions, the germplasm includes advanced crossbreeding selections developed to improve grape quality and introgress tolerance and resistance traits. This objective highlights the importance of verifying accession identity through standardized molecular profiles, complemented by ampelographic characterization when necessary. A systematic inventory of the germplasm was undertaken and a comprehensive ontologization of all accession-related data and metadata was carried out in the context of FAIR (Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, and Reusability) compliance. This overarching survey led to the published FEMVitisDataset encompassing 2,905 accessions, resulting in the identification of 1,931 unique profiles. Of these, 915 were classified as novel, as no exact or near-exact genetic match was found across the consulted reference databases. By providing accession-level passport data, validated SSR profiles, and associated phenotypic information, the FEMVitisDataset expands the documentation of grapevine diversity and represents a valuable resource for germplasm management, genetic studies, and modern breeding programs integrating molecular and phenotypic information.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A chromosome-level genome assembly of the Asiatic black bear (Ursus thibetanus)
abstract: The Asiatic black bear ( Ursus thibetanus ) is a forest-adapted species occupying a critical phylogenetic position within the Ursidae family, serving as an ideal model for studying adaptive radiation and complex trait evolution. However, the absence of a high-quality chromosome-level reference genome has hindered in-depth evolutionary and conservation genetic studies. Here, we present the first chromosome-level genome assembly of the Asiatic black bear, generated by integrating PacBio high-fidelity (HiFi) long-read sequencing and high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) technologies. The final genome assembly is 2.52 Gb with a contig N50 of 52.84 Mb and a scaffold N50 of 72.38 Mb. We identified 1,187.81 Mb (47.07%) of repetitive sequences and predicted 22,339 protein-coding genes, 2,434 long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), and 337 pseudogenes. Assessment confirms the genome is superior in contiguity, completeness (BUSCO score of 96.34%), and accuracy (QV of 51.85). This high-quality genome is a key resource for studying bear traits (e.g., diet shifts, hibernation) and the Asiatic black bear’s population history and conservation genetics.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: StitchingNet-Seg: a semantic segmentation dataset of industrial sewing stitch defects
abstract: Adoption of automated quality control in the textile and apparel industry has lagged owing to inherent features, such as labor-intensive tasks and deformability of flexible fabrics. Precise detection and localized diagnosis of sewing stitch defects remain critical challenges because existing datasets often provide only image-level labels or focus exclusively on raw fabric anomalies. Therefore, we propose StitchingNet-Seg, a comprehensive, large-scale semantic segmentation dataset designed for industrial sewing processes. Derived from the StitchingNet dataset, this dataset comprises 10,836 images covering 11 representative fabric types, 7 defect classes and 1 normal class (8 classes in total). Each image is annotated with pixel-level masks to capture intricate geometric features. To validate the usability and technical quality of the dataset, benchmark experiments are conducted using representative convolutional neural network-based architectures and vision transformer-based models. The evaluation results demonstrated robust overall learnability across diverse architectures. However, they also revealed relatively lower segmentation performance on specific defect classes characterized by subtle thread tension variations and 3D structural deformations. This confirms that StitchingNet-Seg provides a reliable foundation for developing intelligent automated optical inspection systems for the global garment industry.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Large language models accelerate dataset screening for meta-analysis in biomedical data repositories
abstract: Following the adoption of FAIR principles, biomedical data repositories contain thousands of datasets, presenting a significant findability challenge requiring time-consuming, manual screening. Large language models (LLMs) have potential to accelerate this process, but existing work applying LLMs to post-retrieval dataset screening remains limited. To address this gap, we developed a generalizable, repository-agnostic framework and prompt schema for LLM-based dataset screening and systematically evaluated four general-purpose LLMs across three repositories and disease settings: NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (536 lung cancer datasets), ProteomeXchange (258 ovarian cancer datasets), and, retrospectively, ArrayExpress (56 neurodegeneration datasets). Across these case studies, highest median sensitivity for individual LLMs on held-out test sets ranged from 88–93% (up to 100% with ensembled decisions), with 85.1%–99.1% specificity across repositories. In the retrospective ArrayExpress case study, the framework and prompt schema generalized to a distinct repository and disease setting without tuning. These findings indicate that LLMs can maintain high sensitivity and specificity while substantially reducing dataset screening effort, completing screening in a median of 6.0 minutes.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the sap-feeding beetle Amphicrossus lewisi (Coleoptera: Nitidulidae)
abstract: Amphicrossus lewisi is a sap-feeding beetle associated with fermenting tree-sap habitats, but genomic resources for its subfamily, Amphicrossinae, are lacking. We generated a chromosome-level reference genome for A. lewisi using PacBio HiFi long reads, Illumina short reads, Hi-C chromatin-contact data and RNA sequencing from multiple developmental stages. The 991.21 Mb assembly comprises ten chromosome-scale scaffolds and has a scaffold N50 of 129.00 Mb. Repetitive elements account for 69.15% of the genome. Evidence from transcript alignments, protein homology and ab initio prediction identified 12,691 protein-coding genes, of which 12,061 (95.04%) received at least one functional annotation. Assembly quality was supported by 99.5% complete endopterygota_odb10 BUSCOs, a Merqury consensus quality value of 43.89, and mapping rates of 99.85% and 99.11% for Illumina and HiFi reads, respectively. The deposited raw reads, genome assembly and annotations provide a reusable resource for comparative genomics, phylogenetics and studies of adaptation to sap-associated environments in Nitidulidae.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Simultaneous EEG-fNIRS Dataset for Multi-class Visual Imagery Classification
abstract: Visual imagery is a cognitive process that generates internal visual representations in the absence of external visual stimuli and has become an important paradigm in brain-computer interface (BCI) research. In recent years, although publicly available simultaneous EEG-fNIRS datasets have been developed for tasks such as motor imagery and mental arithmetic, bimodal neural signal resources specifically designed for visual imagery tasks remain limited. Therefore, this study constructs and releases a simultaneous EEG-fNIRS dataset for three-class visual imagery tasks.The dataset initially collected neural signal data from 23 participants. After quality control, 22 valid participants were retained for subsequent analyses. During data acquisition, 32-channel EEG was used to record scalp electrophysiological signals, while 22-channel fNIRS was used to measure prefrontal hemodynamic responses. The dataset includes raw EEG and fNIRS signals, event markers, channel information, and example preprocessing codes.Furthermore, EEG-based, fNIRS-based, and EEG-fNIRS fusion baseline models were established to evaluate whether the dataset contains discriminative information for three-class visual imagery classification. The benchmark results demonstrate that the dataset contains neural information associated with visual imagery conditions and can support unimodal analysis, multimodal fusion, and BCI-related research.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A dataset of small-scale coal waste dumps in Shanxi Province, China from high-resolution satellite images
abstract: Coal is central to the global energy mix. Coal waste dumps, the predominant solid waste from mining operations, pose severe ecological threats through prolonged accumulation. Large coal waste dumps receive regulatory attention, but small dumps evade oversight. Their concealed locations and small footprints challenge conventional remote sensing and manual inspection, creating regulatory blind spots. To address this, We developed a dataset for fine-grained identification of small coal waste dumps in typical coal-producing regions of Shanxi Province. The dataset employs high-resolution GaoFen-2 (GF-2) satellite imagery with a pan-sharpened spatial resolution of 0.8 m. Field surveys and image interpretation were combined to enable precise waste dump annotations. The dataset spans multiple coal-producing cities with regionally representative samples. Collection and annotation of often-neglected small dumps were prioritized, substantially enhancing practical utility. The dataset supports high-precision automated extraction of coal waste dumps through deep learning semantic segmentation. Applications include illegal dumping detection, temporal monitoring, abandoned mine remediation, and ecosystem restoration, advancing comprehensive and intelligent environmental governance in mining areas.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Telomere-to-telomere (T2T), gap-free assembly of male and female golden pompano (Trachinotus ovatus) reference genomes
abstract: The golden pompano ( Trachinotus ovatus ), a marine fish species within the Carangidae family, exhibits a broad geographical distribution and a remarkable capacity to adapt to severe environmental rigors. We constructed two telomere-to-telomere, gap-free reference genomes for male and female golden pompano, which serve as essential resources for future studies aimed at elucidating the genetic basis of environmental adaptation and enhancing aquaculture productivity. By combination of Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) ultra-long and PacBio HiFi reads, we assembled 24 chromosomes without any gaps. The golden pompano genome sizes are approximately 642.56 Mb and 644.01 Mb of male and female individuals, with N50 length of 28.02 Mb and 28.45 Mb, respectively. The completeness results of BUSCO evaluation show about 98.8% for males and 99.2% for females, representing a high-level of completeness of both genomes. We also obtained 24,624 and 24,169 protein-coding genes from male and female individuals. The two available gap-free, chromosome-level genomes of T. ovatus provide the precise reference for addressing core biological questions, such as the genetic basis of economically important traits including growth rate, disease resistance, and feed conversion efficiency, as well as the molecular mechanisms underlying stress tolerance and reproductive performance, and will directly advance key aquaculture technologies, thereby enhancing the efficiency and sustainability of golden pompano farming.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A precomputed atlas of protein structural and sequence similarity
abstract: Comparing protein structures and their underlying sequences to one another underpins tasks including homology detection, identification of structurally convergent but sequence-divergent relationships, and classification into structural and evolutionary families. Existing tools support per-query search or curated classification, but obtaining both structural and sequence similarity metrics for a given pair, together with alignment detail, typically requires multiple independent tools. StructomeDB provides precomputed, pairwise structural and sequence similarity data across a representative, non-redundant set of 61,631 UniProt-linked protein chains drawn from the experimental Protein Data Bank. For each of 104,528,817 resulting structurally detected pair records, structural similarity, sequence similarity, and biological annotations are retained in a unified, queryable form. The dataset may support benchmarking of structural and sequence comparison methods, generation of labelled training data for machine learning approaches to protein classification, comparative analyses of structural and evolutionary relationships across taxa, and identification of candidate pairs for detailed structural or phylogenetic follow-up.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the taeniid cestode Echinococcus multilocularis
abstract: Echinococcus multilocularis , responsible for the development of alveolar echinococcosis (AE), remains a significant threat to public health in the Northern Hemisphere. In this study, we generated a chromosome-scale genome assembly by integrating PacBio HiFi long reads, DNBSEQ-T7 short reads, and Hi-C chromatin-conformation data. After HiFi-based gap filling, the final 136.32 Mb assembly comprises 32 sequences, with a maximum sequence length of 28.24 Mb and both contig and scaffold N50 values of 16.06 Mb. A total of 97.24% of the assembled sequence was anchored onto nine pseudo-chromosomes, and two (chr5 and chr9) were resolved from telomere to telomere. Assembly consistency was supported by HiFi and short-read mapping rates of 99.93% and 97.90%, respectively, with > 99.9% genome coverage. BUSCO completeness was 71.7% for the genome against metazoa_odb10, consistent with values reported for other cestode genomes, in which extensive lineage-specific gene loss is well documented. Repetitive elements accounted for 12.81% of the genome. In total, 10,950 protein-coding genes were predicted, of which 98.66% were functionally annotated. The high-resolution genome of E. multilocularis forms a solid foundation for understanding its pathogenic mechanisms, host adaptation, and evolution. This foundation supports future efforts in diagnostics and interventions against AE.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A targeted lipidomic dataset of Tenebrio molitor larvae fed diets with different protein levels
abstract: Tenebrio molitor larvae are increasingly used as a sustainable biomass source for food and feed, yet lipid-level datasets describing their responses to dietary protein remain limited. Here, we present a targeted UPLC–MS/MS lipidomic dataset from whole T. molitor larvae reared on four diets: wheat bran control and three formulated diets containing 15%, 20%, or 25% crude protein. The dataset includes 20 biological samples, with five independent replicates per treatment, each generated by pooling 30 larvae. Using a scheduled multiple reaction monitoring method on a QTRAP 6500 + platform, we obtained internal-standard-normalized semiquantitative abundance estimates for 834 targeted lipid features with MRM-based annotations, including glycerolipids, glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids, fatty acyls, sterols, and prenol lipids. Data records comprise mzML files, concentration matrices, sample metadata, lipid annotations, lipid target information, and quality-control measurements. Technical validation using pooled quality-control samples, coefficient-of-variation analysis, sample correlations, principal component analysis, and heatmap visualization supported the reproducibility of the dataset. This resource can facilitate studies of insect nutrition, dietary lipid remodeling, feed formulation, and comparative lipidomics.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A national 30-m crop yield dataset for major staple crops in China for 2024
abstract: High-resolution crop yield datasets are essential for agricultural monitoring, yet nationwide fine-scale yield products remain limited in China. Here, we developed a national 30-m crop yield estimation framework by integrating multi-sensor Landsat datasets, remote-sensing-based crop distribution and phenology products, and agricultural statistics. The framework combines the Vegetation Photosynthesis Model (VPM) with a crop-specific GPP-to-yield conversion approach to generate spatially explicit yield maps for rice, winter wheat, and maize across China in 2024. Landsat surface reflectance observations were used to estimate gross primary productivity (GPP) at 30-m resolution, while crop distribution and phenology information constrained crop-specific growing areas and growing-season GPP accumulation. Provincial agricultural statistics were used to calibrate crop- and variety-specific harvest index (HI) values for GPP-to-yield conversion. The resulting yield estimates showed generally reasonable agreement with county-level statistics, with relative mean absolute errors ranging from 17.1% to 22.4% across crops. This dataset provides nationwide, high-resolution yield information for three major staple crops in China and offers a scalable framework for satellite-based agricultural productivity monitoring.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Near telomere-to-telomere reference genome assembly of Megacarpaea megalocarpa (Brassicaceae)
abstract: As a perennial spring ephemeral, Megacarpaea megalocarpa escapes extreme summer drought through rapid early-spring growth and deeply buried meristems. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying this specialized stress-avoidance strategy remain unclear. Moreover, the complex mesopolyploid and allopolyploid history of this tribe has continuously obscured its phylogenetic position, complicating our understanding of its evolutionary origins. Here, we present the first near telomere-to-telomere genome assembly of M. megalocarpa integrating PacBio HiFi, ONT ultra-long, Hi-C, and Illumina sequencing. The 983.65 Mb assembly is anchored to nine pseudo-chromosomes, with 37.67% GC content and 77.67% repetitive sequences. Assessments confirm high continuity (contig N50: 40.62 Mb; scaffold N50: 118.87 Mb), completeness (LAI: 15.20; BUSCO: 98.70%), and correctness (QV: 57.12) of the genome. We identified 30,168 protein-coding genes, of which 29,679 (98.38%) were functionally annotated, and the BUSCO assessment confirmed 96.40% completeness of the gene models. This high-quality assembly provides a robust foundation for elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying adaptive evolution in response to extreme environmental conditions and resolving the complex phylogenetic position of the tribe Megacarpaeeae.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Chromosome-level genome assembly and annotation of Lycodon rosozonatus
abstract: Lycodon rosozonatus is an endemic Chinese reptile of the family Colubridae. Historically, it has been known only from Hainan Island. To date, research on L. rosozonatus has primarily focused on its taxonomy, while its physiological, biochemical, and ecological adaptations remain largely uncharacterized. To facilitate future studies on its evolution and adaptation, we sequenced and assembled a high-quality chromosome-level genome for this species. Combining PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing and Hi-C technologies, we yielded a genome assembly of 1.74 Gb, with 99.75% of the sequences anchored onto 23 chromosomes. The assembled genome is highly contiguous, with a contig N50 of 107.10 Mb and scaffold N50 of 168.87 Mb. A total of 21,650 protein-coding genes were annotated, and 98.42% of these genes were functionally described. Assessment with BUSCO revealed high completeness of both the genome assembly (98.2%) and annotation (98.5%). Additionally, repetitive sequences constituted 56.47% (1.02 Gb) of the genome. This high-quality reference genome provides a valuable genomic resource for future research on the genetic diversity and evolutionary history of L. rosozonatus and will support further studies on its conservation and ecological adaptations.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Transcriptomic and phenotypic data from patient-derived astrocytes in sporadic Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Astrocytes are essential regulators of central nervous system homeostasis and actively participate in the progression of neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer’s disease (AD). While familial AD (fAD) has been linked to defined genetic mutations, sporadic AD (sAD)-the predominant and more heterogeneous form-lacks clear causative mechanisms. Human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) offer a powerful platform to model sAD by enabling the generation of patient-specific neural cell types under controlled conditions. In this dataset, we present a detailed characterization of hiPSC-derived astrocytes from individuals with clinically diagnosed sAD and age-matched healthy controls. Cells were exposed to either aggregated amyloid-beta (Aβ) or hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) to mimic disease-relevant stressors associated with proteotoxicity and oxidative damage. We report (1) genome-wide transcriptional responses assessed by bulk RNA sequencing, (2) IL-6 cytokine secretion as a marker of inflammatory activation, and (3) phenotypic outcomes, including morphological alterations and cell viability. This dataset provides a valuable resource for investigating astrocyte-specific contributions to sAD pathophysiology and offers insights into how patient-derived astrocytes respond to key neurodegenerative triggers. The dataset also captures line-to-line variability in astrocyte maturation, providing users with information necessary for the appropriate interpretation of disease-related comparisons. All data, protocols, and metadata are openly available to support reproducibility and further exploration by the neuroscience and stem cell research communities.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: FAPROTAX2-db: A dataset of experimentally validated bacterial and archaeal metabolic functions
abstract: Culture-independent sequencing, including 16S rRNA marker-gene sequencing and metagenomics, has transformed our understanding of bacterial and archaeal diversity and highlighted the importance of prokaryotic metabolism in ecosystem functioning. Systematically collected records of experimentally verified microbial phenotypes are essential for properly interpreting these sequencing data in an ecological context, but existing databases of microbial phenotypes, including the widely used FAPROTAX, are either limited in taxonomic and ecological scope or are outdated. Here, we present the FAPROTAX2-db (Functional Annotation of PROkaryotic TAXa version 2) dataset, an overhaul of the original version that features a dramatically improved taxonomic breadth and resolution, reduced taxonomic and environmental bias, and additional metabolic functions. FAPROTAX2-db contains presence/absence data for >15,600 cultured prokaryotic species across 101 ecologically important functions, manually compiled from the experimental literature. We expect FAPROTAX2-db to expand our ability to analyze and model the taxonomic and phylogenetic distribution of microbial phenotypes, illuminate their relationships with genome content, and make phenotypic predictions for novel species.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Daily Clinical Parameters and Outcomes Adjudication Dataset for Critically Ill Patients with Suspected Pneumonia
abstract: Many analyses of critically ill patients focus on admission features and discharge outcomes, overlooking daily events and intercurrent complications. Pneumonia is a syndromic entity that is difficult to adjudicate outcomes without clinical expertise. Here, we examine clinical features on a day-by-day basis, mirroring the practice of daily multidisciplinary rounds, with annotated pneumonia episodes and outcomes. The Successful Clinical Response in Pneumonia Therapy (SCRIPT) CarpeDiem Dataset includes 21,931 patient-hospital-days from 704 patients enrolled in the SCRIPT study between June 2018 and May 2023. These patients were all receiving mechanical ventilation and underwent bronchoalveolar lavage to diagnose and establish the etiology of their pneumonia or an alternative diagnosis. The dataset captures patient demographics, daily clinical parameters, including vital signs, laboratory results, and mechanical support data, detailed pneumonia episode results adjudicated by critical care physicians, and outcomes. All data are de-identified per HIPAA Safe Harbor guidelines. This dataset offers a unique resource for analyzing the clinical trajectories of patients with severe pneumonia.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Text-mined dataset of sol-gel synthesis protocols with phase purity outcomes using large language models
abstract: Sol-gel synthesis is a versatile method for producing inorganic materials that offers advantages such as atomic-level mixing and lower processing temperatures over traditional solid-state methods. Despite these benefits, achieving phase purity remains a challenge due to the process’s sensitivity to synthesis parameters such as precursor choice, solvent selection, and heating conditions. Phase-impure outcomes are essential for understanding sol-gel reaction pathways, but are largely absent from existing curated datasets. This work leverages Gemini 3.0 Flash to construct a text-mined inorganic sol-gel database with phase purity information. The dataset contains ~148,000 synthesis records, including ~28,000 phase-impure entries. All extracted entities achieved F1 scores greater than 0.89. At the record level, 68% of extracted records match human annotation on all evaluated fields. Furthermore, to validate the scientific utility of our dataset, we demonstrate that the aggregated data reproduces previously reported phase-purity trends for BiFeO 3 thin films.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Quasi-global, land-only, high-resolution and spatially averaged climate variables from downscaled CMIP6 models for climate impact research
abstract: Global climate models (GCMs) are essential tools for understanding the climate system and projecting its evolution under different scenarios. However, differences in model construction introduce uncertainties, and GCMs have coarse resolution and inherent biases, limiting their effectiveness for informing local or regional adaptation and mitigation planning. We apply the statistical Double Bias-Corrected Constructed Analogues (DBCCA) method to generate bias-corrected and downscaled climate model outputs at daily and 0.1° spatial resolution for 1985–2100, with a specific focus on supporting tropical health-related impact research. Our quasi-global, high-resolution outputs are based on six GCMs from Phase 6 of the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP6) under two emission scenarios (SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5), covering 12 land-only domains between 60 °N and 60 °S. Moreover, many impact researchers rely on accessible data aggregated to administrative units, often weighted by population, rather than gridded data, as these align more directly with policy- and decision-making. Based on our bias-corrected and downscaled model outputs, we also provide user-ready (population-weighted) spatially aggregated climate variables at administrative unit levels (0-2) for 110 countries prioritized for tropical disease research.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Korean public documents for visual document retrieval benchmarking
abstract: Visual document retrieval is essential for interpreting information in complex layouts, yet benchmark resources for Korean public-sector documents remain scarce. This article presents a dataset comprising 361 Korean public administrative and legal documents totaling 40,781 pages. These documents contain tables, charts, diagrams, and multi-column layouts and were collected from official government and legal-information portals. To facilitate benchmarking, the dataset includes 600 query-page-answer triples balanced across six public-sector domains. The queries were generated using multimodal language models and subsequently validated by human experts for factual accuracy, evidence alignment, and contextual relevance. We categorize the queries as Text, Visual, or Cross-modal according to the location and modality of the evidence required to answer each query. This resource provides a standardized testbed for developing and evaluating retrieval systems for visually complex Korean documents.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of a cultivated tea tree (Camellia sinensis) cultivar Licha 5
abstract: Camellia sinensis is a globally important perennial crop plant cultivated for tea production. Here, we present a high-quality chromosome-level genome assembly of a cultivated tea cultivar named Licha 5, collected from Lishui, China. We combined PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing, Illumina short-read sequencing, and Hi-C scaffolding to assemble a 3.10 Gb genome comprising 15 pseudochromosomes. The assembly achieved a scaffold N50 of 210.39 Mb and a contig N50 of 149.87 Mb. Repeat elements account for 69.11% of the genome. A total of 54,995 protein-coding genes were annotated. This high-quality reference genome provides a valuable resource for tea tree genetic research, cultivar improvement, and evolutionary studies.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: An integrated national dataset of border interceptions of insects and newly recorded species in South Korea from 1996 to 2022
abstract: This dataset integrates nationwide records of insect interceptions and newly recorded insect taxa in South Korea from 1996 to 2022. It combines summaries of official border quarantine inspections with a curated list of national records linked to supporting publications. The interception component summarizes 159,709 interception records representing 1,350 species in six orders: Coleoptera, Hemiptera, Lepidoptera, Diptera, Thysanoptera, and Hymenoptera. The newly recorded taxon component contains 2,428 entries, including 1,861 dated 1996–2014 and 567 dated 2015–2022. Taxonomic names were standardized separately for the two components, and interception records not reliably identified to species level were excluded. National institutional databases were used to check nomenclature and documented occurrence. The released workbooks provide cumulative species-level interception counts, annual counts by insect order and commodity category, bibliographic records of newly recorded taxa, a curation log, and a commodity classification. These data provide a national resource for biodiversity, biosecurity, and quarantine research.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A multimodal dataset bridging brain activity, cognition, and real-world collective behavior
abstract: We present a multimodal dataset integrating brain activity, cognition, and real-world collective behavior using naturalistic video stimuli recorded in a controlled laboratory setting. The dataset includes 64-channel electroencephalography (EEG) recordings from 65 participants during narrative video viewing, multidimensional subjective evaluations spanning affective, cognitive, and social domains, and participant-level demographic and psychological trait measures. The stimulus set consists of videos organized across seven semantic themes and contrasting narrative perspectives (grand vs. individual). Importantly, each stimulus is associated with real-world engagement metrics, including play counts, likes, comments, danmaku, saves, and sharing behaviors collected from an online video platform. The dataset also includes raw and preprocessed EEG data, stimulus annotations, and preprocessing scripts. This resource supports research on naturalistic information processing, neural synchrony, narrative-related cognition, affective computing, computational social science, and neuroforecasting, and enables investigation of how individual neural and psychological responses relate to population-level behavioral patterns.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A chromosome-level genome assembly of the pygmy grasshopper Tetrix grossus, a resource for Tetrix systematics
abstract: Pygmy grasshoppers, family Tetrigidae, are a species-rich orthopteran lineage with substantial morphological variation, but genome resources for the group remain limited. Here, we report a chromosome-level genome assembly of the pygmy grasshopper Tetrix grossus , providing a genomic resource for Tetrix systematics and comparative studies of Tetrigidae. PacBio HiFi reads, Hi-C chromatin interaction data and RNA-seq data were integrated for genome assembly, scaffolding and annotation. The final assembly spans 1.247 Gb and contains 16 scaffolds, including seven chromosome-scale scaffolds corresponding to the haploid chromosome set. The assembly has a scaffold N50 of 155.07 Mb, a contig N50 of 29.59 Mb, GC content of 35.40% and a low ambiguous-base content. BUSCO analysis using the insecta_odb12 dataset recovered 97.0% complete orthologues, indicating high genome completeness. Repetitive elements occupy 36.33% of the genome, with LINEs and unknown repeats representing major components. We predicted 18,206 protein-coding genes, of which 84.72% received functional annotations, and the annotated proteome recovered 95.4% complete BUSCOs. Homology-based screening of structural RNA families further identified 4,115 non-coding RNA loci, comprising 4,058 transfer RNA, 36 ribosomal RNA and 21 small nuclear RNA loci and spanning 921,191 bp (0.07% of the assembly). This assembly provides a reference for species delimitation, chromosome evolution, repeat dynamics and comparative genomics in Tetrigidae.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Mitochondrial apoptosis imaged by high-throughput confocal microscopy
abstract: Mitochondrial programmed cell death (i.e. intrinsic apoptosis) is regulated through the formation of pro-apoptotic protein complexes at the mitochondrial outer membrane (MOM), which permeabilize the MOM and commit the cell to die. This step is modulated by mitochondrial dynamics. To capture this, we treated cells with the mitochondrial dynamics inhibitor M1 before inducing apoptosis with actinomycin D (ActD), and imaged them by high-throughput spinning-disk confocal microscopy. In mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) we followed apoptosis by long-term live-cell imaging, and in human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) we stained fixed cells for the pro-apoptotc protein BAX at mitochondria. Here, we provide a description of these two large-scale microscopy datasets. Dataset 1 contains 637,632 images of MEFs imaged as time series after labelling of mitochondrial morphology and integrity with the mitochondrial membrane potential-sensitive dye tetramethylrhodamine-ethylester (TMRE) and apoptosis with Annexin V-FITC. The dataset also contains a digital phase contrast channel which can be useful to track cells. Dataset 2 contains 9,504 images of hiPSCs with immunofluorescence labelling of BAX and COX IV. The datasets are made available through the BioImage Archive repository.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Ocular wavefront vergence coefficients and peak-to-valley normalised metrics in myopic eyes 2013–2025
abstract: We describe and share a de-identified clinical dataset of total ocular wavefront measurements acquired with the OPD-Scan III (Nidek) in myopic candidates for corneal refractive surgery without other reported ocular comorbidity, one preoperative examination per eye, comprising 1892 eyes from 1045 subjects. Wavefront error is provided as device-exported Zernike coefficients up to radial order 8, with several derived, clinically-oriented representations. From the Zernike expansion we compute an alternative low-order/high-order decomposition separating refractive from higher-order content, and vergence-function coefficients in diopters in two complementary bases: a fully orthogonal basis suited to unbiased summary statistics, and a partially orthogonal basis preserving the low-order/high-order separation. Oriented modes—those carrying an orientation, such as astigmatism, coma and trefoil—are additionally summarised by a magnitude and an axis. We also provide peak-to-valley normalised coefficients, each equal in diopters to the optical-power range the mode produces across the pupil (analogous to a clinical astigmatism amplitude). Coefficients are given at 3, 4, 5 and 6 mm pupils (6 mm reference; smaller pupils by analytical rescaling).
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Hourly Measurements of Moisture Content, Salinity, and Temperature from a Coastal Dune at Madeira Beach, Florida, USA
abstract: Coastal dune evolution is typically assessed as a function of external forcings (i.e., wind, wave runup, and vegetation growth). It is likely that there are also internal processes that influence dunes evolution. We deployed 5 moisture probes along a cross-shore transect in a dune at Madeira Beach, Florida, USA from January 25 – August 31, 2023. The probes collected hourly readings of moisture content, salinity, and temperature at depths ranging from 0.05–0.85 m in 0.10 m intervals. This dataset contains hourly readings from the moisture probes as well as coordinates for where the probes were located, collected using post-processed kinematic global navigation satellite system (PPK-GNSS). This dataset also includes 5-minute observations of wind speed, wind direction, gust speed, air pressure, rain, air temperature, relative humidity, and dew point that were collected from a meteorological station at Madeira Beach. The meteorological data can be used to assess the flux of moisture, salinity, and heat into the dune and as model input data (e.g., Aeolis) to analyze how it influences dune morphodynamics.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Rainfall, Streamflow, and Groundwater Dataset from a Complex Basin in Northeastern São Paulo, Brazil
abstract: Representative hydro(geo)logical studies are based on high-quality monitoring data. The water cycle’s inherent complexity, as well as its socioeconomic and ecological functions, is represented by a multitude of physical data that varies in space and time. This data descriptor provides ready-to-use hydro(geo)logical datasets of the complex Baixo Pardo Grande Basin, located in the northeastern part of São Paulo state, Brazil, within the Paraná Sedimentary Basin (PSB), from 1931 to 2025. The datasets include temporal and spatial data on rainfall, streamflow, and groundwater monitoring of the sandy, unconfined Bauru Aquifer System (BAS) and the sandy, confined Guarani Aquifer System (GAS). The datasets also include 2021 water demand data and groundwater level measurements. Rainfall and streamflow time series were evaluated using an Automatic Quality Control Procedure (A-QCP) and a Local Indicator of Spatial Association (LISA), which apply temporal and spatial analyses to identify years of poor-quality data. A confusion matrix was used to compare the methods, and the results showed that most of the high-quality years in both rain gauge records (90.1%) and streamflow station records (86.0%) were successfully identified. Moreover, this dataset provides novel data from a monitoring well in the confined portion of the GAS.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Comprehensive dRNA-Sequencing Dataset of Aβ42-Induced and APP/PS1 Transgenic Mice Modeling for Early Alzheimer’s Disease
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease involves complex transcriptional and post-transcriptional alterations that are incompletely captured by conventional short-read RNA sequencing. Here, we present an Oxford Nanopore direct RNA sequencing dataset generated from 24 mouse brain samples representing two complementary models of amyloid-associated pathology and their matched controls. The dataset comprises six biological replicates per group, including three males and three females: 8-week-old C57BL/6 control mice, Aβ1–42-injected C57BL/6 mice, 4-month-old C57BL/6 controls, and age-matched APP/PS1 transgenic mice. Native RNA was sequenced on the Oxford Nanopore PromethION platform, generating approximately 6.5–9.5 million reads and 8.0–10.8 Gb of sequence data per sample. Mean read lengths ranged from approximately 1.2 to 1.4 kb, with N50 values of 1.86–2.23 kb and mean read quality scores above Q19. Reads were aligned to the Mus musculus GRCm39 reference genome, with an average mapping rate of 88.2 ± 3.5%. The resource includes raw signal and basecalled sequencing data, genome alignments, transcript annotations, transcript abundance matrices, poly(A)-related outputs, and comprehensive sample metadata. Principal component and correlation analyses supported reproducibility among biological replicates and differentiation among experimental groups. This resource enables transcript- and isoform-level expression analyses, alternative splicing studies, poly(A)-tail profiling, RNA modification analyses, and comparative investigation of acute and chronic amyloid-associated molecular responses.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: High-quality haplotype-resolved genome assemblies of two phenotypically divergent strains of Lepista sordida (Basidiomycota), Hua8 and L-2
abstract: We report high-quality, haplotype-resolved diploid genome assemblies for two phenotypically divergent Lepista sordida strains, Hua8 and L-2. Using the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 and PacBio HiFi sequencing, we assembled two haplotypes per strain. Hua8 haplotypes measure ~49.06 Mb and ~44.33 Mb (total ~93.39 Mb), and L-2 haplotypes measure ~57.03 Mb and ~47.93 Mb (total ~104.97 Mb). Each assembly consists of 24 scaffolds with high continuity, exhibiting multi-megabase N50 values. Notably, 21 of the 24 Hua8 pseudo-chromosomes and 21 of the 24 L-2 pseudo-chromosomes achieved telomere-to-telomere (T2T) continuity, with canonical telomeric repeats detected at both ends of each of these chromosomes. BUSCO (fungi_odb10) completeness exceeds 99%, and Merqury QV scores are > 60 (Illumina) and > 70 (HiFi). We annotated 24,444 and 25,335 protein-coding genes in Hua8 and L-2, respectively, along with extensive non-coding RNAs and repetitive elements. These assemblies provide a genomic foundation for dissecting genetic diversity, trait regulation, and dikaryotic genome biology in L.sordida .
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Large-Scale Multi-Domain Unified Reverse Arabic Dictionary Dataset
abstract: Arabic is a linguistically and culturally rich language with a vast vocabulary that spans scientific, religious, and literary domains. However, large-scale lexical datasets linking Arabic words to precise definitions remain limited. We present MURAD (Multi-domain Unified Reverse Arabic Dictionary), an open lexical dataset with 96,243 word–definition pairs. The data come from trusted reference works and educational sources. Extraction used a hybrid pipeline integrating direct text parsing, optical character recognition, and automated reconstruction. This pipeline is designed to improve accuracy and minimize extraction noise. Its output undergoes validation through systematic quality checks and human review. Each record pairs a target word with its standardized Arabic definition and includes metadata specifying the source domain. The dataset encompasses terms from linguistics, Islamic studies, mathematics, physics, psychology, and engineering, supporting both computational linguistics and lexicographic research. Potential applications include reverse dictionary modeling, semantic retrieval, and educational tools. The release of this resource is intended to advance Arabic natural language processing and facilitate reproducible research on Arabic lexical semantics.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: An electricity smart meter dataset of Chinese households: insights into prosumers
abstract: This paper presents an electricity smart-meter dataset of Chinese households for prosumer identification and low-voltage distribution-system analysis. The dataset covers 15 low-voltage transformer areas in China from June 2025 to May 2026 and contains household net active power records for 2,162 households, including 620 prosumers and 1,542 consumers. It further provides household labels distinguishing prosumers from consumers, transformer-area membership, data-quality statistics, and hourly NASA POWER weather data matched to each transformer area. The dataset enables household-level comparisons between prosumers and consumers within the same local distribution context and comparative analyses across multiple transformer areas. Power data are released in a unified daily format with 96 time fields while retaining the original sampling information. Data quality is evaluated using completeness metrics, label plausibility checks, and irradiance–power consistency checks. The dataset can support prosumer identification, research on behind-the-meter photovoltaic generation estimation, and operational assessment of low-voltage distribution systems.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: The chromosome-level genome assembly of the Neotropical yellow-tailed tetra fish Astyanax lacustris (Teleostei: Characiformes)
abstract: Astyanax is one of the most diverse genera of characiform fishes and plays an important role in Neotropical freshwater ecosystems. However, high-quality genomic resources remain scarce for the group, with most available studies focused on the model species Astyanax mexicanus . Here, we present a high-quality chromosome-level genome assembly for the yellow-tailed tetra Astyanax lacustris , a widespread and ecologically important species from the upper Paraná River basin, Brazil. The final assembly spans 1.31 Gb, with a scaffold N50 of 49 Mb and 98.8% of the sequence anchored into 25 chromosome-scale scaffolds, corresponding to the expected haploid chromosome number. Assembly completeness was supported by 99.1% complete BUSCOs against the actinopterygii_odb12 dataset. This reference genome provides a valuable foundation for future comparative genomics, evolutionary studies, and conservation genetics of Neotropical fishes.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A red panda gut microbiome genome catalog from PacBio HiFi and short-read metagenomes and isolates
abstract: The red panda ( Ailurus styani ) is a bamboo specialist with a carnivore-like gastrointestinal tract; however, genome-resolved microbiome resources for this host remain limited. Here, we present a reference genome dataset for the red panda gut microbiome integrating short-read metagenomes, PacBio HiFi metagenomes, and cultured isolate genomes. We compiled 49 gut metagenomic datasets from four geographic regions, including 37 public and 12 newly sequenced Illumina metagenomes (nominal yield, 351.73 Gbp), and generated 9 PacBio HiFi metagenomes (203.63 Gbp). In parallel, culturomics across 12 fecal samples yielded 12,300 colonies, resulting in 51 isolates for whole-genome sequencing. Following quality filtering and additional taxonomic screening, a total of 551 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) and isolate genomes were jointly dereplicated at 99% average nucleotide identity (ANI), yielding 442 representative bacterial genomes (396 MAGs and 46 isolates). Across the representative genome set, median estimated completeness and contamination were 86.2% and 0.75%, respectively. The dataset provides a genome resource that supports taxonomic profiling and comparative genome-resolved analyses of the red panda gut microbiome.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A decade of disease survey data in a progeny-provenance trial: Dothistroma needle blight in Scots pine
abstract: Long-term data on disease susceptibility in forest trees are rare but essential for understanding host–pathogen dynamics and genetic variation in susceptibility traits. We present a multi-year, multisite common garden dataset quantifying susceptibility of Scots pine ( Pinus sylvestris ) to Dothistroma needle blight. The dataset comprises annual disease assessments collected from the same trees across 11 years, spanning 168 families and 21 Scottish provenances. This design enables partitioning of genetic and environmental sources of variation, evaluation of temporal stability in host response, and estimation of variance components and narrow-sense heritability of susceptibility. The data support analyses of phenotypic plasticity, provenance-level responses, and interactions between disease susceptibility and other adaptive traits. This data resource will facilitate predictive modelling of host susceptibility under current and future environmental conditions.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Synthetic Multi-modal Dataset for Type 2 Diabetes
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a widespread chronic disease that impacts multiple organ systems. Artificial intelligence (AI) has shown promise in advancing type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) research by enabling the integrated analysis of complex, multimodal data. However, progress is constrained by limited access to such multimodal datasets as contractual restrictions and concerns around patient privacy often limit the dissemination of existing resources. Here, we present the development and evaluation of a publicly accessible synthetic version of AI-READI, a large multimodal dataset for T2DM research. This synthetic dataset, constructed through generative AI, contains 93,856 retinal fundus images, 56,512 optical coherence tomography slices, and 10,518 tabular data records that combine clinical diagnoses, laboratory measurements, and data from wearable sensors. Our evaluation illustrates that the synthetic data captures many of the relationships within each modality of the original AI-READI dataset while being strongly resilient against membership inference attacks aimed at compromising participant privacy.
