This synthetic dataset is designed to support education, innovation, and reproducibility in T2DM research and is released under a permissive license that supports broader reuse than the original AI-READI dataset.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Biogeochemical time-series and surveys in the North Sea, Skagerrak and Kattegat, 1990 – 2024
abstract: This dataset contains biogeochemical samples analyzed by the Plankton Chemistry Laboratory at the Institute of Marine Research (IMR), from the North Sea, Skagerrak and Kattegat regions. The number of surveys and stations have varied greatly over the last 35 years. Generally, IMR usually conduct one annual Ecosystem Survey in April-May each year with trawl surveys and multiple net tows at selected stations, but only water sample collections are reported here. Three transects constitute the core of the time-series and are visited multiple times each year ( Torungen-Hirtshals , Utsira-West , Hanstholm-Aberdeen ). On each station, the CTD sampler collected seawater to determine dissolved inorganic nutrients (nitrate, nitrite, phosphate, silicate) and phytoplankton chlorophyll- a and phaeopigments (ChlA, Phaeo) at predetermined depths. At the Torungen-Hirtshals transect, and adjacent transects in the German Bight and in the Skagerrak-Kattegat region, an additional number of environmental samples, including dissolved ammonium (AMON) and Winkler oxygen (DOW), are also collected. This unique data set has seen limited use over the years but is a great contribution towards global ocean research and climate change investigations in these waters.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Multi Utility Dataset of Water and Energy Consumption from Spanish Residential Households
abstract: This paper introduces a household-level multi-utility dataset capturing one year of telemetry at a 7-minute sampling interval from 10 Spanish homes. Signals include cold and hot water volumes, electricity use, and thermal/HVAC (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning) measurements, complemented by an outdoor temperature probe. In addition to the household measurements, the dataset includes a complementary set of labelled lab-generated events recorded at a 1-minute sampling interval. The laboratory data reproduces common residential end-uses like showers (with varying durations and patterns), water closet (WC) flushes, and washing-machine programs aligned to the sensor streams. This resource enables exploration in anomaly detection, predictive modelling, disaggregation studies, activity recognition, and analysis of water-energy coupling.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: French urban tree dataset with age, dimensions and species
abstract: Urban trees deliver ecosystem services and generate environmental pressures that evolve over a lifespan of decades to centuries. Quantifying these effects over time relies on relationships between tree age and dimensions, yet most urban tree datasets record dimensions without age. This dataset presents 464,705 individual urban trees in France, compiled by harmonizing 16 municipal inventories published as open data by local authorities. Each record reports the contributing inventory, harmonized genus and species, the original taxonomic entries, diameter at breast height, height, estimated age, a location category, and coordinates, though completeness varies across records and inventories. Age is derived from planting dates recorded by the data producers rather than inferred from allometric models. Because the source inventories differ in survey protocol, every derived attribute carries a companion field recording how its value was derived during compilation, so analyses can be restricted to directly measured or reported values. The dataset can be used to calibrate age-to-dimension relationships for French and other European urban contexts, and to compare tree populations between cities.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A pan-transcriptome of cultivated peach (Prunus persica) and its wild relatives
abstract: Peach ( Prunus persica L.) is an important Rosaceae fruit crop and a model species for Prunus research. Although a peach graph pangenome has recently been reported, transcript diversity across cultivated peach and its wild relatives remains incompletely captured by a single reference annotation or by unspliced pangenome graphs. Here, we describe a peach pan-transcriptome resource built from 477 RNA-seq libraries representing 224 accessions, together with support from 217 whole-genome sequencing datasets. The dataset covers cultivated peach and four wild relatives: P. mira , P. davidiana , P. kansuensis and P. ferganensis . After de novo assembly, redundancy reduction, contaminant filtering, reference-based classification and genome-read support filtering, we obtained a non-redundant pan-transcriptome containing 29,622 genes, including 26,871 reference genes, 2,218 unannotated genes and 533 non-reference genes. BUSCO evaluation, read-support filtering and PCR amplification of selected genes were used for technical validation. This resource provides a practical dataset for comparative transcriptomics, presence/absence variation analysis and annotation improvement in peach.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A dataset of inter-county distances along the real-world highway and railway networks in the contiguous United States
abstract: Reliable information on transportation mode-specific distances between origin–destination pairs is essential to better understand and plan for freight transportation in the United States. However, such dataset is not available at fine spatial resolution. Here, we develop a data construction crosswalk by integrating geographic information system processing with network-based analysis to transform transportation infrastructure shapefiles into spatial networks and compute shortest-path distances between origin–destination pairs across scales. Through this crosswalk, we generate a dataset of inter-county distances [in miles] across real-world highways and railways in the contiguous United States, comprising over 15.2 million records. This dataset can serve as a more accurate benchmark for broad inter-county freight distances in practice, supporting further applications in transportation planning, infrastructure investment, and supply chain and logistics analysis at a granular spatial scale.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Paired Fundus and Optical Coherence Tomography Dataset for Neovascular Age-related Macular Degeneration
abstract: Accurate classification of macular neovascularization (MNV) subtypes and reliable prediction of anti-VEGF treatment response are essential for individualized management of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), yet existing public AMD-related datasets lack multimodal imaging with fine-grained, longitudinal annotations to support these tasks. Here we present PCO-nAMD , a rigorously curated dataset of P aired color fundus photography ( C FP) and optical coherence tomography ( O CT) images designed to facilitate multimodal research on MNV subtype classification and treatment response prediction in nAMD . The dataset comprises two subsets: PCO-nAMD_MNV provides paired baseline CFP and OCT images from 327 patients with expert-adjudicated labels for four MNV subtypes (Type 1, Type 2, Type 3, and Mix), while PCO-nAMD_Response, a subset of 101 patients, further incorporates annotated pre-treatment image biomarkers alongside four-tier treatment response labels (good, partial, poor, and non-response). To characterize dataset difficulty and benchmark its utility, we conducted evaluation experiments showing that both tasks remain highly challenging for state-of-the-art multimodal large language models (MLLMs), and that incorporating curated biomarker annotations alongside imaging data consistently yields the best performance in treatment response prediction for GPT-5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: TyphoonSat: A high-resolution satellite imagery dataset for tropical cyclone detection in the Northwest Pacific (2015–2024)
abstract: Tropical cyclones (TCs) in the Northwest Pacific pose significant threats to coastal regions, yet the lack of a standardized object-detection dataset hinders fair algorithm evaluation. We present TyphoonSat, a high-resolution satellite imagery dataset for TC detection spanning 2015–2024. It comprises 5390 Himawari-8/9 infrared cloud images (1601 × 1201 pixels, 5 km resolution) covering 100°E–180°E and 0°–60°N, with 7895 bounding-box annotations in YOLO format, derived from best-track records from the China Meteorological Administration (CMABST). The dataset supports coarse (all intensities regarded as one category) and fine-grained (six intensity levels) detection tasks. Benchmarks using YOLOv8 variants demonstrate strong performance for coarse detection (mAP@50 up to 0.923, CSI up to 0.791) and highlight challenges in distinguishing weak-to-moderate intensities, while SuperTY detection excels (CSI up to 0.609). This dataset provides a unified benchmark for TC detection and fosters advances in deep-learning-based meteorological remote sensing.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A dataset on radical and extremist attitudes in Europe
abstract: This dataset introduces the first cross-nationally validated measurement scales for left-wing and right-wing radicalism, and general political extremism, along with an implicit association test (IAT) for implicit political extremism in the Western world. It includes data from more than 18,000 participants collected through ten surveys conducted between 2022 and 2024 in France, Germany, Great Britain, Greece, Hungary, the Netherlands, and the United States. The dataset facilitates comparative analyses of the origins and consequences of radical and extremist attitudes across different political systems. Moreover, by linking attitudinal measures with behavioral indicators such as party support, it provides a foundation for examining how latent forms of extremism are translated into political action. Beyond extremism research, the dataset contributes to the broader study of democratic resilience, political polarization, and ideological belief structures.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Single-cell RNA sequencing dataset of hippocampus from mice of neuropathic pain at different time points
abstract: Chronic pain (CP) affects more than 30% of the global population and is often accompanied by significant cognitive impairments. Although an increasing number of studies have focused on the pathological mechanisms associated with chronic pain-induced cognitive impairments, most have concentrated on the stage after the onset of cognitive impairments. Currently, the course by which chronic pain induces cognitive impairment has not been fully reported. Therefore, single-cell RNA sequencing were conducted in this study in order to map the mice hippocampus altas before and after cognitive impairments induced by spared nerve injury (SNI) on days 3, 7, 14, and 21. After quality control screening, 53852 out of 64207 cells from 11 samples were retained for subsequent analysis. The reliability of the sequencing data was verified through analysis of various evaluation indicators and sequencing alignment rates. Preliminary analysis identified 16 major cell types in the hippocampal tissue, and differential expression analysis revealed transcriptomic changes in hippocampal cells following SNI model establishment, with these early transcriptomic changes being more pronounced in neurons. In summary, the data obtained in this study provide a valuable research basis for researchers to further explore the transcriptomic changes in the hippocampal region before and after pain-induced cognitive impairments.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Water quality data from the Paute and Jubones river systems of Ecuador
abstract: In Ecuador, the Paute river basin supports the generation of approximately 40% of the national electricity demand, yet studies on its ecological quality tend to be spatially or temporally limited. Moreover, the underlying raw data often remains unpublished and stored in personal or institutional databases. To counter this situation, we collected data from the Paute and Jubones river systems every three months over a two-year period (July 2023 – April 2025), amounting to a total of eight time points. The data record covers 67 unique stations and includes information on the aquatic habitat, the abiotic water quality status, the prevailing macroinvertebrate communities, and the presence of both dissolved and emitted greenhouse gases. Climate conditions varied considerably during this two-year period, as Ecuador experienced two severe droughts that affected the overall water supply and the associated energy production. Hence, the provided data can be useful for local water managers, scholars, and academics interested in the Andean headwater system under normal and exceptional circumstances.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Trace-IN625 a source aware literature derived dataset of tensile properties and microstructure for additively manufactured IN625
abstract: Additively manufactured IN625 superalloy has been widely studied, but evidence linking processing history, microstructure and tensile response remains dispersed across publications. We present Trace-IN625, a source-traceable, literature-derived dataset assembled from 305 papers. The dataset contains 482 specimen or source condition records, 149 tensile property records from 72 publications, 2206 microstructure and figure evidence records and 280 figure crops with source attribution. The tensile layer includes 120 IN625 records and 29 records for IN625-containing composite, graded or joined materials. Stable identifiers and page, figure, table and panel-level locators connect processing conditions, reported properties and published characterization evidence. Technical validation integrated AI assisted cross checking and manual review with verification of process condition classifications and measurement definitions, as well as relational consistency and file integrity checks. The image layer represents published figures and descriptors rather than instrument-native characterization data. Trace-IN625 supports source-aware property retrieval, condition-specific literature comparisons and inspection of published microstructural evidence.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A comprehensive transcriptome and metabolome dataset for Erigeron breviscapus (Asteraceae) response to different light intensities
abstract: Erigeron breviscapus is a widely utilized medicinal herb in traditional Chinese medicine, characterized by high annual demand and notable pharmacological activities. Light intensity is a critical environmental factor influencing secondary metabolism in medicinal plants. However, the effects of light intensity on the accumulation of active ingredients in E. breviscapus remain largely unexplored. In this study, we examined the transcriptomic and metabolomic responses of E. breviscapus to five levels of light intensity (50, 100, 200, 400, 800 μmol·m −2 ·s −1 ). The results revealed that higher light intensity (EB-L800) significantly increased the accumulation of scutellarin, chlorogenic acid, isochlorogenic acid A, and isochlorogenic acid C. A total of 1,334 metabolites were detected, and 127.10 Gb of high-quality clean data were generated through transcriptomic sequencing. This study elucidates the regulatory effects of light intensity on the levels of active components in E. breviscapus . The metabolite profiles not only lay a foundation for future investigations into light-regulated scutellarin biosynthesis but also provide preliminary theoretical references for the standardized cultivation and quality-oriented breeding of E. breviscapus .
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: An Accurate Land Cover Classification Map in China Integrating High-resolution Satellite Imagery and Planning Data with Deep Learning
abstract: This study presents a planning-oriented high-resolution land cover dataset for China, developed to address the limitations of existing products in territorial spatial planning and regional land analysis. The dataset integrates 2-m optical satellite imagery with official planning maps using a deep learning semantic segmentation framework based on ConvNeXt. It includes six land cover classes—built-up areas, cropland, roads, green spaces, water bodies, and others—and is designed to better align remote-sensing outputs with planning-relevant land categories. We conducted a comprehensive validation using pixel-level test-set evaluation, point-based assessment with an open-access validation dataset, and nationwide areal consistency analysis against aggregated results from China’s Third National Land Survey. The product achieved competitive classification performance and showed the strongest agreement with official area statistics among the compared datasets, particularly for built-up areas, cropland, and roads. Visual comparisons further demonstrate clearer boundary delineation and more realistic spatial patterns in both urban and rural settings. As a planning-oriented baseline dataset, this product is particularly useful for built-up land accounting, cropland protection assessment, urban–rural spatial analysis, road-network extraction, and regional policy evaluation in situations where up-to-date survey data are unavailable. Its combination of high spatial resolution, strong semantic consistency, and nationwide coverage makes it valuable for both research and practical decision-making in China’s territorial spatial planning.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A bias-corrected & downscaled massive ensemble to diagnose uncertainty in climate impact projections
abstract: Projections of climate change and climate impacts require bias-corrected, downscaled output from ensembles of earth system models (ESMs). Potential impacts are uncertain due to modeling differences between ESMs, internal variability stemming from the chaos of the earth system, and differences in the historical reference datasets used to bias-correct and downscale ESM output. Here, we introduce the Bias-Corrected and Downscaled Massive Ensemble (BCD-ME), a multi-model large ensemble of over 1,400 projections of daily mean and maximum temperature. The BCD-ME samples model and internal uncertainty with up to 86 runs from 12 CMIP6 Large Ensembles and uncertainty in the reference dataset by using 4 different reanalysis products to bias-correct and downscale output. Output is organized by Global Warming Levels (GWL), accounting for differences between forcing scenarios and ESM climate sensitivities. The ensemble contains 20-year daily time series for each GWL on a uniform 1° grid, bias-corrected using Quantile Delta Mapping, and statistics of 20-year time series for each GWL on a uniform 0.25° grid, downscaled using Quantile-Preserving Localized Analog Downscaling. The BCD-ME is stored in Analysis-Ready, Cloud-Optimized (ARCO) Zarr stores, enabling efficient computation of the 97 TB (uncompressed) dataset.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Global, depth-resolved marine fish occurrences from digitized natural history collections
abstract: Digitized natural history collections provide an important foundation for repeatable, transparent, large-scale biodiversity research. However, depth information associated with marine specimens is frequently heterogeneous, inconsistently formatted, and difficult to fit for use in quantitative analyses. Here we present a curated, depth-resolved global dataset of preserved marine ray-finned fishes (Actinopterygii) derived from the iDigBio data aggregator. Raw occurrence records were filtered to include preserved specimens with geographic coordinates and taxonomic identification, then taxonomically harmonized. Depth values were standardized through regular-expression parsing of verbatim entries, unit conversion, reconciliation of minimum and maximum reported depths, and bathymetric validation using a global relief model. After removal of terrestrial and depth-inconsistent records, the final dataset comprises 354,622 specimen records representing more than 11,294 species collected between 0 and 8,000 meters depth across all major ocean basins. These data provide a depth-explicit basis for macroecological, biogeographic, and conservation-oriented analyses of marine fish biodiversity and our open-source workflow serves as a template for future work using heterogeneous natural-history-specimen-derived data sources.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A multi-source dataset for solar energetic particle forecasting
abstract: Solar energetic particle (SEP) event forecasting often involves integrating heterogeneous observations that differ in cadence, temporal coverage, format, and historical availability, posing challenges for reproducible analysis of data-driven approaches. This paper presents SEP-PRISM Data , a curated multi-source dataset designed for 24-hour-ahead forecasting of operational SEP events, defined as proton flux exceeding 10 pfu in the GOES > 10 MeV channel. SEP-PRISM Data integrates flare records, active-region magnetic field parameters, coronal mass ejection (CME) catalog data, GOES soft X-ray flux, and historical proton flux into a common window-based representation spanning 3 February 1986 to 10 September 2025. To improve temporal coverage and cross-source consistency, SHARP and SMARP magnetic products were aligned into a unified SMHARP archive, and CME records from DONKI and CDAW were aligned into a unified CDAWDONKI event set. Predictor variables were summarized over fixed non-overlapping 24-hour historical windows using minimum, mean, and maximum statistics and paired with targets defined over the subsequent 24-hour window, forming a supervised learning dataset. The resulting SEP-PRISM Data contains 14,464 labeled samples, including 650 positive operational SEP cases, and is intended to support reproducible benchmarking, model development, feature analysis, and future studies of space weather forecasting.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A high-quality chromosome-scale genome assembly of Erythrophleum Fordii
abstract: Erythrophleum fordii Oliv ., a valuable rosewood species of Fabaceae native to southern China, Vietnam and Laos, boasts multiple economic, medicinal, ornamental and ecological values. This endangered IUCN-listed plant faces poor natural regeneration due to limited seed dispersal and habitat fragmentation, and the absence of chromosome-level genome data also hinders studies on its genetics, adaptive mechanisms and the progress of conservation and molecular breeding. Here, we construct a high-quality chromosome-scale reference genome for E. fordii using integrated sequencing data. The final assembled genome size is 886.3 Mb with a contig N50 of 60.2 Mb, and 98.2% of the assembled sequences are anchored to 14 pseudochromosomes. A total of 33,237 protein-coding genes are predicted, of which 96.4% (32,044) are functionally annotated. This high-continuity and high-accuracy genome provides a valuable genomic resource for future studies on adaptive evolution, population genetics, germplasm conservation and genetic improvement of E. fordii .
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A visible light-thermal infrared multimodal image dataset collected from a real greenhouse tomato cultivation scene for flower and fruit detection
abstract: The rapid development of machine vision has promoted the automation of crop monitoring, providing technical support for planting management. For this purpose, this paper constructs a visible light-thermal infrared multimodal image dataset for the detection of flowers and fruits of facility tomatoes: it includes 300 images of the flowering period and 343 images of the fruiting period collected by the H982 visible light camera, as well as 145 images of the fruiting period collected by the HIKMIC thermal infrared camera. The LabelImg tool is used to complete the bounding box annotation of tomato flowers, fruits, and fruit maturity. Based on the evaluation of YOLOv11 (n/s/l) and YOLOv13 (n/s/l), the optimal mAP50 for the flower subset can reach 89.86%, while the optimal mAP50 for the fruit subset and the entire dataset is above 84%. The overall detection accuracy is excellent, indicating that the dataset is practical. The multimodal fusion experiment shows that compared with single visible light, the fusion strategy significantly improves the detection performance without sacrificing the inference efficiency almost at all, verifying the complementarity of thermal infrared and visible light, and providing data support for the research and deployment of intelligent monitoring algorithms for facility tomatoes.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the molluscivorous Conus textile
abstract: Conus textile , a representative molluscivorous cone snail, primarily preys on some marine mollusks and thus represents a carnivorous gastropod with a highly specialized ecological niche. Compared with piscivorous and vermivorous Conus lineages, C. textile displays unique clade-specific features in venom composition, arrangement of toxin-related gene superfamilies, and pharmacological activities of its venom. To facilitate biological, evolutionary and pharmacological investigations, we employed an integrated strategy by combination of Illumina short-read, PacBio HiFi long-read, and Hi-C sequencing technologies to construct a chromosome-level genome assembly for C. textile . The final assembly spanned 2.15 Gb, with a high scaffold N50 of 60.12 Mb. Notably, the assembled haploid sequences were successfully anchored onto 35 chromosomes, representing 98.66% of the total genome length with a good BUSCO completeness of 93.29%. Repetitive sequences accounted for 62.25% (1.34 Gb) of the entire assembly, and we predicted a total of 30,055 protein-coding genes, among which 27,901 (92.83%) were assigned putative functional annotations based on sequence homology. Therefore, this high-quality genome assembly of C. textile can not only serve as a valuable genomic resource (being the first reference for molluscivorous cone snails), but also provide a solid basis for elucidating the adaptive evolution of diverse cone snails and promoting the translational development of endogenous conopeptides into novel clinical therapeutics.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Complete Telomere-to-Telomere Assembly of the Y Chromosome in the Chinese Quartet
abstract: The complete assembly of the human Y chromosome remains a formidable task due to its highly repetitive, palindromic, and heterochromatic architecture. While complete telomere-to-telomere (T2T) assemblies have recently been generated for select individuals, high-quality, gapless Y chromosome references for East Asian lineages—specifically within well-characterized multi-omics reference cohorts—remain scarce. The Chinese Quartet (CQ), comprising monozygotic twin daughters and their parents, represents a premier national reference material system for genomic standardization. However, because the female offspring inherited their father’s X chromosome rather than his Y chromosome, previous pedigree-based T2T assemblies (CQ v3.2) lacked a gapless Y chromosome sequence. Here, we present a complete, gapless T2T assembly of the Y chromosome (designated CQ_chrY) from the father of the CQ. This assembly was generated by integrating Oxford Nanopore Technologies ultra-long reads, PacBio high-fidelity reads, and Hi-C data, resulting in a sequence of 68.50 Mb. The assembly shows exceptional base accuracy (QV = 57.54) and structural assembly quality (CRAQ AQI = 99.781). We completely resolved the 40.09 Mb Yq12 heterochromatic region, a ~940 kb centromeric higher-order repeat array, and annotated 96 protein-coding gene models evaluated against GENCODE/T2T-Y standards, alongside 57.59 Mb (84.07%) of repetitive elements. CQ_chrY serves as a complementary paternal resource extending the CQ reference platform, providing a robust foundation for population genetics, structural variation analysis, and East Asian genomic standardization.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Genomes from Coleus comosus and an interspecific hybrid facilitate taxonomic classification
abstract: Coleus comosus Hochst. ex Gürke is an East African semi-succulent herb widely cultivated for remedial uses and ornamental landscaping. The rich specialised metabolite contents of C. comosus and closely related Coleus species have attracted considerable biochemical interest, but difficulties with accurate identification of species within the genus have hindered the systematic investigation and accurate identification of bioactive constituents. We provide two genome assemblies: a contig-level C. comosus genome assembly and a pseudochromosome-level genome assembly of an interspecific hybrid Coleus accession ( Coleus comosus x Coleus neochilus ). The C. comosus genome assembly spans 1.57 Gb with a contig N50 of 96.52 Mb. The hybrid Coleus genome is fully phased to 30 pseudochromosomes which sum up to 2.60 Gb, with its scaffold N50 reaching 86.9 Mb. Both genome assemblies are highly complete at the gene level; the C. comosus genome has a BUSCO completeness score of 98.9% and the genome assembly of the hybrid Coleus accession scored 99.2%. These two genome assemblies provide a foundation for future studies into specialised metabolic pathways and taxonomic classification within the genus Coleus .
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Multi-Omics Dataset of Heat Stress-Induced Memory in Arabidopsis
abstract: In their natural environment, plants experience temperature fluctuations, including intensified heat waves driven by climate change, which pose significant threats to their productivity. To adapt, plants have evolved diverse mechanisms to withstand heat stress (HS), minimizing potential damage and ensuring survival. One such adaptation is acquired thermotolerance (AT), in which prior exposure to HS primes plants to withstand subsequent severe HS. AT can persist for several days and involves a recovery period during which plants establish heat stress memory (HSM), reorganize cellular processes, and strengthen stress resilience. The molecular mechanisms underlying HSM remain an active area of investigation. This dataset provides high-throughput comparative multi-omics data, including the transcriptome, metabolome, and proteome of Arabidopsis thaliana seedlings at distinct intervals during the HSM phase. As the first detailed multi-omics dataset of the HSM phase in Arabidopsis seedlings, it serves as a valuable resource for future research aimed at identifying regulators of heat stress resilience and advancing the development of heat-tolerant crops.

title: A ubiquitinome and proteome dataset of the red alga Gracilariopsis lemaneiformis under cold stress
abstract: Low temperature is a major environmental factor constraining the growth and aquaculture performance of the red alga Gracilariopsis lemaneiformis , yet systematic protein-level data describing cold stress responses remain limited. Ubiquitination is a key post-translational modification involved in regulating protein stability and turnover during stress adaptation. Here, we present a paired dataset of the global proteome and the ubiquitin-modified proteome of G. lemaneiformis under cold stress, generated using a matched experimental design across identical conditions. This paired dataset provides a valuable resource for future investigations of the relationship between protein abundance changes and ubiquitination regulation during cold-stress responses. We further provide detailed technical validation demonstrating high data quality and strong reproducibility among biological replicates. These datasets constitute a valuable resource for investigating ubiquitination-associated protein homeostasis during cold adaptation, facilitating the identification of ubiquitination-regulated substrate candidates under cold stress, and supporting downstream functional studies as well as the breeding of cold-tolerant G. lemaneiformis strains.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Arabidopsis nanopore direct RNA sequencing data for mutants in splicing, polyadenylation, and m6A methylation
abstract: Co-transcriptional RNA processing, including alternative splicing and polyadenylation, generates diverse mRNA isoforms essential for development, differentiation, and stress responses. We present Oxford Nanopore Direct RNA Sequencing (DRS) data from Arabidopsis thaliana wild-type (Col-0) plants and mutants defective in RNA processing pathways, including polyadenylation, RNA methylation, and pre-mRNA splicing. We obtained full-length reads together with native poly(A) tail information. The provided resources include FAST5 and FASTQ files, poly(A) tail length estimates from Nanopolish, poly(A) composition data from Ninetails, and differential expression analyses generated with DESeq2, all aligned to the TAIR10 reference transcriptome. These data offer a comprehensive view of RNA processing at the single-molecule level and can be reused to explore alternative polyadenylation, RNA modification patterns, or indirectly, splicing alterations across various genetic backgrounds. This resource is intended to support studies of gene expression regulation and RNA metabolism in Arabidopsis thaliana and related plant systems.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Characterizing the NIH-funded data resource landscape: resource types, functions, access models, and funding
abstract: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) invests substantially in data resources supporting biomedical data sharing, curation, discovery, and reuse. Yet the structure, functions, access models, and funding patterns of these resources have not been systematically characterized. We conducted a cross-sectional inventory of 105 NIH-funded domain-specific data resources listed in NIH’s data sharing catalog as of April 2026. We classified resources by their scientific scope, functional characteristics, access and submission policies, and NIH affiliations. Funding for 2015–2025 was estimated using publicly available data, NIH catalog metadata, and NIH RePORTER. Resources varied substantially in structure and function; primary data repositories were the largest category, and data archival and harmonization were the most common functions. Funding rose from approximately $322 million in 2015 to a peak of $517 million in 2024, with the National Library of Medicine (NLM) accounting for the largest share. This inventory characterizes the NIH data resource landscape and identifies considerations for data sharing policy, governance, infrastructure sustainability, and future efforts to improve data findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reuse of data.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Multi-Model Large Ensemble Dataset of Global Hydroclimatic Stress Indices
abstract: Understanding the frequency, variability, and uncertainty in drought and atmospheric moisture stress across historical and future states requires large ensembles that capture both internal variability and the externally forced response. Here we present a new dataset of hydrometeorological stress indices derived from large ensemble simulations of two Earth system models: the Community Earth System Model version 2 (CESM2) and the Energy Exascale Earth System Model version 2 (E3SMv2). It includes daily vapor pressure deficit (VPD) and Keetch-Byram Drought Index (KBDI), and the Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) for 1-, 3-, 6-, 9-, and 12-month accumulation timescales. The dataset combines output from the 100-member CESM2 and the 21-member E3SMv2 ensembles, covering the historical period (1850–2014) and the future SSP3-7.0 scenario (2015–2100). All indices are provided in analysis-ready formats to support investigations of large-scale hydrometeorological stress and their spatial and temporal characteristics, the relative contributions of internal variability and externally forced change, and subsequent application-specific analyses with appropriate bias correction and downscaling.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: The chromosome-level genome assembly of Sakhalin surf clam, Spisula sachalinensis
abstract: The Sakhalin surf clam Spisula sachalinensis is a large cold-water bivalve with high economic, ecological and evolutionary significance, serving as an important aquaculture resource, an eco-environmental indicator for marine conditions, and a non-model organism for studying longevity mechanisms. However, the lack of comprehensive genomic resources has hindered evolutionary studies and molecular breeding research. Here, we report a high-quality chromosome-level genome assembly for S. sachalinensis , generated by integrating PacBio HiFi sequencing with Hi-C scaffolding. The genome assembly spans 865.03 Mb and is anchored to 19 chromosomes, with a scaffold N50 of 46.40 Mb and 38.23% repeat content. Gene annotations yielded 23,982 predicted protein-coding genes, and BUSCO assessment revealed 97.8% completeness of metazoan conserved genes. Synteny analysis revealed deeply conserved synteny between S. sachalinensis and the presumed bilaterian ancestor (CI = 0.785) and nearly perfect genome-wide collinearity with Spisula solida , indicating strong genomic preservation and limited interchromosomal rearrangements within the genus Spisula . Phylogenetic analyses placed S. sachalinensis as most closely related to S. solida , from which it diverged approximately 39.27 Mya. This high-quality genome fills a critical gap in the genomic resources for this species, providing a valuable foundation for understanding its environmental adaptations and evolutionary traits and serving as an essential resource for the molecular breeding of sustainable aquaculture.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: VentVirGenomes: A Global Ocean Hydrothermal Vent Virus Genome Dataset for Exploring Diversity, Function, and Host Interactions
abstract: Ocean hydrothermal vents constitute chemically driven oases of life that fundamentally differ from photosynthesis-based ecosystems. Recognized as one of Earth’s most extreme environments, they serve as key systems for investigating the origins of life. To elucidate the still poorly understood diversity of viruses and virus–host interactions in these settings, we analyzed 405 globally distributed metagenomic samples from ocean hydrothermal systems across seven habitat types and depths ranging from 0 to 5000 m. From these data, we constructed the Global Ocean Hydrothermal Vent Virus Genome Dataset (VentVirGenomes), which comprises 392,166 viral contigs and 332,833 viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs). Taxonomic classification at the realm level could be estimated for 68.37% of these vOTUs, with Caudoviricetes representing the dominant class. Furthermore, we identified 79,317 predicted virus-host linkages. The VentVirGenomes provides a foundational resource for advancing research into the diversity, evolution, and ecological functions of viral and microbial communities within global hydrothermal vent ecosystems.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Key Officers of U.S. Foreign Service Posts: A Dataset of U.S. Diplomatic Representation, 1966-2017
abstract: Diplomats have long played a crucial role in facilitating interstate relations: they negotiate international treaties and agreements, facilitate commerce, settle disputes, and generally represent their home governments abroad. Yet, due to a lack of administrative data on diplomatic personnel, extant scholarship has studied almost exclusively the highest-ranking bilateral diplomats—ambassadors—while neglecting the vast majority of the foreign policy bureaucracy. We introduce KOFSP, a dataset of all individuals designated by the State Department as the “key” officers at American diplomatic posts from 1966-2017. We collect this data from digitized directories. These consistently capture the senior leadership at diplomatic posts and the mid-ranking officers leading major administrative subunits within posts. Over time, the State Department designated additional “key” positions and the coverage grows beyond this, encompassing about a quarter of all American diplomats in the later years. We use record-linking record-linking techniques to track over 35,000 unique diplomats throughout their careers. We also provide data on the name, location, and category of post at which each diplomat was serving, as well as information about the position that they occupied at the post. We validate this data through comparison to other sources. KOFSP stands to substantially advance the study of diplomacy, foreign policy, and bureaucratic career advancement.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A global ionosonde dataset of validated foF2 observations for the May 2024 Mother’s Day superstorm
abstract: The May 2024 Mother’s Day superstorm offers a rare opportunity to document the global ionospheric response to an extreme geomagnetic disturbance using ground-based ionosonde observations. Here, we present and describe a manually validated dataset of the F2-layer ordinary critical frequency ( fo F2) observations recorded by 38 ionosonde stations distributed across high, mid, and low latitudes from 10 to 14 May 2024, covering both the main and recovery phases of the storm. The dataset was produced through a careful inspection and validation of individual ionograms, overcoming limitations of automatic scaling procedures that can become particularly unreliable during disturbed ionospheric conditions. To our knowledge, this is the first time that such a large collection of fo F2 observations has been compiled for an extreme event such as the May 2024 Mother’s Day superstorm. The availability of this validated fo F2 dataset provides a high-quality benchmark for investigating storm-time ionospheric dynamics, assessing ionosonde autoscaling performance, and evaluating empirical and assimilative ionospheric models under extreme space-weather forcing.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A large-scale expert-annotated 3D image dataset of dermal tissue macrophages
abstract: Tissue macrophages are highly versatile immune cells whose morphologies shift dramatically depending on their activation state and tissue environment. This morphological plasticity reflects their diverse origins and functions but also poses significant challenges for both manual and automated image analysis. In the skin, macrophages display particularly intricate shapes, ranging from rounded to highly elongated, irregular, and non-convex forms. We developed a deep learning–based approach for the automated identification, 3D segmentation, and quantitative morphological profiling of dermal tissue macrophages in mice, facilitating large-scale analysis of cellular volume and elongation. This allowed us to build a dataset of 3D-segmented dermal tissue macrophages, comprising 947 single cells. To ensure accuracy, automatically generated segmentations were refined using a custom-designed Napari plugin. To illustrate technical validity and potential reuse, we quantified macrophage volume and elongation in adult steady-state and five-day post- Staphylococcus aureus infection samples, showing that the dataset captures biologically interpretable morphological variation.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A CT-based 3D pelvic anatomy dataset of 99 healthy Chinese subjects for anatomical landmark detection
abstract: Accurate automated pelvic anatomical landmark identification for intelligent surgical applications has been limited by the lack of high-quality, standardised 3D data. To address this need, we developed a curated dataset of 99 high-resolution pelvic CT cases from Chinese subjects, comprising CT volumes, segmentation masks, 57 clinically defined anatomical landmark coordinates, pelvic surface meshes (STL files), and reference point clouds. Dataset quality was assessed through annotation completeness, pelvic geometric descriptors, landmark–surface alignment, STL mesh quality checks, and intra- and inter-operator annotation reliability. All cases contained the complete 57-landmark set. The mean distance between the left and right anterior superior iliac spines (ASIS) was 228.5 ± 18.2 mm, and the mean landmark-surface distances were 0.21 mm for cortical landmarks and 1.54 mm for intra-pelvic landmarks. Regeneration of the STL meshes eliminated the detected topological defects with minimal change in enclosed volume. The resulting multimodal dataset provides a reusable resource for developing and evaluating pelvic landmark detection, anatomical measurement, pose estimation, and surgical planning methods.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Labels for automated step recognition in cataract surgery for videos in the Cataract-1K dataset
abstract: We provide surgical step annotations for all 1,000 videos in the publicly available Cataract-1K dataset of phacoemulsification cataract surgery. We manually labeled 386 videos using an annotation protocol with explicit boundary criteria for 10 surgical steps. Manual annotations demonstrated excellent inter-annotator reliability (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.994–1.000; mean intersection over union 0.980–0.993). Using the manually annotated videos, we trained five state-of-the-art deep learning models for surgical step recognition and localization and generated pseudo-labels for all 1,000 videos. We release the manual annotations, model-predicted pseudo-labels, and associated prediction probabilities through a publicly accessible repository. These data products, alongside our annotation protocol and statistical evaluation methodology, serve as a resource for developing context-aware systems for cataract surgery and as a guidance for annotation of steps and statistical evaluation of large surgical video datasets.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A multimodal biomechanics and electromyography dataset of drop vertical jump under virtual-reality visual height perturbations in individuals with and without chronic ankle instability
abstract: Chronic ankle instability (CAI) is associated with altered sensorimotor control during jump–landing, but open biomechanics datasets rarely combine clinically relevant cohorts with controlled visual perturbations. We present a multimodal drop vertical jump dataset from 28 young adults (12 with CAI and 16 non-CAI controls). Participants completed one real-world 30-cm condition and four virtual-reality (VR) visual-height conditions (0, 10, 30 and 50 cm), while physical drop height remained 30 cm. Kinematic data and ground reaction forces were synchronously recorded for all participants, and bilateral surface electromyography (EMG) from six lower-limb muscles is available for 17 participants (6 with CAI and 11 non-CAI controls). The EMG acquisition protocol was designed to capture task-evoked muscle activity during high-velocity drop vertical jumps, with separate maximum voluntary isometric contraction (MVIC) assessments outside its scope. The released EMG signals were band-pass filtered by the acquisition hardware but remain unrectified and unnormalized. Participant-specific MVIC reference measurements are not available for amplitude normalization. Motion-capture data were acquired using a 38-marker Plug-in-Gait–compatible set. The resource contains labeled and quality-checked C3D files, format-converted TRC, MOT, and ASCII files, anonymized metadata, an OpenSim model, and a MATLAB kinematic-processing script. Metadata include group classification, limb dominance and affected side, demographics, anthropometrics, body composition, and bilateral lower-limb morphometrics. The dataset can support secondary analyses of landing biomechanics, neuromuscular responses to visual-height perturbations, and musculoskeletal-modeling workflows.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A telomere-to-telomere gap-free genome assembly of the protogynous hermaphrodite rice field eel (Monopterus albus, Synbranchidae)
abstract: Monopterus albus (rice field eel) is a key economic fish in East and Southeast Asia. Its unique protogynous sequential hermaphroditism (first female, then male) makes it an ideal model for research on sex determination and differentiation in vertebrates. With nutrient-rich and delicious meat, it also holds high economic value in aquaculture. In this study, we integrated PacBio HiFi, Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) ultra-long reads, and Hi-C sequencing technologies to complete the first gap-free telomere-to-telomere (T2T) chromosome-level genome assembly of M. albus . Spanning 838.56 Mb with a contig N50 of 70.71 Mb, the assembly is anchored to 12 chromosomes each of which contains complete telomeres and centromeres. It contains 45.45% repetitive sequences, with 25,035 protein-coding genes annotated. Genomic quality was further validated by a Quality Value (QV) of 46.93 and 98.20% BUSCO completeness. This high-quality T2T genome provides precise genetic resources for deciphering the molecular regulatory mechanisms of sex reversal in M. albus and identifying key sex-control genes, while laying the foundation for its molecular breeding and superior germplasm creation.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: An openly available OpenStreetMap-to-Foursquare category benchmark for points of interest
abstract: The heterogeneity of Point of Interest (POI) taxonomies is a persistent challenge for the integration of urban datasets and the development of location-based services. OpenStreetMap (OSM) adopts a flexible, community-driven tagging system, while Foursquare (FS) relies on a curated hierarchical structure. Here we release an openly available, manually validated benchmark dataset that links 1,205 OSM tags to full FS category paths, from broad thematic groups down to fine-grained labels. By making these two widely used but previously unconnected sources interoperable, the dataset enables consistent, multi-scale analyses of urban functions and can be downloaded and reused as a high-precision resource. The dataset is complemented by an automatic alignment procedure, combining text embeddings with LLM-based refinement, whose code we release to support scalable updates of the benchmark as OSM evolves. Together, these elements provide both a robust reference resource and a practical tool for the community. The benchmark is manually curated and validated to serve as a high-quality gold-standard reference, with direct applications to urban analytics, mobility studies, and smart city services.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Small non-coding RNA profiling in the hippocampus of mice with postoperative cognitive dysfunction
abstract: Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) commonly affects elderly surgical patients and is associated with impairments in memory, attention, and executive function that can substantially reduce quality of life. The precise pathogenesis of POCD remains unclear, although trauma-induced epigenetic mechanisms have been implicated. Conventional sequencing methods are hindered by reverse-transcription arrest at modified RNAs, which may result in the underrepresentation or loss of small noncoding RNAs (sncRNAs) with important regulatory functions. Here, we applied panoramic RNA display by overcoming RNA modification-induced aborted sequencing (PANDORA-seq) to generate a comprehensive profile of highly modified sncRNAs in the hippocampus of mice with surgery-induced cognitive impairment. The dataset profiles the composition of hippocampal sncRNA classes—including miRNAs, tsRNAs, rsRNAs, and piRNAs—in control and surgery-exposed mice during the early postoperative period. We performed sequencing quality-control analyses and, as an orthogonal, assay-level check on selected sequencing signals, quantified selected tsRNAs by qRT-PCR. Structural mapping of these tsRNAs to their parental tRNAs was also performed. Overall, this resource provides a foundation for investigating neuroepigenetic changes associated with early postoperative cognitive impairment and for generating hypotheses regarding the molecular mechanisms of POCD.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Global forest typology at 10-meter resolution for forest and land-use monitoring
abstract: Distinguishing forest types—primary, naturally regenerating, planted, and plantation forests—from agricultural tree crops and other land uses is essential for carbon accounting, biodiversity assessment, conservation planning, and supply-chain regulation. However, no existing global dataset resolves this typology at high spatial resolution. We present the Forest Typology (ForTy) v1 dataset, a global 10-meter resolution baseline map for 2020 that classifies all land into six categories aligned with FAO and EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) definitions: Primary Forest, Naturally Regenerating Forest, Planted Forest, Plantation Forest, Tree Crops and Agroforestry, and Other Land. A cascaded deep learning pipeline, trained on 1.7 million globally distributed samples, generates per-class relative confidence maps from geospatial satellite embeddings by combining weakly supervised learning with active learning. Independent validation against 8,190 expert-labeled stratified random sites yields an overall accuracy of 90.2% for the six-class scheme, 94.8% for natural forest classification, and 95.5% for forest/non-forest classification.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Beyond the catch: Survey data on the human dimensions of commercial fishing in England
abstract: A thriving fishing industry, that sustains livelihoods whilst sustainably exploiting marine resources, requires policy and management decisions that consider social sustainability objectives alongside environmental and economic objectives. Currently there is no robust monitoring of social conditions and the motivations and attitudes of commercial fishers in the UK. To address this gap, we compiled a dataset from a survey on a sample (N = 435) of the commercial fishing vessel owners and skippers in England. The survey collected data on respondents’ fishing activity, job satisfaction and job security, perception of and engagement with fisheries management, health and wellbeing and demographic profile. Analyses of these data will enable scholars, policymakers, fisheries managers and the fishing industry to gain valuable insights about the social conditions and opinions of English commercial fishers and will provide a baseline for future longitudinal surveys to monitor change in social conditions over time. Such data will contribute to delivery of the ‘social sustainability’ objective of the Fisheries Act (2020).
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Correction: Characterizing organisms from three domains of life with universal primers from throughout the global ocean
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Experimental modeling of gusty bora windstorms
abstract: Bora is a non-synoptic downslope severe windstorm characterized by severe wind gusts. While it commonly occurs all around the world, bora origins and turbulence have been predominantly studied at the eastern Adriatic coast. The bora mean wind velocity rarely exceeds 17 m/s. However, its maximum gust velocity can reach up to five times the average wind velocity, i.e., 70 m/s and more. Due to its gusty and unpredictable nature, bora wind may cause substantial damage and failure to infrastructure, traffic and agriculture. In the present work, three bora simulation approaches are developed in the unique WindEEE Dome Research Facility at the Western University, Canada: a) a rapidly increasing/decreasing angular velocity of the fans yielding generic oscillations between the base- and gust-flow velocity, b) a scaled-down reproduction of the bora velocity time record, previously observed on a meteorological mast, by adjusting the angular velocity of the fans, and c) a concurrent application of the constant horizontal boundary-layer flow and the downburst flow. Flow velocity profiles in all three directions were measured using seven Cobra probes on a stiff mast. In total, 140 experiments were performed, the most comprehensive and unique laboratory dataset regarding bora wind thus far. This study outlines the novel experimental approaches developed for this purpose and the respective dataset.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A multiparametric liver MRI dataset with multiple tumor and liver segmentations of pre-treatment hepatocellular carcinomas
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common primary liver cancer and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. While dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) plays a key role for HCC screening, diagnosis and treatment planning, the development of AI models for detection and characterization of focal liver lesions is hindered by the scarcity of publicly available annotated MRI datasets. Here, we present OpenSwissHCC, a curated multiphasic dataset of 132 multiparametric DCE-MRI scans from adult patients with chronic liver disease acquired on 1.5 T and 3 T MRI scanners between 2011 and 2020. The dataset includes both HCC-positive (n = 63) and HCC-negative (n = 69) patients, with up to five lesions per patient segmented across each sequence when confidently identified. Whole-liver and lesion segmentations were manually performed and expert-validated, with lesion metadata including LI-RADS scores, size, liver segment location, major LI-RADS imaging features (non-rim APHE, washout, capsule, threshold growth) and key ancillary/background findings (e.g., mosaic architecture, fat/blood products, necrosis, tumor-in-vein; cirrhosis and portal-hypertension signs). In total, 140 lesions were annotated, including 97 confirmed HCC. Additionally, we provide liver masks for all T1-weighted images (T1-WI) sequences, generated using a pre-trained nnU-Net model, as well as pre-computed transforms to facilitate registration across T1-WI phases. By providing a comprehensive, well-annotated, and standardized collection of liver MRI examinations, OpenSwissHCC aims to assist the development and benchmarking of advanced computational methods for automated HCC detection, segmentation, and characterization, fostering progress toward precision imaging and personalized treatment planning.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Combined Dataset of Road Accidents on the D1 Motorway in the Czech Republic (2025) with Average Annual Daily Traffic (AADT) and Spatial Attributes
abstract: This paper presents a combined and processed dataset of road accidents on the D1 motorway in the Czech Republic for the year 2025, enriched with Average Annual Daily Traffic (AADT) and spatial road attributes. The dataset integrates three primary data sources: police-reported road accident records 1 , a national road network database 2 , and traffic census data 3 . Unlike the original source datasets, which are distributed separately and use different spatial structures, the presented dataset provides a unified sector-based representation by harmonising accident locations, traffic exposure, and road infrastructure characteristics into common spatial units. To enable high-resolution spatial analysis and future integration with additional road-related attributes, including regulatory information, the motorway geometry was divided into uniform sectors of approximately 10 m in length, which serve as the fundamental spatial units. Each sector contains aggregated information on accident occurrence, traffic volume by vehicle category (passenger vehicles, light commercial vehicles, heavy vehicles, and motorcycles), and road infrastructure characteristics, including the number of lanes, road width, and local curvature derived from angular changes between consecutive sectors. The dataset is structured into four directional segments corresponding to the two main parts of the D1 motorway and their respective travel directions. Due to licensing restrictions, only the processed and integrated dataset is provided; however, all original data sources are publicly accessible and referenced. The dataset is made available through the Mendeley Data repository 4 to ensure transparency and reproducibility.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Multi-Scenario UAV RF Dataset with Real-World Acquisition and Signal Processing Benchmarking
abstract: We present a real-world multi-scenario unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) radio frequency (RF) dataset, namely DRFF-R2, which is collected using a dedicated acquisition platform under diverse operational conditions. All signals are acquired within a unified framework to ensure consistency in hardware configuration and environmental settings. The dataset is systematically organized into seven well-defined subsets corresponding to different operational and signal composition scenarios to facilitate structured experimentation. Each file follows a clearly annotated naming convention to enable convenient data indexing and reproducible analysis. The dataset contains RF recordings from 26 UAV units spanning 8 distinct models, captured across varying flight states, altitudes, speeds, acquisition days, and receiver configurations. By covering diverse acquisition settings and signal compositions, the dataset provides a comprehensive resource for future UAV RF signal research, including RF fingerprinting (RFF) identification, model-level recognition, flight state analysis, time-varying RFF study, and interference-aware signal processing.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A single-nucleus multiomic high-resolution atlas of the Mus musculus spleen
abstract: The spleen is a central organ for systemic immune surveillance and is especially important in mouse models to study infection, vaccination, and inflammatory disease. However, a high-resolution single cell reference for the murine spleen has been lacking. Here we present a single-nucleus multiomic atlas using same-cell single-nucleus RNA-seq and single-nucleus ATAC-seq profiling of 12 adult C57BL/6 mouse spleen samples. After extensive filtering, we retained 41,823 highest-quality nuclei for both assay modalities. Integrated analysis identified 46 fine-grained cell populations spanning lymphoid, myeloid, erythroid, fibroblast, endothelial, and mesothelial types, including diverse B cell, T cell, dendritic cell, macrophage, and fibroblast subpopulations. These cell populations were annotated through careful literature-guided curation of the spleen and related immune tissues, including canonical transcriptional markers, protein markers, and signatures obtained from single-cell expression profiles. Chromatin accessibility profiles showed lineage-consistent promoter accessibility. This publicly available dataset provides a comprehensive multiomic reference for the murine spleen, supporting transcriptomic and epigenomic studies of immunity and translational modeling of human disease.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Pre- and postoperative multi-sequence MRI-CT and pathological feature dataset
abstract: Brain gliomas represent the most prevalent primary malignancies of the central nervous system, characterized by marked invasiveness, frequent recurrence, and significant intratumoral heterogeneity. These characteristics pose significant challenges to achieving precise diagnosis, accurately assessing prognosis, and developing personalized treatment plans. Clinical practice requires the comprehensive integration of multimodal imaging information and pathological features to improve diagnostic accuracy, relies on longitudinal comparisons of preoperative and postoperative images to enhance prognostic assessment, and combines structured clinical information, image data analysis, and pathological classification features to guide personalized treatment. Although studies based on single-modality imaging or isolated molecular data have made some progress, publicly available datasets that simultaneously integrate complete pre- and post-operative multi-sequence MRI and CT images, systematic molecular pathological profiles, and structured clinical information remain limited. This study curated a disease-specific dataset comprising 63 cases of adult glioma, encompassing WHO grades I–IV and classified according to the 2021 WHO Classification of Central Nervous System Tumors (CNS5), providing pre- and post-operative paired T1, T2, T1-weighted contrast-enhanced, T2-weighted FLAIR, and CT sequences. The dataset covers key molecular pathological features including isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1) mutation status, 1p/19q co-deletion status, O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) promoter methylation status, epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) amplification, α-thalassemia/mental retardation syndrome X-linked (ATRX) expression, and the cell proliferation index (Ki-67). It also integrates structured clinical information such as WHO classification and grading, detailed medical history, surgical records, immunohistochemistry results, overall survival, and survival status. All data have undergone standardized preprocessing, strict de-identification, and systematic organization. This dataset is intended to support the development of glioma imaging algorithms and the investigation of image-molecular correlations, thereby advancing precision medicine research in this field.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: An atlas of gene expression in the adult female domestic goat (Capra hircus)
abstract: Atlases of gene expression are an essential resource to connect transcript abundance and structure with tissue biology. The goal of this study was to build a comprehensive atlas of gene expression in adult female domestic goats ( Capra hircus ). To this end, we have extracted and sequenced total RNA from 33 tissues retrieved from six Murciano-Granadina goats. On average, more than 54 million paired-end raw reads (2 ´ 150 bp) per sample were obtained, and 92.5% of them were successfully aligned to the goat reference ARS1 genome. Downstream analyses were performed to ensure the quality of the atlas of gene expression generated with the procedures mentioned before. Sample clustering revealed 7 outliers, which were eliminated from the data set. Moreover, a second PCA demonstrated that functionally related tissues tended to group together, forming well defined clusters, while strong transcriptional signatures were observed for encephalic, muscle and hypophyseal tissues. These findings are highly consistent with previous reports and provide evidence about the high reliability of the transcriptomic resource generated in the current work.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: An Annotated Rip Current Image Dataset for Benchmarking Rip Current Detection
abstract: Rip currents are a common coastal hazard and the leading cause of beach-related drownings worldwide. However, their dynamic and variable appearance makes them difficult for beachgoers to identify, highlighting the potential of automated rip current detection tools for operational beach safety. To support the development and evaluation of rip current detection algorithms, we present a comprehensive dataset comprising 7,541 finely annotated images for training and validation, together with 24 annotated test videos containing 16,212 frames, resulting in a total of 23,753 annotated images. The images were collected from diverse locations along the Australian coastline under a range of acquisition conditions, including varying camera viewpoints, camera types, illumination conditions, and environmental settings. The dataset provides three types of instance-level annotations for each rip current: horizontal bounding boxes, oriented bounding boxes, and polygons. In addition, each image is assigned observation perspective tags in both the vertical and horizontal directions, and each rip current is categorized into one of three common subtypes: channelized, boundary, and flash rip currents. To establish benchmark performance, we evaluate several widely used state-of-the-art object detection models on the dataset. We anticipate that this dataset will serve not only as a benchmark for rip current detection but also as a valuable resource for advancing research on rip current monitoring and coastal safety.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Human-reviewed Rooftop Photovoltaic Annotations Initialized by a Vision–language Model
abstract: Variation in rooftop interpretation limits reliable models for photovoltaic (PV) assessment. We present RoofeNet-Multi, comprising 12,761 annotation sets for 5,359 building-centered Czech orthophoto tiles. The release contains 7,402 human review outputs and one matched Google Gemini proposal per image. Every human task began from that image’s proposal, after which the reviewer could edit, delete, or add boxes; human outputs are therefore not independent of the VLM or one another. Each set uses a common schema of axis-aligned boxes for flat/pitched roof planes and rooftop obstructions. Coverage is uneven: 1,502 images have at least two human outputs and 3,857 have one. The multi-reviewer subset supports analysis of review variation conditional on shared initialization. The full release supports image-space detection and provenance-aware human–AI comparison, but lacks georeferencing and polygon geometry for engineering-grade PV potential estimation.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Haplotype-resolved chromosome-level genome assembly of Alpinia officinarum Hance
abstract: Alpinia officinarum Hance is a medicinal and edible plant whose secondary metabolites possess significant pharmacological value. However, the lack of genomic resources has hindered a comprehensive understanding of this species and constrained its breeding efforts. In this study, we integrated PacBio HiFi, Illumina paired-end (PE), and high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) sequencing data to construct the first haplotype-resolved, chromosome-level reference genome of A. officinarum Hance. The resulting assembly achieved a contig N50 of 51.42 Mb, with the two haplotypes spanning 2.08 Gb and 1.99 Gb, respectively, and anchored onto 48 chromosomes. Repetitive sequences accounted for 82.04% and 81.02% of the two haplotypes, respectively, and 31,605 and 31,438 protein-coding genes were predicted, respectively. This high-quality genomic resource provides a solid foundation for genomic and genetic studies of A. officinarum Hance and related Zingiberaceae species, and also facilitates future haplotype-based breeding efforts.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Carbon footprint and energy-related performance indicators of Mediterranean and Black Sea trawl fisheries
abstract: Spatially explicit information on fuel consumption and energy efficiency is essential for evaluating the climate-related and economic performance of trawl fisheries, yet such data are rarely available at regional scales. This Data Descriptor presents four harmonised spatial datasets describing fuel consumption, fuel costs, and energy-related performance indicators for Mediterranean and Black Sea trawl fisheries during 2013 to 2022. The datasets integrate fleet-segment economic data from the EU Annual Economic Report with spatially resolved fishing effort and landings from the Fisheries Dependent Information database, using a reproducible framework that allocates fleet-segment fuel consumption and costs to spatial fishing grounds according to the distribution of fishing effort and landings. Indicators include Energy Consumption, Energy Costs, Fuel Use Intensity, Energy Use Intensity, and Fuel Efficiency, reported on a 0.5° c-square grid. The four products provide energy indicators at increasing levels of aggregation, ranging from datasets disaggregated by fishing technique, gear type, and vessel length to datasets summarised across all trawl fleet segments within each c-square grid. Spatial patterns of energy consumption were independently validated using Automatic Identification System data combined with empirically derived fuel-consumption relationships to reconstruct fuel use. These datasets provide a consistent spatial representation of energy use to support spatial analyses, modelling applications, and assessments of energy efficiency and decarbonisation strategies.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Single-cell short- and long-read transcriptomic atlas of seven male reproductive-axis tissues from the Baoshan pig (Sus scrofa)
abstract: The male reproductive axis coordinates neuroendocrine regulation, spermatogenesis, sperm maturation, and accessory gland secretion, whereas paired single-cell short- and long-read transcriptomic resources spanning this system remain limited in pigs. Here, we generated single-cell short-read and long-read transcriptomic datasets from seven reproductive-axis tissues, including the hypothalamus, pituitary, testis, epididymis, vesicular gland, prostate gland, and bulbourethral gland, collected from an 18-month-old Baoshan boar. Integrating the short-read data, we retained 76,398 cells and resolved 10 major cell types across the seven tissues, thereby providing a cell-type framework for cross-tissue comparison. In parallel, analysis of the long-read data identified 158,048 full-length transcripts, enabling transcript structure characterization and isoform identification at single-cell resolution. Together, these datasets provide a cell-type-resolved resource for investigating gene expression, transcript diversity, and cell-type-specific splicing features across the porcine male reproductive axis.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Telomere-to-telomere gapless genome assemblies of Coreius heterodon and Coreius guichenoti
abstract: Coreius heterodon and Coreius guichenoti are endemic cyprinid fishes of the upper Yangtze River Basin. C. guichenoti is classified as Endangered (EN) by the IUCN and listed as a national second-class protected wild animal in China, whereas C. heterodon is classified as Not Evaluated (NE) by the IUCN. However, genomic resources for these species have remained limited, constraining evolutionary and conservation genetic studies. Here, we present near telomere-to-telomere genome assemblies for both species. The assemblies span 1.09 Gb for Coreius heterodon and 1.08 Gb for Coreius guichenoti , with contig N50 values of 43.10 Mb and 42.62 Mb, respectively, and are anchored to 25 chromosomes. Repetitive elements account for approximately 58% of each genome, and 25,876 and 25,778 protein-coding genes were annotated, respectively. Both assemblies exhibit exceptional completeness, with BUSCO scores exceeding 98.9%, confirming their high quality and reliability. These genome assemblies provide high-resolution resources for future studies on genome evolution, adaptive diversification, and conservation genomics of endemic fishes in the Yangtze River Basin.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A labeled dataset for resource scheduling in heterogeneous IoT-fog-cloud computing systems
abstract: Fog computing brings computation closer to IoT devices to reduce latency, but assigning tasks to the right execution node demands scheduling decisions that are difficult to automate without labeled training data. Machine learning-based schedulers require such labels, yet publicly available datasets either carry no assignment labels, record only post-execution metrics, or assign binary tier labels that discard node-level information. This paper describes FogMLS, three labeled tabular datasets generated by a genetic algorithm scheduler with greedy initialization across a three-tier IoT-fog-cloud simulation, modeling three heterogeneous fog nodes and a cloud server. Three load configurations are deposited under fixed random seed 42, each spanning 5,000 scheduling slots. The primary high-load dataset contains 404,919 task-resource assignments across 200 task positions per slot, with pre-execution features encoding task type, instruction count, data size, and the live remaining capacity of each fog node at scheduling time, alongside GA-derived node assignment labels. A Random Forest classifier achieves 76.35% overall accuracy across four scheduling classes with consistent results across seeds 42, 123, and 456 (76.14-76.35%), confirming that the labels carry sufficient signal for training a scheduling model.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A UAV Imagery Dataset of Potential Aedes aegypti Mosquito Breeding Containers
abstract: To facilitate the surveillance and control of mosquito-borne diseases, proper identification of potential mosquito breeding containers is significant to support public health. Aedes aegypti is one of the major urban mosquito species that breeds in artificial containers, including drums, tanks, discarded tires, and small home receptacles, and transmits diseases such as dengue, chikungunya, Zika, and yellow fever. This data descriptor presents a UAV-generated image dataset depicting potential mosquito breeding containers collected in several urban and peri-urban areas of Tamil Nadu, India. The aerial images were captured at altitudes of 50–65 meters above ground level and processed photogrammetrically to create orthomosaic, which were subsequently divided into 512 × 512 image tiles to enable standardized annotations. Five types of containers, namely coconut shell, drum, tire, water tank, and other containers were manually annotated using bounding boxes. The dataset is available in COCO, YOLOv8, and Pascal VOC formats, with predefined training, validation, and test splits.
