A baseline object detection experiment was conducted to demonstrate the usability of the dataset. This dataset supports studies on the automated identification and detection of potential mosquito breeding containers in UAV imagery.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Canadian fractional landcover maps from 1985 onward
abstract: Canada’s northern ecosystems are undergoing rapid environmental change driven by climate warming, shifting disturbance regimes, and vegetation transitions. However, national-scale datasets describing non-treed and sparsely treed environments remain limited. This study presents a pan-Canadian dataset of annual fractional landcover at 30-m spatial resolution for the period 1985–2025, extending the Spatialized Canadian National Forest Inventory (SCANFI 1 ) framework to include both treed and non-treed surface components. The dataset integrates imagery from Landsat, Sentinel-2 and Very High-Resolution data to estimate the annual fractional cover of water, rock, soil, burn scars, lichen, herbaceous vegetation, low shrubs, tall shrubs, broadleaf trees, and coniferous trees. Fractional estimates were produced using machine learning techniques and harmonized within a vertical surface projection framework to ensure that all pixel-level components sum to 100%. The resulting dataset provides temporally consistent information for monitoring vegetation dynamics, post-disturbance recovery, and land-surface composition across Canada.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A Comprehensive Digital Pathology Dataset for Liver Cancer Research
abstract: Liver cancer, especially hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), imposes a substantial global disease burden. Accurate diagnosis and prognostic assessment directly influence treatment selection and patient survival, and pathological examination remains the gold standard for liver cancer diagnosis. Identifying diverse tissue components and pathological subtypes on histopathology slides is crucial for estimating postoperative recurrence risk and overall prognosis. However, most publicly available liver cancer histopathology resources are provided solely at the whole-slide image (WSI) level, and high-quality, finely annotated datasets for granular tissue component identification remain scarce. This lack of specialized annotated data severely hinders reproducible analytical research, standardized quantitative evaluation, and fair comparative analysis in liver cancer pathological studies. To address this critical gap, we present HepatoBench, a publicly accessible patch-level image dataset for liver cancer histopathology with rigorous manual annotations covering seven key tissue categories. The dataset is constructed from clinical liver cancer histopathological slides, with standardized patch cropping and professional pathological annotation procedures to ensure high data quality and clinical relevance. We provide complete benchmarking protocols and supporting auxiliary resources for dataset utilization, enabling standardized data evaluation and consistent analytical validation. HepatoBench offers a dedicated, fine-grained data foundation for liver cancer histopathological research, supporting robust and reproducible quantitative analysis and unbiased method comparison in liver cancer pathology studies.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Resting-state EEG recordings with clinical and medication data from individuals with myotonic dystrophy type 1
abstract: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) is a rare, multisystem neuromuscular disorder with well-documented central nervous system involvement, including cognitive, behavioral, and sleep-related symptoms. Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a non-invasive, scalable measure of brain function that complements MRI-based markers, yet publicly available EEG data for DM1 remain scarce. We present a curated dataset of resting-state EEG recordings and rich accompanying metadata from 29 individuals with genetically or clinically confirmed DM1. Each participant completed a standardized EEG session (target duration ~15 minutes) using a wireless dry-electrode system, with recording duration varying across participants; data were structured according to the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS-EEG) standard. The release includes raw EDF files, preprocessed EEG derivatives, subject-level quality-control summaries, and de-identified participant-level measures capturing demographics, sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale), sleep habits, recent caffeine exposure, medication class summaries relevant to arousal, and cytosine-thymine-guanine (CTG) repeat length binned for privacy. This resource provides a foundation for identifying EEG-derived central nervous system markers that align with patient-reported symptoms and supports reproducible development and evaluation of analysis pipelines for rare-disease clinical research and future therapeutic studies.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: TrussGraph: A dataset of graph-based trusses for machine learning and structural design applications
abstract: Traditionally, reticulated (truss) structures and conceptual structural design models are abstracted as minimal equilibrium systems composed of nodes and bars in compression or tension. Such abstractions are naturally mapped onto graph formulations (G = V, E) enriched with structural attributes. As a result, only minimal post-processing is required to prepare these data for Graph Neural Network (GNN) workflows. Despite rapid advances in GNN and their increasing adoption in structural engineering, there is a lack of publicly available, well-documented, and reproducible datasets relevant to this domain. To address this gap, we present a curated dataset of symmetric, planar structural truss configurations that includes geometric, topological, and performance-related metrics, while remaining material-agnostic, and thus supporting applications across diverse materials (steel, timber, etc.) and cross-sections. The dataset includes 917098 data points generated using Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS). Each structure is digitized as a human-readable JSON file, representing a feature-rich object whose attributes can be extended or modified using the provided codebase. The dataset enables multi-level investigation–from geometry and topology to performance and efficiency. This data descriptor details the ontology of the dataset, demonstrates its utility through preliminary analyzes, and highlights the broader need for similar datasets.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: European multi-trial data set on carbon and nitrogen isotope ratios of winter wheat spanning 170 years
authors: Marcel G. A. van der Heijden
abstract: Long-term and multi-site datasets are essential for understanding crop responses to environmental variability and management practices, yet such data remain scarce, particularly for physiological indicators. Here, we present a harmonized dataset of analyses of stable carbon (i.e., δ 13 C values) and nitrogen (i.e. δ 15 N values) isotope ratios from winter wheat samples collected across ten long-term and short-term field trials in Europe. The dataset spans over 170 years (1850–2024) and includes sites in Switzerland, France, Germany, Denmark, and the United Kingdom. Samples originate from experiments encompassing unfertilized controls, mineral and organic nitrogen fertilization at multiple rates, and contrasting management systems, including conventional and organic practices. Grain samples were available for all selected years, with straw samples included when available. In addition to isotope ratios, the dataset provides harmonized management information, including sowing and harvest dates, nitrogen inputs, and yield data. Technical validation confirmed that management records and isotope ratios are agronomically and physiologically plausible and internally consistent across sites and years. This dataset offers a unique resource for investigating long-term (genotype by) environment by management interactions, benchmarking crop models, and conducting comparative analyses of carbon and nitrogen dynamics in European agroecosystems.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A wearable respiratory dataset spanning clinical and asymptomatic adults
abstract: Respiratory diseases require assessment, yet conventional techniques such as spirometry are restricted to clinical settings and unsuitable for continuous monitoring. Wearable respiratory sensors offer an alternative; however, datasets enabling comparison across sensing modalities remain limited. We present a multimodal respiratory dataset comprising synchronised recordings from respiratory inductive plethysmography (RIP), piezoelectric (PZT), and force-based belt sensors. Data were collected from 104 adults, including 53 asymptomatic participants and 51 participants recruited during clinical respiratory assessment. **The clinical-recruitment label indicates recruitment context rather than confirmed disease, while asymptomatic status was self-reported.** The protocol included normal breathing, controlled breathing, reading, walking, and spirometry manoeuvres. The dataset contains 37.8 hours of recordings, with 1,358,955 synchronised samples per sensor channel, alongside metadata, spirometry-derived reference measurements, and analysis scripts. No missing numerical samples were identified; signal quality was assessed during and after acquisition. Cross-sensor validation demonstrated activity- and sensor-pair-dependent waveform similarity, with highest correspondence during normal breathing and greater divergence during walking and speech-related breathing. The dataset supports respiratory pattern recognition, multimodal sensor comparison, and wearable monitoring research.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Synchronized overnight polysomnography–radar dataset for sleep apnea–hypopnea analysis of 60 participants
abstract: Apnea–hypopnea events are clinically diagnosed using overnight polysomnography (PSG), the gold standard for evaluating sleep stages and respiratory events. However, PSG requires multiple contact-based sensors and laboratory infrastructure, limiting its scalability for home or large-scale monitoring. Contactless radar sensing has emerged as a promising alternative; however, publicly available datasets containing synchronized full-night PSG and raw radar measurements remain limited. We present a synchronized overnight dataset comprising 60 participants who underwent full-night PSG alongside continuous radar acquisition. The dataset includes epoch-level sleep stages, thoracic and abdominal respiratory effort signals, heart rate, breathing rate, and event-level annotations following clinical scoring guidelines. Annotated events include obstructive apnea, hypopnea, respiratory effort–related arousal, oxygen desaturation, snoring, arousal, and leg movements. Raw radar measurements are provided as time-aligned multi-frame data. All modalities are temporally aligned with compensated timestamps to support cross-modal analysis. Technical validation demonstrated a strong linear association between radar-derived and PSG-derived AHI over the synchronized radar–PSG analysis interval (r = 0.862), with Bland–Altman analysis used to further assess agreement.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Hydropower Site-level Monthly Availability Data Ensemble for 1950–2100 at Existing and Potential Global Sites
abstract: There is a growing demand for time-series data on hydropower availability at the site level, particularly to enable detailed investigation of the evolving role of hydropower in power grids. Such a dataset for both existing and potential hydropower sites, with global coverage, and incorporating future uncertainty, is still not available. Here, we present HydroSMADE (Hydropower Site-level Monthly Availability Data Ensemble) v1.0, a new open dataset that provides monthly hydropower availability for 1,593 existing and 124,333 potential sites worldwide over the period 1950–2100. The dataset is generated by using a global hydrologic model (Xanthos) with explicit representation of hydropower operations. Specifically, HydroSMADE distinguishes between storage and diversion sites, applies optimized operating rules, and incorporates site-specific characteristics such as generation capacity, maximum turbine flow, and reservoir storage. Driven by bias-corrected meteorological inputs, the site-level hydropower availability data is provided for 30 alternative future scenarios. Technical validation demonstrates consistency with reference datasets and literature across spatial scales, while highlighting improvements in representing operational differences between storage and diversion sites.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A dataset of the European fishing fleet and maritime infrastructure
abstract: We present the European Fishing Fleet Knowledge Graph (EFFKG), a provenance-aware semantic dataset integrating heterogeneous maritime data describing the European fishing fleet and the contextual maritime infrastructure required to represent vessels, ports and administrative relationships. Maritime information in Europe is fragmented across international standards, European registries, and national administrative systems, limiting interoperability and cross-source analysis. The dataset integrates vessel registries, fishing gear classifications, geospatial resources, and administrative datasets from authoritative sources, including detailed national-level data from Spain, within a unified Wikibase-based data model. The current release contains approximately 191,000 entities and 3.7 million statements linking vessels, ports, fishing areas, classifications, and administrative entities. Provenance is preserved at the statement level, enabling traceability of integrated values and transparent representation of source-specific discrepancies. Technical validation confirmed high structural consistency, complete referential integrity, and provenance coverage of 99.99% of all statements. The dataset is publicly available through RDF serialisations, Wikibase JSON exports, and a public SPARQL endpoint, supporting fisheries monitoring, maritime governance, and cross-source maritime data analysis.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: China’s Public Livelihood Concern Index for Education, Employment and Healthcare (2011–2023)
abstract: We release a 2011–2023 panel dataset of public livelihood concern indices derived from messages submitted to China’s Leadership Message Board. Annual observations cover national, provincial, and prefectural levels and three domains: education, employment, and healthcare. The domains comprise six subdimensions: basic education, higher education, pre-employment, post-employment, routine healthcare, and catastrophic healthcare. After field standardization and duplicate control, each subdimension index equals the number of deduplicated messages with at least one lexical match, divided by valid messages and multiplied by 100. Domain and overall indices are additive composites. The release includes a balanced panel of 4,966 rows in CSV and XLSX formats, annual high-frequency terms, a stopword list, a 357-term feature-word dictionary, and executable processing and validation code. Validation covers formula and aggregation reconstruction, denominator and temporal robustness, comparisons with official provincial statistics, and sensitivity to independently documented events. The dataset can support longitudinal, cross-regional, external-linkage, and policy-evaluation studies of expressed livelihood concerns.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: The chromosome-scale genome assembly of the reef-building coral Platygyra daedalea
abstract: The genus Platygyra represents an essential group of reef-building corals in marine ecosystems. Here, we present the first high-quality genome assembly of the brain coral Platygyra daedalea , a widespread species known for its ecological resilience across diverse marine environments. Using long-read sequencing combined with chromosomal-level scaffolding based on a genetic linkage map, we assembled an 878.6 Mb genome with a contig N50 of 34.8 Mb (7.C.Q66). A total of 99.78% of the assembly was anchored into 16 linkage groups, with only eight contigs remaining unplaced. Annotation identified 27,516 protein-coding genes. This reference genome provides a critical resource for understanding coral biology, aiding conservation efforts, and exploring adaptive potential under climate change.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A cone-beam computed tomography dataset for three-dimensional detection of temporomandibular joint osseous abnormalities
abstract: Temporomandibular disorders are common orofacial conditions that can impair mastication, speech, and quality of life. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is widely used to evaluate osseous structures of the temporomandibular joint (TMJ), but identifying subtle degenerative changes is time-consuming and requires specialist expertise. Although artificial intelligence (AI) may improve the efficiency and standardization of TMJ CBCT assessment, progress is limited by the lack of large-scale datasets with expert labels and three-dimensional localization annotations for TMJ osseous abnormalities. Here, we present an expert-annotated CBCT dataset for three-dimensional (3D) detection of TMJ osseous abnormalities. The dataset contains 1,043 de-identified TMJ CBCT examinations from 1,043 patients, covering 2,086 left and right joints. Each joint was independently annotated using a side-specific, multi-label scheme for common osseous abnormalities, including cortical erosion, subchondral sclerosis, subchondral cystic changes, osteophyte formation, and condylar flattening. Temporomandibular joint osseous-abnormality detection in 3D (TMJ-OD3D) provides joint-level labels and side-specific 3D bounding boxes, encoded as a two-dimensional rectangle on a representative Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) slice together with the corresponding axial slice range. All annotations were generated through a multi-step expert consensus workflow involving oral and maxillofacial surgeons. The released dataset includes de-identified DICOM image series, structured JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) annotations, and patient-level metadata, providing a reusable resource for developing and benchmarking AI models for TMJ abnormality classification, localization, and 3D object detection.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Panel data on mobility, socio-economic, and political impacts of riverbank erosion and flooding in Bangladesh
abstract: We present the Bangladesh Environmental Mobility Panel (BEMP), a household panel along Bangladesh’s Jamuna River that traces the impacts of riverbank erosion and flooding on (im)mobility, including short- and long-distance movements, socio-economic outcomes, and political attitudes. The dataset follows 1,691 households with a total of 2,170 panel respondents from 2021–2024 through four annual in-person survey waves and ten phone survey waves at two- to six-month intervals, yielding 24,279 completed surveys with low attrition. Respondent selection via a spatially randomized draw supports inference to households in sampling villages at risk of erosion along the 250 km eastern bank of the Jamuna River. Migrants were tracked, and the plausibly exogenous timing of erosion, conditional on sampling zone and location, provides leverage for research designs linking environmental shocks to mobility. Surveys include measures of socio-demographics, livelihoods, economic outcomes and well-being, conflict and cooperation, and political attitudes, supporting questions in development economics and politics in a rural Global South setting. The design enables gender- and age-sensitive analyses by providing data on household heads (n = 1,691), additional senior female (n = 269) and youth (n = 210) respondents, and left-behind members of migrating-head households (n = 273), complemented by village profiles, focus group discussions, and qualitative interviews with women.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the Brazilian merganser (Mergus octosetaceus), a rare waterfowl species
abstract: The Brazilian merganser ( Mergus octosetaceus ) is a critically endangered bird, with fewer than 250 mature individuals remaining in fragmented populations of the Cerrado biome in Brazil. We generated the first high-quality, chromosome-level genome assembly for M. octosetaceus using PacBio HiFi long reads and Arima Hi-C data from a female specimen. The highly complete assembly is 1.25 Gb in length, scoring 98.9% of BUSCO completeness, and includes both sex chromosomes (Z and W). Annotated repetitive elements comprise 18.94% of the genome, with evidence of recent transposing activity, particularly among LINEs and LTR retrotransposons. We also produced and annotated the complete mitochondrial genome, identifying 37 genes and the control region. This reference genome provides a fundamental resource for M. octosetaceus , enabling insights into genome evolution, chromosomal dynamics within Anatidae, and past population history. It is a remarkable foundation for future research and conservation strategies for managing and restoring populations of this critically endangered species.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: An Environment-Aware GNSS Dataset
abstract: This paper presents a multi-site, environment-aware GNSS dataset that captures comprehensive satellite visibility cycles for local propagation-environment sensing and total electron content (TEC) related ionospheric analysis. The dataset includes observations from 12 fixed monitoring sites and 3 synchronized monitoring sites, covering typical scenarios such as open sky, building blockage, vegetation blockage, and mixed building–vegetation blockage. The records consist of multi-constellation and multi-frequency raw UBX messages, along with processed satellite–time structured observations, including pseudorange, carrier phase, Doppler, carrier-to-noise (C/N 0 ) density ratio, satellite geometry, pseudorange residuals, among other satellite-level observation features. Technical validation demonstrates the reliability and usability of the released observations through quantitative assessments of data completeness, observation continuity, carrier-phase stability, and cross-site alignment consistency. Additional application examples further show its potential for TEC monitoring, propagation-environment sensing, and synchronized GNSS signal blockage detection.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of Oulenziella bakeri (Hughes, 1962) (Acari: Winterschmidtiidae)
abstract: Oulenziella bakeri is a fungivorous mite species native to tropical regions that has been widely utilized as a factitious prey for rearing predatory mites, while also being frequently intercepted during cross-border phytosanitary inspections. To gain deeper insights into this species, in this study, we employed a multi-platform hybrid sequencing strategy combining Illumina, PacBio, ONT, and Hi-C technologies to construct a chromosome-level genome assembly and annotation. The final genome assembly is approximately 55.12 Mb in size. The contig and scaffold N50 lengths are 3.43 Mb and 11.55 Mb, respectively. By using the Hi-C, we anchored 99.91% of the assembled sequences onto five chromosomes. There are 9,773 protein-coding genes in the genome, and the repetitive elements occupy 10.06% of the sequence. Moreover, BUSCO assessment against the arachnida_odb12 database showed high completeness for both assembly (93.1%) and annotation (95.1%). Acquiring this chromosome-level genomic resource with high continuity will greatly advance comparative genomics research in Astigmata.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A high quality chromosomal-scale genome assembly of chafer beetle, Holotrichia serrata (Coleoptera: Scarabaeidae)
abstract: Holotrichia serrata (Coleoptera: Scarabaeidae) is an economically important chafer beetle species commonly referred to as root grub or white grub, responsible for severe root damage in many cultivated crops and forest nurseries across South Asia. Its soil-dwelling larval habit and broad host range make it a persistent challenge for its management. Here, we present a high-quality chromosome-scale genome assembly of H. serrata generated using PacBio HiFi long reads, Illumina short reads, and Arima Hi-C proximity ligation data. The final assembly spans 920 Mb with a GC content of 33.12%, organised into 10 pseudo-chromosomes anchoring 97% of the assembled sequence, with a scaffold N50 of 92.6 Mb. Repetitive elements constitute 68.4% of the genome, predominantly DNA transposons. A total of 18,322 protein-coding genes were predicted, of which 96% were functionally annotated. BUSCO assessment against coleoptera_odb12 indicated 96.1% completeness. Gene family analysis identified 1,330 expanded and 832 contracted gene families. This genome resource can facilitate comparative genomics, functional studies on host adaptation and insecticide resistance, and the development of targeted management strategies for this pest.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Global multi-scale Eulerian and Lagrangian oceanic environmental variables for the period 2000-2009
abstract: Oceans are dynamic environments, with processes occurring over a wide range of spatio-temporal scales. The development of remote sensing and data-assimilative numerical modelling has created a wealth of environmental data to better understand the marine environment. Environmental data are typically released at the scale at which they are observed, but it can be equally important to consider a coarser resolution in space and time, whether to match the resolution of other datasets or to target coarser scale processes. Deriving such coarsened datasets can be very computationally demanding when a large amount of data is involved. Here, we present a ~17TB multi-scale dataset of Eulerian (chlorophyll concentration, light attenuation coefficient, photosynthetically active radiation, particulate organic carbon concentration, euphotic zone depth, sea surface temperature) and Lagrangian (dilation rate, finite-time Lyapunov exponent) variables for the period 2000-2009. Data were first acquired at the finest scale with remote sensing (SeaWiFS, MODIS-AQUA, AVHRR) and numerical modelling (HYCOM, OSCAR), before reprocessing at 20 different spatio-temporal scales (spatial scales of 8 or 9 km, 50 km, 100 km, 500 km; and temporal scales of 1 day, 8 days, 30 days, 365 days, and a climatology averaged over all available data) to facilitate multi-scale analyses of oceanic processes.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Dataset Supporting Context-Based Energy Consumption Modeling in Sofia City
abstract: This dataset provides a harmonised and enriched building-level energy database for Sofia City, supporting context-based modelling and prediction of annual energy consumption. It integrates information from multiple official sources, including Energy Performance Certificate records and cadastral building data, and standardises the attributes into a consistent structure suitable for urban energy analysis. The dataset includes function, construction characteristics, and energy performance indicators for 2,027 buildings. A multi-stage data preparation workflow was applied to clean, validate, and enrich the records, improving their suitability for data-driven modelling. The dataset enables the study of spatial energy patternsand relationships between building characteristics and energy demand at the city scale. It is designed to support research on urban energy modelling, benchmarking, energy policy development, and future scenario analysis. The dataset is publicly available and can be reused or extended for applications such as machine learning, simulation models, and decision support tools for sustainable urban energy planning.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A region-level H&E histopathology image dataset for bone and soft tissue tumors
abstract: Bone and soft tissue (BST) tumors are a heterogeneous and rare group of mesenchymal neoplasms that pose significant diagnostic challenges owing to their complex morphologies and overlapping histological features. Despite rapid advances in digital pathology, most publicly available datasets predominantly focus on common epithelial tumors and offer a limited representation of BST tumors. To address this gap, we introduced the region-level H&E image dataset for bone and soft tissue tumors PAIR-BST , a dataset consisting of 2,252 BST pathologist-annotated regions of interest derived from 470 hematoxylin and eosin-stained whole-slide images obtained from 268 patients diagnosed with BST tumors. Each region was curated and annotated with multi-level labels, including 33 histologic diagnoses, 11 lines of differentiation, and 6 growth patterns, enabling comprehensive characterization of the morphological heterogeneity inherent to BST tumors. Technical validation evaluated pathology foundation models across diagnostic, differentiation, growth-pattern, and image-retrieval tasks. PAIR-BST provides a benchmark for developing and evaluating computational pathology methods for rare mesenchymal tumors.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A cross-sectional psychometric and demographic dataset of adolescents at high-risk for suicide
abstract: This data descriptor presents a dataset containing demographic and psychometric information from 207 adolescents aged 12 to 17. The data were collected as part of a three-group, cross-sectional study design. The sample includes a High-Risk Group (HR-G) (N=43) of adolescents recently admitted for an acute suicidal crisis; a Psychiatric Control Group (PC-G) (N=55) receiving care for non-suicidal conditions; and a General Control Group (GC-G) (N=109) with no known psychiatric history. Data collection includes sociodemographic variables (age, sex, school grade) and item-level responses alongside aggregated scores from seven validated self-report instruments. The assessment includes suicidal ideation, general mental health difficulties, depressive symptoms, bullying, cyberbullying, and problematic internet use. This dataset provides a valuable resource for researchers in psychiatry, psychology, statistics and machine learning to investigate the psychological factors associated with adolescent suicidality and develop predictive models for risk assessment.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: Whole-genome sequencing of Verticillium alfalfae strain Va8
abstract: Verticillium alfalfae is the causal agent of alfalfa Verticillium wilt, a destructive disease that causes significant economic losses. To elucidate the genetic basis of its pathogenicity, we sequenced the genome of V. alfalfae strain Va8 using the PacBio Sequel single-molecule real-time sequencing platform, supplemented with Illumina short-read for error correction. Genome assembly was performed using Hifiasm (version 0.16.1), polished with Racon/Pilon, and filtered, yielding a high-quality, contig-level reference genome. The assembled genome is 33,951,091 base pairs (bp) in size and consists of 57 contigs, with a contig N50 of 3,990,853 bp and a contig N90 of 3,057,321 bp. A total of 2,186,990 bp of repetitive sequences (6.44% of the genome) were identified, and 9,441 protein-coding genes were predicted, of which 9,425 (99.83%) were functionally annotated using multiple public databases. This study enhances our understanding of the genetic basis of V. alfalfae pathogenicity and provides a foundation for future research on disease control and fungal evolution.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: A dataset of records of alien vertebrates in mountains of the World
abstract: Mountains host highly diverse biota that are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic pressures around the globe. Although biological invasions are a well-recognized driver of global change, the available information on the distribution of alien species in mountains remains fragmented. To advance in filling this gap, we present a comprehensive dataset focused on alien vertebrates that contain roughly 320,000 records of over 700 species reported across ~3,000 mountains of the World. The dataset can be downloaded or visualized through interactive maps that facilitate access to species-specific occurrence records, mountain-specific lists of alien vertebrate species and mountain characterizations based on environmental and anthropogenic features. A workflow for the customized compilation of alien species records for specific taxonomic groups or study areas is also available at the RAVeM repository. Ours is a dynamic dataset open to continuous development based on user feedback, that has the potential to facilitate and support future studies and monitoring efforts of alien vertebrates in mountains worldwide.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary

title: gTREND-P-Canada - A 250-m Gridded and Harmonized Phosphorus Mass Budget Dataset Across Canada (1961–2021)
abstract: Phosphorus (P) pollution remains a major challenge for freshwater quality across Canada, yet comprehensive, high-resolution data on its sources and sinks have been limited. The gTREND-P-Canada addresses this gap by providing the first gridded and harmonized phosphorus mass budget dataset at the county-scale, as well at a 250-meter resolution for the entire country, covering the period from 1961 to 2021. This dataset integrates multiple national and global data sources, harmonizing land use, climate, population, livestock, and agricultural management information to estimate annual phosphorus inputs (fertilizer, manure, atmospheric deposition), outputs (crop removal), and net P balances across around 90 million grid cells. The dataset is openly available and will allow for fine-scale analysis of both historical and current P dynamics, offering a valuable tool for researchers, policymakers, and watershed managers to evaluate trends, identify hotspots, and inform sustainable nutrient management strategies. The dataset also supports integration with hydrological and ecological models to assess long-term impacts on water quality under historical and future scenarios.

title: A high-resolution, bias-corrected daily CMIP6 climate projection dataset for Canada with derived extremes-relevant indices
abstract: High-resolution daily climate projections are essential for climate impact assessment and adaptation planning, but raw Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) simulations are too coarse and systematically biased for regional applications. Here, we present QDM-SDM-CMIP6-CAN, a high-resolution, bias-corrected daily climate projection dataset for Canada on a regular 1/12° (~10 km) grid for 2021–2100. The dataset was developed from 23 CMIP6 global climate models (GCMs) under four Tier-1 Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5) using two trend-preserving bias correction (BC) methods, Quantile Delta Mapping (QDM) and Scaled Distribution Mapping (SDM). It provides daily fields of near-surface air temperature ( tas ), maximum temperature ( tasmax ), minimum temperature ( tasmin ), and precipitation ( pr ), together with annual climate indices derived from the bias-corrected daily series, including metrics of hot and cold extremes, heavy precipitation, threshold exceedance, and spell persistence. In addition to individual-model projections, the dataset includes the multi-model ensemble mean of the individually bias-corrected GCMs (ensemble-mean), providing an ensemble summary for applications requiring mean-state information alongside model-specific projections. Technical validation assesses the quality and internal consistency of the released products, including temporal continuity, spatial coherence, consistent behavior of derived climate indices, and substantial model-to-model dispersion among the individually bias-corrected GCMs. This dataset provides a comprehensive national-scale climate projection resource for Canada and is intended to support hydrological, ecological, agricultural, infrastructure, and climate-risk studies requiring high-resolution daily climate information.
keywords: Science, Humanities and Social Sciences, multidisciplinary
